topic_name: Soil physical properties and soil moisture
short_explanation: Soil moisture content is the term for the quantity of water held in a given mass or volume of soil at a particular moment, expressed gravimetrically or volumetrically.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 'Soil moisture quotient' is not a term used in soil physics.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 'Soil moisture ratio' is not the standard name for this quantity.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Soil moisture determination is the act of measuring — oven drying, tensiometer, neutron probe — not the quantity measured.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 'Soil moisture' alone names the water in the soil generally; the stem asks for the amount per unit volume, which is the content.

key_note: The item is loosely drafted: option D is the same idea stated less precisely, and the key relies on 'content/capacity' naming the measured amount. Note that moisture content and water-holding capacity are not the same thing, even though the key pairs them.

short_explanation: 'Investigating' is either pbz or jpa. The second sentence is the only one containing it, and comparing that sentence with the others fixes its other two codes — while and in — leaving jpa and pbz to share 'investigating' and 'terrorism' with no clue to separate them.
explanation_text: Compare sentences pairwise. The first and second share only the word 'while' and only the code prc, so while = prc. The second and third share only 'in' and only ngs, so in = ngs. That accounts for two of the second sentence's four codes; the remaining words, 'investigating' and 'terrorism', carry the remaining codes jpa and pbz. Since 'terrorism' appears nowhere else, nothing distinguishes the two.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: pbz is one of the two candidates, but nothing rules out jpa.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: jpa is the other candidate, and nothing rules out pbz either.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ngs is fixed as 'in' by the overlap between the second and third sentences.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: itg appears only in the third sentence and, once 'in', 'the' and 'challenges' are accounted for, must be 'related'.

common_traps: Two codes that appear in one sentence only can never be separated. Recognising that saves the time spent hunting for a clue that is not there.
key_note: Solved from the three coded sentences shared by Q.15-Q.17. Fixed codes: while = prc, in = ngs, explaining = bfa, related = itg. Undecided: 'the' and 'challenges' are kue and cdw in some order; 'investigating' and 'terrorism' are jpa and pbz in some order.

short_explanation: Net irrigated area is the land irrigated at least once in a year, and it has risen over time, so the passage supports only the conclusion that the area under irrigation has expanded.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The stem states the opposite — net irrigated area has increased.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Irrigation potential per unit area is a different measure and the stem gives no figure for it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 'Irrigation per area of a region' is not a conclusion; it just restates a ratio.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Irrigation efficiency compares water delivered with water used by the crop, which nothing in the stem measures.

key_note: The row is drafted as an inference item without the original paragraph, so the answer rests on the definitional point rather than on quoted data.

short_explanation: While is prc, in is ngs, and related is itg, so the three codes in any order are itg, prc and ngs.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: bfa is 'explaining' and pbz belongs to the investigating-or-terrorism pair; neither word is in the phrase.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: cdw is either 'the' or 'challenges', and pbz is not 'related'.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: All three words are pinned down, so the phrase can be coded.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: prc and itg are right, but kue is 'the' or 'challenges', not 'in' — 'in' is ngs.

common_traps: Codes may be given in any order, so match the set of three codes rather than the sequence of the words.
key_note: Solved from the three coded sentences shared by Q.15-Q.17. Fixed codes: while = prc, in = ngs, explaining = bfa, related = itg. Undecided: 'the' and 'challenges' are kue and cdw in some order; 'investigating' and 'terrorism' are jpa and pbz in some order.

short_explanation: Punjab has the highest proportion of its cropped area irrigated — close to 98 per cent — on the back of canal command from the Sutlej and Beas and very dense tubewell cover.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Haryana is second on this measure, at roughly 90 per cent, but still below Punjab.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Himachal Pradesh is largely rainfed hill farming with a low irrigated share.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Uttarakhand irrigates only the Terai plains well; the hill districts pull the share down.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Kerala has high rainfall and a low irrigated proportion.

common_traps: The question is about the share of cropped area irrigated, not the absolute irrigated area. Uttar Pradesh leads on absolute area; Punjab leads on proportion.

short_explanation: cdw appears in the first and third sentences, which share the words 'the' and 'challenges' — so cdw is one of those two, and since neither is offered, none of the options fits.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 'While' is prc, fixed by the overlap between the first and second sentences.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 'Explaining' appears only in the first sentence and takes bfa, the code left after while, the and challenges are accounted for.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 'Related' appears only in the third sentence and takes itg.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 'In' is ngs, fixed by the overlap between the second and third sentences.

common_traps: The four named options are all words whose codes are already settled as something else. Eliminating them is faster than trying to pin cdw down.
key_note: Solved from the three coded sentences shared by Q.15-Q.17. Fixed codes: while = prc, in = ngs, explaining = bfa, related = itg. Undecided: 'the' and 'challenges' are kue and cdw in some order; 'investigating' and 'terrorism' are jpa and pbz in some order. cdw is 'the' or 'challenges', neither of which is offered, so None of these is the answer.

short_explanation: Post-harvest losses in fruits and vegetables in India are commonly put at 25-35 per cent, the range the paper uses, driven by poor handling, inadequate cold chain and long transit.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 40-55 per cent overstates the loss; no national estimate reaches that band.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 35-60 per cent is wider and higher than any accepted estimate.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 10-20 per cent is closer to the measured CIPHET range for some commodities but below the band the question uses for fruits and vegetables as a group.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 70-85 per cent would mean most of the crop is lost, which no study reports.

key_note: The widely quoted 25-30 per cent figure comes from older estimates. The CIPHET 2015 study, which measured losses commodity by commodity, put fruit and vegetable losses far lower, at roughly 5-16 per cent. Flag if the item is reused with a newer source.

short_explanation: Linking A ≥ B, B ≥ C and C > G gives A > G, so conclusion IV holds; none of the other three can be drawn.
explanation_text: Build the chain: A ≥ B ≥ C > G. A strict sign anywhere in a chain makes the whole relation strict, so A > G — conclusion IV. Conclusion II asks for A > C, but both links from A to C are 'greater than or equal', so A could equal C; only A ≥ C follows. Conclusion III asks for I = A; I equals B and A is at least B, so I could be smaller than A. Conclusion I compares H with C, and H is joined to the chain only by A ≥ H, which leaves H anywhere below A — no relation with C follows.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: H is only known to be at most A. It is never compared with C, so H > C does not follow.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A ≥ B ≥ C gives A ≥ C, not A > C — every link is weak, so equality is possible.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: An either-or option needs two conclusions that are complements of each other, such as A > C and A ≤ C. A > C and I = A are not complements.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: It is true that neither II nor III follows, but the question asks which conclusion holds, and stopping here would miss IV, the one that does.

common_traps: Every sign between A and C is ≥, so A = C is allowed. One weak link is enough to kill a strict conclusion.
key_note: Option D is a true remark about II and III taken alone, but only option E names a conclusion that actually follows from the statements.

short_explanation: Grapes, peach and pear are grouped as semi-perishables — they keep for a few weeks in cold storage, longer than the highly perishable soft fruits but far less than staples.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Banana, tomato and avocado are all climacteric and highly perishable, ripening and softening quickly after harvest.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Guava and watermelon are perishable; watermelon in particular bruises and splits in handling.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Papaya and berries are among the most perishable produce, with a shelf life of a few days.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Pear is semi-perishable but pomegranate is usually placed with it only in some lists; the paper's grouping takes the grapes-peach-pear set as the intended one.

key_note: Shelf-life groupings vary a little between textbooks — grapes are sometimes listed as perishable, and pomegranate stores well — so the item rests on the standard three-fruit grouping the paper used.

short_explanation: Jackfruit maturity is judged largely by aroma, together with a dull hollow sound on tapping and flattening of the spines, whereas mango is judged mainly by shape, shoulder development and specific gravity.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Skin colour is the common index for mango and many other fruits, so it does not distinguish jackfruit.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Jackfruit does not split or open on the tree at maturity.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Leaf changes reflect the tree's condition, not the fruit's maturity.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Size varies widely between jackfruits on the same tree and is an unreliable index.

short_explanation: From F ≤ C ≤ V = Z, F ≤ Z follows; and U = X > Z = V ≥ C gives U > C. Conclusions II and IV fail because X is strictly greater than V and than F.
explanation_text: The chain reads F ≤ C ≤ V = Z < X = U. Conclusion I, F ≤ Z: every link from F to Z is 'less than or equal' or an equality, so F ≤ Z holds. Conclusion III, U > C: U equals X, X is strictly greater than Z, Z equals V and V is at least C, so U > C holds. Conclusion II claims V = X, but V equals Z and Z is strictly less than X, so V < X. Conclusion IV claims X ≤ F, and the chain runs the other way — X is strictly greater than F.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: III is true but II is not: V = Z and Z < X, so V is strictly smaller than X.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: II is the one conclusion that is plainly contradicted by the chain.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: An either-or option needs complementary conclusions. F ≤ Z and X ≤ F are not complements, and in any case F ≤ Z is definitely true while X ≤ F is definitely false.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: II and IV both contradict the chain, so not all four can be true.

common_traps: The single strict sign, Z < X, is what breaks conclusions II and IV. Scan for the one < in a chain of = and ≤ before testing any conclusion.

short_explanation: Companion cropping is the pattern the stem describes — a short-duration crop grown alongside sugarcane and harvested before the cane matures, so neither crop's yield is cut.
explanation_text: Sugarcane takes ten to eighteen months and covers the ground slowly for the first three months, leaving space and light unused. Growing a 60-90 day crop such as potato, onion, mustard or a short pulse in that window uses the gap and gives the grower an income before the cane is cut. The test in the stem is the timing: the companion crop finishes before the main crop reaches maturity, so the two never compete at their peak demand.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Intercropping is the general practice of two crops in the same field in a definite row pattern; it does not require the second crop to be harvested before the first matures.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Nurse cropping uses one crop to shelter another seedling from sun or wind, which is not the purpose here.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: In relay cropping the second crop is sown into the standing first crop near its maturity, so the sowing overlaps rather than the harvest being early.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Alternate cropping means growing different crops in successive seasons on the same field, not together.

key_note: Several texts treat companion cropping as a form of intercropping, so option B is a defensible wider reading; the paper wants the narrower term for the early-harvested partner.

short_explanation: Two pairs qualify in FRUITFUL: the first F with I — three apart in the word and three apart in the alphabet — and R with the final L, six apart in both.
explanation_text: Write the word out and check each pair for the same separation in the word as in the alphabet. The first F is the first letter and I is the fourth, a gap of two letters between them; F and I are also two letters apart in the alphabet, with G and H between. R is the second letter and the last L the eighth, five letters between them; from L to R the alphabet runs M, N, O, P, Q — again five. No other pair matches: U and T sit next to each other in the alphabet but two places apart in the word, and the second F and the second U repeat letters already checked without producing a fit.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: One undercounts — both the F-I pair and the R-L pair qualify.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Four overcounts; no third or fourth pair survives the check.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Three overcounts by one. The near-misses are U with T and I with L, and neither has matching gaps.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: More than four is far beyond what an eight-letter word with repeated letters can produce here.

common_traps: FRUITFUL repeats F and U, so each copy has to be tested separately — the first F pairs with I, the second does not.
key_note: Counted in both directions, forward and backward, which is the standard reading for this question type.

short_explanation: The passage says IMF conditionalities now pertain "not just to balance-of-payments or exchange rate and price policies, but to a large number of structural features of an economy", so what they now reach is the structure of the borrowing economy itself.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Balance-of-payments conditions are the older, narrower ground the sentence sets aside with "not just"; on their own they understate the present reach.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Exchange rate policy belongs to that same older list the passage moves past.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Price policy is also in the older list, and taken alone it misses how wide-ranging and stringent the passage says the conditions have become.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: GDP is never named as a conditionality anywhere in the passage.

common_traps: A, B and C all appear in the passage, but inside the clause that "not just" sets aside. A hurried reader picks the first familiar phrase.

short_explanation: The rice-wheat system is India's largest cropping system, covering roughly 10 million hectares across the Indo-Gangetic plains of Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
explanation_text: Rice in the kharif followed by wheat in the rabi became dominant after the Green Revolution, once assured irrigation, dwarf high-yielding varieties and assured procurement at MSP made both halves profitable on the same land. It carries most of the country's procured grain, and most of its resource problems too — falling water tables in Punjab and Haryana, declining soil organic carbon, and paddy residue burning in the short window between the two crops.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Rice-maize is a growing system in the peninsular states but covers far less area.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Rice-sugarcane is limited to pockets with heavy irrigation and mill access.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Rice monocropping occurs in high-rainfall eastern and coastal tracts but is smaller than the rice-wheat belt.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Wheat monocropping is uncommon; wheat is nearly always part of a rotation.

short_explanation: Until the mid-1970s the World Bank "lent money primarily to finance development projects", and the conditions it imposed "related to performance with respect to specific projects" - the financing and the project-linked conditions together.
explanation_text: This is a best-answer item rather than a true-or-false one. Financing development projects is a true statement about the early Bank, but the passage gives the initial role in two halves: the money went to specific projects, and whatever conditions the borrower carried were tied to performance on those same projects. That pairing is exactly what later changes - non-project financing in the 1970s, then SALs and SECALs in the early 1980s, which bring conditions on trade policy, public finance, public sector ownership and agricultural and industrial policy. Choosing the fuller statement is the point of the question.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Non-project financing began only in the 1970s; before that it is the very thing the Bank was not doing.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Dictating terms across a borrower's economy came with the structural adjustment loans of the early 1980s, not with the early project lending.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: True as far as it goes, but it drops the second half of what the passage describes - conditions tied to performance on the specific projects.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The passage speaks of financing development projects, not of helping countries finish infrastructure already due; that idea is not in the text.

common_traps: Option C is a correct sentence and is simply less complete. On detail-retrieval items, check whether the passage gives one element or two before settling on the shorter option.

short_explanation: After rice-wheat, the maize-based cropping systems occupy the largest cereal area, with maize grown in both kharif and rabi across Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Telangana.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Tur (pigeonpea) is a pulse, so a tur-based system does not answer a question about cereal systems.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Mustard is an oilseed, not a cereal.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Sugarcane is a long-duration commercial crop, again not a cereal.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Barley occupies a small and shrinking area, mainly in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

common_traps: The stem asks for a cereal system. Three of the options are built on a pulse, an oilseed and a commercial crop, and can be dropped before comparing areas.

short_explanation: The passage sets out three grounds of criticism in order - the programs undermine the sovereignty of borrowing nations, they fail to stimulate social production and economic growth, and they impose a severe burden on the poor - so all three statements belong to the critics.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Sovereignty is one of the three grounds, not the only one.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Leaves out the burden on the poor, which the passage names third and returns to in its closing sentence.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Leaves out the loss of sovereignty, which the passage names first.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Leaves out the failure to stimulate social production and economic growth, named as the second ground.

short_explanation: The paper keys broiler marketing at 3-4 weeks of age; broilers are meat birds grown to market weight as fast as feed conversion allows, then sold and the shed restocked.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 5-8 weeks spans the modern marketing window but the paper's key is the shorter band.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 6-8 weeks is the older textbook range from before feed and genetics improved.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A single figure of 8 weeks is the upper end of the older range, not a marketing window.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 1-3.5 weeks is below any marketable weight; a chick of that age is still in the brooder.

key_note: Standard poultry texts put broiler marketing at about 6 weeks, and older ones at 6-8 weeks, so options A and C are the defensible readings on subject knowledge. The source key reads (b), 3-4 weeks, which no standard reference supports. Verify against the official key before publication.

topic_name: Vocabulary from context within a passage
short_explanation: The passage explains cross conditionality with its own example: the World Bank "may not agree to an SAL unless the borrower country has accepted the terms of a stand-by agreement with the IMF" - one lender's terms stacked on the other's.
explanation_text: The crossing runs between the two Bretton Woods institutions, not between a lender and a borrower. Once both were lending for stabilisation and structural adjustment, a borrower could not satisfy one and ignore the other, because the Bank's loan waited on the Fund's agreement. The passage adds the role-reversal that follows - the Fund able to set conditions on particular sectors, the Bank on macro-management - which is why it says the two sets of conditionalities are no longer easy to tell apart.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pairs a borrower with one institution; the crossing described is between the Bank and the Fund.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Developed against developing countries is not the relation the term names.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Another country-and-lender pairing, and "most countries" is not the passage's frame.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Same fault: the IMF and the developing countries are lender and borrower, not the two crossing sets of conditions.

topic_name: Multilateral development banks and the IMF
short_explanation: The IMF came into existence in December 1945, when the first 29 countries signed the Articles of Agreement drafted at the Bretton Woods conference of July 1944; it began financial operations only in March 1947.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 1942 predates the Bretton Woods conference, which met only in July 1944.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 1947 is when the Fund began financial operations, not when it was established.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 1941 predates Bretton Woods; wartime planning had not yet produced a draft agreement.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 1943 is still a planning year - the Keynes and White plans were being argued over and no institution existed.

common_traps: 1947 is the year the IMF started operations; the stem asks when it was established.

short_explanation: A WTO ruling asks a member to bring its measure into conformity and can authorise retaliation if it does not, but the WTO cannot strike down or overrule a national law - so that is the statement which is not true.
explanation_text: A panel or the Appellate Body finds a measure inconsistent with a covered agreement. How the member complies - amend the law, withdraw the measure, offer compensation, or simply accept retaliation - stays with the member and its own legislature. That is why the WTO is called member-driven: it has no supranational power over national law-making.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: True, so not the answer: the WTO is an independent international organisation, not a UN specialised agency, unlike the IMF and the World Bank.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: True: India was a GATT contracting party and joined the WTO at its creation on 1 January 1995, making it a founding member.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: True: the WTO works on one member one vote, in practice by consensus, unlike the weighted voting of the IMF and World Bank.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: True: the Ministerial Conference, meeting at least once every two years, is the WTO's highest decision-making body.

common_traps: The stem asks which statement is NOT true, so four of the five options are correct statements.

short_explanation: The passage names the typical elements in two parts - "first, fiscal austerity, monetary contraction and devaluation, and second, a set of policies at the sectoral and micro level" - so both together are the main constituents.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The first element only; the passage explicitly adds a second.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The second element only.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Norms for spending the money lent is not how the passage describes either element; the conditions bear on policies and institutions, not on the use of the loan.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: "All of the above" would pull in the spending-norms statement, which the passage does not make.

common_traps: "All of the above" looks safe once two options are already true, but it holds only if every listed statement holds. Here the third does not.

short_explanation: Demographic transition is the shift a population makes from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as incomes, health care and education improve.
explanation_text: The transition runs in stages. Deaths fall first, on better nutrition, sanitation and medicine, while births stay high - that gap is the phase of fastest population growth. Births then fall as child survival improves and families choose smaller size, and the population settles again at low fertility and low mortality. India is in the later part of this transition, which is exactly what has opened its demographic dividend.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The demographic dividend is the growth bonus from a large working-age share; it is a consequence of the transition, not the transition itself.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Demographic curves is not a defined concept in population studies.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Demographic reversal describes populations ageing and shrinking after the transition, not the move from high rates to low.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Demographic quotient is not a standard demographic term.

common_traps: Transition and dividend are neighbours: the transition is the process, the dividend is the window it opens.

short_explanation: "Helps in" takes a gerund, so the oven helps in retaining the vitamins, and "makes cooking faster" is the ordinary make + object + adjective pattern.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: "Provides cooking faster" is not English; provide needs a noun object, not an adjective complement.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: An oven does not determine the vitamins in food, and "accelerates cooking faster" states the speed twice.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Estimating the vitamins is measuring them, not keeping them, and "enhances cooking faster" repeats the same redundancy.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Controlling the vitamins says the wrong thing about what the oven does to them.

short_explanation: Targeting cancer stem cells would improve the efficacy - the effectiveness - of the chemotherapeutic regimens, the fixed courses of treatment already in use.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Potency could fill the first blank, but "chemotherapeutic sustenance" is not a thing; sustenance is nourishment.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Emasculation is a weakening, the opposite of an improvement, and nutriments are nutrients rather than treatments.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Germaneness means relevance, which is not what molecular targeting improves in a drug already in use.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Sufficiency and subsistence belong to the language of bare adequacy and of living, not of treatment effectiveness.

short_explanation: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act was passed in 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010.
explanation_text: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002, made free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 a fundamental right, but a right needs a law to work. The RTE Act supplied it: a neighbourhood school, no capitation fee, no screening at admission, 25 per cent of entry-class seats in private unaided schools for disadvantaged children, and no detention up to Class VIII, which the 2019 amendment later relaxed.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 1 April 2012 is around when the Supreme Court upheld the Act's private-school admission requirement, not when the Act commenced.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2 May 2013 has no connection with the Act's commencement.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 1 April 2011 is a year late; commencement was on that date in 2010.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 1 April 2015 is well after commencement.

topic_name: Kisan Credit Card and agricultural credit targets
short_explanation: Statement 2 is the odd one: collateral-free crop loans under the Kisan Credit Card run up to Rs 1.6 lakh, not Rs 2 lakh, the limit having been raised from Rs 1 lakh in 2019.
explanation_text: The KCC, introduced in 1998, gives a farmer a single revolving credit limit for crop expenses, post-harvest costs, consumption needs and farm asset maintenance. The working rules candidates are asked for are the short-term crop loan limit of Rs 3 lakh at 7 per cent with interest subvention, a further 3 per cent prompt repayment incentive taking the effective rate to 4 per cent, no collateral up to Rs 1.6 lakh, and repayment tied to the harvest and marketing cycle of the crop financed.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 1 is a genuine feature — the short-term crop loan limit with subvention is Rs 3 lakh — so it cannot be part of the answer.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: This adds statement 3; the paper treats the credit-and-repayment statement as a feature, leaving statement 2 alone as the exception.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 3 alone leaves out the collateral figure, which is the one that departs from the circular.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Statements 1 and 3 both describe the card correctly, so all three cannot be non-features.

common_traps: The collateral-free ceiling is Rs 1.6 lakh, a figure candidates often round to Rs 2 lakh or leave at the older Rs 1 lakh.
key_note: Statement 3 is also shaky: a KCC is sanctioned for five years with annual review, not three, so 'B: 2 and 3 only' is a defensible competing reading. Check against the official key.

short_explanation: The contrast turned by "although" is between the cells mattering to chemotherapy and their still ranking only as secondary targets for therapy.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: "Affiliated to chemotherapy" is not how the relation is expressed, and fatuous means silly.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Analogous means similar in form, and cells are not similar to a treatment; insignificant also kills the contrast the sentence needs.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Pertinent works in the first blank, but inane means empty-headed and cannot describe objectives for therapy.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Feigned means pretended, which cannot apply to the cells' relation to chemotherapy.

key_note: The sentence is loosely drafted - in the source literature cancer stem cells are described as resistant to chemotherapy and therefore a priority target. The pair has to be settled on the second blank, where only "secondary" collocates normally with "objectives".

short_explanation: The Rangarajan Committee was set up in 2012 after the outcry over a rural poverty line of about Rs 22 a day, and built its line on a normative nutrition standard plus behaviourally observed non-food spending.
explanation_text: Rangarajan split the line in two. For food he fixed a normative requirement - calories along with protein and fat. For non-food such as rent, clothing, schooling and conveyance he used what households near that food level actually spend. The result was higher than Tendulkar's: about Rs 972 a month rural and Rs 1,407 urban for 2011-12, putting 29.5 per cent of Indians below the line against Tendulkar's 21.9 per cent. The government never formally adopted the report.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Alagh Committee of 1979 fixed the original calorie norms - 2,400 rural and 2,100 urban - decades before this controversy.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Lakdawala Committee of 1993 kept those calorie norms and updated them with price indices; it is not the post-2012 committee.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Tendulkar Committee of 2009 produced the very line whose Rs 22 a day rural figure caused the outrage this committee was set up to answer.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: There is no Bansal Committee on poverty estimation.

common_traps: Tendulkar is the committee being reacted against; Rangarajan is the one set up in response.

short_explanation: "There can be no denial that..." is the fixed pattern, and blind beliefs are things to be erased.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: "No cause that" does not work; cause takes "for" or an infinitive, not a that-clause of this kind.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: "No reason that" has the same fault, and undermining a belief weakens it rather than doing away with it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: "No dispute that" is possible, but beliefs are not deliberately forgotten; the sentence calls for removal.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: "No doubt that" fits the first blank well, but restored brings blind beliefs back instead of ending them.

common_traps: Option E's first word is the best single fit in the set. A double-blank item is decided by the weaker blank, and "restored" reverses the sentence.

short_explanation: Evil is said to live off the good, so what it needs is the good's acquiescence - the passive going-along that is given by not objecting.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Ratification is a formal act of approval, far more deliberate than the quiet consent the passage has in mind.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Corroboration is confirming evidence for a claim, which does not fit the moral relation described.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Patronage is active support and funding; the passage's point is that evil needs only that the good not resist.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Condescension is a manner of talking down, not a form of consent.

topic_name: Production economics and factors of production
short_explanation: Statement 3 is the incorrect one: in the short run at least one input is fixed by definition — that is what makes it the short run — so not all inputs are variable.
explanation_text: The production function relates output to inputs. The short-run function varies one input, usually labour, while land, capital and management stay fixed, which is what produces the familiar curve with increasing, then diminishing, then negative marginal returns. The long run is the period in which every input can be varied, including plant size, so the distinction between the two is precisely which inputs are fixed. Statements 1 and 2 describe the short-run curve correctly: output is plotted against a single variable input, and that input, labour, is the independent variable.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 1 correctly describes the short-run function as output against one variable input.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 2 is correct — labour is the independent variable plotted on the horizontal axis.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: This includes statement 2, which is correct.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Only statement 3 is wrong; statements 1 and 2 both describe the curve accurately.

common_traps: The stem asks which statements are INCORRECT. Reading it as 'correct' inverts the whole answer.

topic_name: Street vendor credit and livelihood schemes
short_explanation: PM SVANidhi lends a street vendor working capital of up to Rs 10,000 repayable in monthly instalments over one year, not in four quarterly instalments, so that is the statement which is not true.
explanation_text: The design is a ladder: Rs 10,000 for a year, then Rs 20,000 on timely repayment, then Rs 50,000. The vendor gets a 7 per cent interest subsidy credited quarterly and cashback for digital transactions. Repayment is monthly precisely because a vendor's earnings are small and daily; quarterly lumps would defeat the purpose.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: True: it is a Central Sector Scheme funded entirely by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: True: the scheme was extended to December 2024 with a target of about 42 lakh street vendors.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: True: vendors vending in urban areas, including those from surrounding peri-urban and rural areas, are covered.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: True: a State or UT must have notified rules and a scheme under the Street Vendors Act, 2014 for its vendors to come under PM SVANidhi.

common_traps: The stem asks which statement is NOT true about the scheme.

short_explanation: The clause explains itself - "by feeding off the rational" - and the adverb for living off another is parasitically.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Triumphantly describes victory on its own strength, the opposite of surviving off something else.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Haplessly means unluckily and says nothing about the mechanism the clause goes on to name.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Dispassionately is about absence of emotion and has no bearing on how the irrational survives.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Jinxed is an adjective and cannot stand in an adverb slot.

short_explanation: The National Action Plan on Climate Change, released in 2008, is the umbrella framework, and it is delivered through eight National Missions - solar, enhanced energy efficiency, sustainable habitat, water, sustaining the Himalayan ecosystem, green India, sustainable agriculture, and strategic knowledge for climate change.
explanation_text: Keep the four climate words apart. The UNFCCC is the 1992 treaty; the COP is its annual meeting of parties; the NAFCC is a fund that pays for state adaptation projects, with NABARD as National Implementing Entity; the NAPCC is India's own policy framework. Only the NAPCC is organised as eight named missions, so the count of eight in the stem settles the row by itself.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change is a financing window for state adaptation projects, not a framework holding eight sub-schemes.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Climate Action Plan is a generic description, not the name of India's framework.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The COP is the Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC - a meeting, not a scheme framework.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The UNFCCC is the international convention; India's eight missions sit under its own national plan.

common_traps: NAPCC and NAFCC differ by one letter: the plan holds the eight missions, the fund pays for adaptation projects.
key_note: This row's stem points at 'the above' framework and the passage behind it is not carried in this chunk. It sits with the other 2020 climate rows here - question 45 refers to the same missing climate passage - and the give-away is inside the stem itself: only the National Action Plan on Climate Change is built as eight sub-schemes, its eight National Missions. So the row was solved from the set context plus that count, without the passage.
tag_note: Both subject_slug and topic_name are null on this row. It belongs to economic-social-issues, with a topic along the lines of 'Climate change framework and the National Action Plan on Climate Change' - the same set as question 45.

short_explanation: Covering itself with a false show of rationality is deception, so the idea gains influence fraudulently - the intellectual counterpart of the parasitic survival named just before.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Fallaciously points to faulty reasoning; what the sentence describes is a disguise deliberately put on, which is fraud rather than bad logic.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Forebodingly means in a way that suggests coming trouble.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Errantly means straying or wandering, not deceiving.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Illusory is an adjective and will not fill an adverb slot.

common_traps: "Fallaciously" is close enough in flavour to tempt, but the sentence names an act of covering up, not an error in reasoning.

short_explanation: A veneer is a thin surface layer, exactly the thin show of rationality the irrational idea lays over itself.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: An edifice is a whole built structure, too solid for something described as a covering.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A modicum is a small quantity, and a modicum of rationality would grant the idea some real rationality.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: "A protection of rationality" is not idiomatic, and the sentence is about appearance rather than defence.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Succour is help given in distress, which does not fit "covering itself with".

common_traps: "Edifice" sounds impressive and takes "of" comfortably, but it names a substantial structure and so reverses the point: the covering is thin and false.

short_explanation: Eklavya Model Residential Schools are run by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for Scheduled Tribe children, giving free residential schooling from Class VI to XII in tribal-majority blocks.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Scheduled Caste students are served by separate hostels and scholarship schemes; EMRS is a Ministry of Tribal Affairs programme.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Other Backward Classes are not the target group of EMRS.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Minority students are covered by Ministry of Minority Affairs schemes.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups are a subset of Scheduled Tribes and are certainly covered, but the schools are for ST children generally, so this option is narrower than the answer.

common_traps: PVTGs is the tempting narrower option; EMRS covers Scheduled Tribes as a whole.

short_explanation: "Defend ourselves against" is the fixed combination, and justice is being called the weapon for it.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Obscure means to hide from view; one does not obscure oneself against something.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Strive does not take an object like "ourselves".

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Conceal has the same fault as obscure, and hiding is the opposite of meeting evil with justice.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Penalize turns the punishment on ourselves rather than on the evil.

short_explanation: India's external debt stood at about USD 558.5 billion at end-March 2020, a rise of roughly 2.8 per cent over the year, driven mainly by external commercial borrowings and NRI deposits.
explanation_text: External debt is a stock measured on a date and reported by the RBI every quarter. Its health is read through ratios rather than the absolute number: external debt to GDP was about 20.6 per cent at end-March 2020, short-term debt was comfortably covered by foreign exchange reserves, and most of the debt was long-term. A large absolute figure is therefore not by itself a warning sign.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: USD 710.4 billion is far above India's external debt stock in 2020.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: USD 443.8 billion is below even the end-March 2016 level.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: USD 666.7 billion overstates the end-March 2020 stock.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: USD 521.6 billion is closer to the end-March 2018 figure than to 2020.

key_note: The stem says 'central government's external debt', but USD 558.5 billion is India's total external debt on RBI data for end-March 2020; sovereign external debt was around USD 100 billion. The keyed figure is the country total, so the stem is loosely worded rather than the key being wrong.

short_explanation: Justice here is naming evil as evil and leaving no room for a second reading, which is what unequivocal says.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Categorical describes a statement made without conditions or exceptions; the sentence is about admitting no ambiguity in the naming, which is what unequivocal picks out. It is the closest of the five.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Blatant means offensively obvious and carries disapproval, which cannot attach to the act of justice being praised.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Covert reverses the paragraph, which is about refusing to hide the judgement.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Irresolute means wavering, the opposite of what the identification must be.

common_traps: Two of the five, categorical and unequivocal, both fit the slot; the paragraph's insistence on refusing any moral respectability decides it.
key_note: "Categorical" in option A is a genuine near-synonym and would read naturally. The keyed "unequivocal" is defensible because the surrounding sentences insist on withholding even a crumb of moral sanction, so the stress falls on leaving no ambiguity.

topic_name: Pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers
short_explanation: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan is open to unorganised-sector workers aged 18 to 40 with monthly income up to Rs 15,000, and pays Rs 3,000 a month as pension after 60.
explanation_text: The contribution is matched rupee for rupee: the worker pays a monthly amount fixed by entry age - Rs 55 at 18, rising to Rs 200 at 40 - and the Centre pays the same. The upper age of 40 exists so that every entrant contributes for at least twenty years before the pension begins at 60. PM-KMY for farmers and the traders' pension scheme use the same 18 to 40 design.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 16-45 is not the band; entry begins at 18 and closes at 40.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 18-50 would leave only ten years of contribution before the pension age of 60.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 20-55 matches no unorganised-sector pension scheme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Stripped of the sanction it borrows from the good, evil is left with no power of its own - impotent names that standing condition.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Indisposed means slightly unwell or unwilling, far too mild.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Crippled implies an injury inflicted on it, whereas the method described is withholding support rather than maiming.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Incapacitated carries the same sense of damage done, and it is a heavier clinical word than the sentence wants.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Herculean means enormously strong, the opposite of the result described.

key_note: Crippled and incapacitated both mean rendered powerless and are the near-misses. Impotent is defensible because it names a lasting powerlessness that follows from being left unaided, not an injury done to evil.

short_explanation: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana pays Rs 5,000 to a pregnant and lactating woman for her first living child, as partial compensation for wage loss and for better nutrition.
explanation_text: The Rs 5,000 came in instalments tied to behaviour: early registration of pregnancy, at least one antenatal check-up, and registration of the birth with the first cycle of immunisation. A beneficiary who also receives the Janani Suraksha Yojana incentive for institutional delivery typically reaches about Rs 6,000 in all, which is why Rs 6,000 is so often quoted; the PMMVY entitlement itself is Rs 5,000.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 2,000 is neither an instalment nor the total under the scheme.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 4,500 is not the entitlement.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 3,000 is the sum of the first two instalments under the earlier three-instalment structure, not the whole benefit.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 3,800 is not a scheme figure.

common_traps: Rs 6,000 is the figure most candidates remember, but that includes the Janani Suraksha Yojana payment.

short_explanation: Monitoring at village level under MGNREGA rests with the Gram Sabha, which the Act requires to conduct a social audit of all works taken up in its area at least twice a year.
explanation_text: Keep the two village bodies apart. The Gram Panchayat is the executive: it receives job applications, issues job cards and executes at least half the works by value. The Gram Sabha is the assembly of all adult voters in the village: it recommends the works to be taken up and then audits them. Placing the audit with the assembly rather than the executive is what makes the check meaningful.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Gram Panchayat implements the works; it cannot be the body auditing its own execution.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Panchayat Samiti is the block tier, above the village.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The Zilla Parishad is the district tier and oversees the programme at district level.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Municipalities are urban bodies; MGNREGA is a rural employment guarantee.

common_traps: Gram Panchayat and Gram Sabha are the classic swap: implementation with the panchayat, social audit with the sabha.

short_explanation: The original's fault is "concerned of"; the fixed combination is "concerned about" or "concerned over", and "aware" must keep its own "of" before the shared object.
explanation_text: Two rules decide this item. First, when two adjectives share one object but take different prepositions, both prepositions have to appear: "aware of and concerned over environmental issues". Drop the first and the sentence reads "aware ... environmental issues", which is not English. Second, "little doubt" and "a little doubt" are not the same phrase. Without the article the word is negative and means hardly any doubt, which is what this sentence intends; with the article it means that some doubt does exist.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: "Raise" is wrong for an increase in a number - a raise is an increase in pay - and rise is needed.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: "A little doubt" says some doubt exists, reversing the sentence's claim that the rise is beyond question.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: "Aware and concerned about" leaves aware without its "of".

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: It drops the "of" after aware and keeps the original's wrong "concerned of".

common_traps: "Little doubt" against "a little doubt" turns on a single article and flips the meaning.

short_explanation: Gupta rejects the Johl protection for one house and five acres on the ground that it "may result in denial of credit by moneylenders to small farmers", which only makes sense if the moneylender lends against attachable security.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The reason given is about small farmers losing credit, not about any preference for large ones.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The passage says the moneylender "could even be said to prefer default to repayment", so a particular concern with repayment does not follow.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Moneylenders lend to agriculturists heavily; the passage's complaint is the terms, not any reluctance to lend.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The passage calls the relationship "utterly exploitative".

topic_name: DAY-NRLM, self-help groups and rural livelihoods
short_explanation: Every marker in the passage - the November 2015 renaming, the 7 crore rural poor households, the Self Help Groups and their federations, the 8 to 10 year horizon - describes the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission, not MGNREGA.
explanation_text: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of unskilled manual wage work on demand to every rural household that asks for it. DAY-NRLM builds Self Help Groups, village organisations and cluster federations of poor women and links them to bank credit and livelihoods. One is a demand-driven wage safety net created by an Act of 2005; the other is an institution-building and credit mission whose earlier name, Aajeevika, was changed in November 2015. Both sit under the Ministry of Rural Development, which is why papers confuse them.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: This is the scheme the passage actually describes - Aajeevika, renamed DAY-NRLM in November 2015. The paper marks it wrong; see the key note.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: DDU-GKY is the placement-linked skilling programme for rural youth and is a component under NRLM, not the mission described here.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission develops rural clusters with urban amenities; it has no SHG mobilisation target.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: SVAMITVA surveys inhabited village land and issues property cards; it is a 2020 land-records programme, not a livelihoods mission.

key_note: The key marks MGNREGA, but MGNREGA is a 2005 wage employment guarantee: it was not renamed in November 2015, it does not work through Self Help Groups, and it has no 7 crore household mobilisation target over 8 to 10 years. Every detail in the passage belongs to Aajeevika, renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - NRLM in November 2015. Proposed answer: option A, DAY-NRLM.

short_explanation: Interlocking means a party's standing in one market is what lets him deal in another - the lender is also the trader who takes the harvest. Requiring an insurable interest works the same way: the insurance contract is open only to someone who already has a stake in the life insured.
explanation_text: The passage describes the moneylender-trader buying the harvest at throw-away prices, so credit and produce are not two separate deals but one linked arrangement, and it is the lender's position in the produce market that makes the loan cheap to administer and safe to make. The parallel the question asks for is structural - a transaction in the second market being open only to someone with a pre-existing interest in the first - rather than a parallel of exploitation.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A lawyer's hold over documents is security taken inside a single service relationship, over the client's own papers; there is no second market in which the lawyer also deals.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A guarantee is an ordinary term of one sale, offered because the seller expects no failure.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Overvaluing goods to recover the premium is a misstatement of value within an insurance claim, not two markets locked together.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Raising the price of one good when another's price moves is a price response inside the same market.

key_note: Option B is the reading many candidates take, since a lien also uses a hold over an asset to force payment. The key holds if "interlocked" is read as a dealing in one market being open only to someone with a stake in the other, which is what insurable interest requires. The item is loosely framed.
