option_rationales.rationale: The sunk cost trap is staying with a course to justify money or effort already spent and not recoverable. The pull comes from the past investment, not from the comfort of things as they are.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The prudence trap is over-caution in estimates, padding figures to be safe, which distorts the numbers a decision rests on.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The anchoring trap is giving too much weight to the first figure or fact encountered, so that every later estimate is dragged towards it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Loss aversion describes losses weighing heavier than equivalent gains. It helps explain why inertia appeals, but the named trap for keeping things as they are is the status quo trap.

common_traps: The sunk cost trap is the closest neighbour. Ask what is holding the decision in place: past spending points to sunk cost, comfort with the present arrangement points to status quo.

short_explanation: The directive style is the fast, low-information style: the leader decides from knowledge and past experience already held, without gathering views from anyone else.
explanation_text: In the common four-style grid, directive and analytical are both task-oriented, but the analytical leader wants more information and more alternatives before committing while the directive leader is content to act on little. The conceptual and behavioural styles sit on the people-oriented side, the conceptual leader taking a long view and canvassing widely. The trade is what matters in practice: the directive style buys speed at the cost of the correction that other people's information would supply, so it fits routine or urgent matters within the leader's own competence and authority, and fits badly where the decision is novel, irreversible or properly someone else's to take.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The delegating style passes the decision itself to someone else, so the leader is not the one reaching it.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The facilitative style has the leader and the group work towards a shared decision, so information is gathered from others by design.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The conceptual style takes a broad, long-range view and canvasses many people and possibilities before deciding.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The analytical style deliberately gathers more information and weighs more alternatives before committing, which is the opposite of deciding without seeking input.

topic_name: School education schemes and curriculum frameworks
short_explanation: Samagra Shiksha was launched in 2018 as a single scheme for school education from pre-school to Class 12.
explanation_text: Samagra Shiksha merged three earlier schemes — Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan for elementary education, the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan for secondary, and the centrally sponsored teacher education scheme. The point of the merger was to treat school education as one continuum instead of funding three stages through separate windows, with a single outcome-linked allocation to states. It is the vehicle through which later initiatives such as NIPUN Bharat are delivered.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2005 is not the launch year; Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, one of the merged schemes, began in 2001.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2008 is not the launch year; the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, another merged scheme, came in 2009.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2010 is when the Right to Education Act came into force, not when Samagra Shiksha began.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2014 is not the launch year of this scheme.

common_traps: 2010 belongs to the Right to Education Act coming into force; the merged school-education scheme is 2018.

short_explanation: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, launched in 2015, was framed first of all to stop gender-biased sex selection and lift the declining child sex ratio, with girls' survival, protection and education following from that.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Reducing gender disparity describes the scheme's wider purpose but not the specific objective written into it; the measurable target is the child sex ratio.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Female wages are a labour-market question; the scheme does not work on earnings.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Training women as teachers is not part of the scheme's design.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Reducing patriarchy is too diffuse to be a scheme objective and is not how the guidelines state the aim.

key_note: Option A is a fair description of what the scheme is ultimately for, so a candidate choosing it is not being unreasonable. The key takes the scheme's stated first objective — improving the child sex ratio — which is the specific measurable target in the guidelines.

short_explanation: The Financial Stability Report is published by the Reserve Bank of India, twice a year, and reflects the collective assessment of the sub-committee of the Financial Stability and Development Council on risks to financial stability.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The National Statistical Office produces national accounts and the price and employment statistics, not financial-sector risk assessments.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Finance Ministry chairs the FSDC and publishes the Economic Survey, but the FSR itself comes from the RBI.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: SBI is a commercial bank; its research notes are not the FSR.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The International Financial Services Centres Authority regulates the GIFT City IFSC; it does not publish the FSR.

common_traps: The FSDC is chaired by the Finance Minister, which pulls answers towards the Finance Ministry; the report is still an RBI publication.

short_explanation: The EASE Reforms Index scores public sector banks on a large set of objective parameters — more than 140 under EASE 4.0 — so that their reform progress can be measured and ranked rather than asserted.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Basel capital norms are prudential requirements supervised by the RBI; the index does not exist to check Basel compliance.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Financial inclusion is one theme measured inside the index, not the reason the index was created.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Post-pandemic growth is a policy objective, not what an index of bank performance measures.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The other three options are not what the index does, so they cannot all be right.

key_note: The parameter count is restated with each EASE edition — earlier editions used a smaller set. Verify the '140 plus' figure against the EASE 4.0 report before publication.

short_explanation: An Infrastructure Investment Trust is set up as a trust, registered with SEBI, in which a trustee holds the assets for unit holders while an investment manager runs them and a sponsor brings them in.
explanation_text: The trust form is what makes the pass-through work. Because the vehicle is a trust rather than a company, cash flows from the underlying road, transmission or pipeline assets can be distributed to unit holders without being taxed twice, and SEBI's regulations require at least 90% of net distributable cash flows to be paid out. The four parties are fixed by regulation: sponsor, trustee, investment manager and project manager, with the trustee independent of the sponsor. REITs are built on the same template for rent-yielding real estate.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A private limited company would not give the pass-through treatment or the mandatory distribution structure the SEBI InvIT Regulations require.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Co-operatives are member-owned bodies under co-operative law and are not used for capital-market vehicles of this kind.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: An NBFC is an RBI-registered lender; an InvIT owns and distributes income from infrastructure assets instead.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The regulator here is SEBI; the InvIT is the vehicle being regulated, not a regulator.

short_explanation: UNDP India's 'Sahi Disha' campaign marked the work of Project Disha, which created livelihood and entrepreneurship opportunities for women in rural India.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The seventy-fifth year of independence was marked by Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav, a government programme, not by a UNDP campaign.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The campaign was not a youth-guidance programme for Jammu and Kashmir.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Rural prosperity in general is too broad; the campaign was specifically about women's livelihoods and enterprise.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Rural poverty alleviation is the wider field the project sits in, but the campaign's subject was women's livelihood and entrepreneurship.

key_note: The campaign name and its link to Project Disha should be checked against a UNDP India source before publication; options D and E are close enough in theme that the distinction rests on the campaign's own wording.

topic_name: Irrigation, water resources and river linking
short_explanation: Ken-Betwa is the first river interlinking project taken up under the National Perspective Plan, moving surplus water from the Ken in Madhya Pradesh to the water-short Betwa basin, largely for Bundelkhand.
explanation_text: The National Perspective Plan of 1980 identified 30 links — 16 peninsular and 14 Himalayan — with the National Water Development Agency preparing the feasibility reports. Ken-Betwa is the first to move to implementation: a dam at Daudhan on the Ken inside Panna Tiger Reserve, a link canal to the Betwa, irrigation for around 10 lakh hectares, drinking water for about 62 lakh people and hydropower. The project is contested precisely because the submergence falls inside a tiger reserve, which is why the environmental clearances took as long as the engineering.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Krishna-Godavari transfer is a state-level scheme in Andhra Pradesh, not the first link taken up under the national interlinking plan.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Jhelum-Sutlej is not a link in the National Perspective Plan.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Ganga-Yamuna is not one of the identified interlinking projects; the two rivers already join at Prayagraj.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Subarnarekha-Mahanadi does not feature as the first project taken up.

topic_name: School education schemes and curriculum frameworks
short_explanation: NIPUN Bharat — the National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy, launched by the Ministry of Education in 2021 under Samagra Shiksha — sets out to give every child foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of Class 3, covering the learning needs of children aged 3 to 9.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Creating a skilled rural workforce is the remit of skilling missions such as DDU-GKY, not of a foundational-learning initiative.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Guiding rural youth towards entrepreneurship is a livelihoods objective, not what NIPUN Bharat does.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: This is in fact NIPUN Bharat's stated aim — see the key note; it is the option marked wrong in the source key.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A correct description of the mission is present among the options.

key_note: The keyed option, on creating efficient administrators, has nothing to do with NIPUN Bharat on any reading. NIPUN Bharat is a foundational literacy and numeracy mission under Samagra Shiksha, with a target of universal foundational learning by 2026-27 for children up to Class 3, that is the 3-to-9 age group. Option C is the correct answer and the key looks like a data-entry error.

short_explanation: After the 2010 Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis the RBI appointed the Malegam Committee, whose 2011 report produced the NBFC-MFI category and the caps that govern the sector.
explanation_text: The Andhra crisis came from multiple lending to the same borrower, coercive recovery and interest rates that were not visible to the borrower, ending in a state ordinance that halted repayments. The Malegam Committee's response was structural: create a separate NBFC-MFI class regulated by the RBI rather than by states, cap the margin and the interest rate, limit the number of MFIs that may lend to one borrower and cap total indebtedness, and require a minimum share of income-generating loans. This is the framework the RBI later revised in 2022 by moving from rate caps to a household-income-based affordability test.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Narasimham committees of 1991 and 1998 dealt with banking-sector and financial-system reform, not microfinance.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Bimal Jalan committee worked on the RBI's economic capital framework and on screening bank licence applicants.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: D. Subbarao was the RBI Governor under whom the committee was set up; the committee does not carry his name.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The Sivaraman Committee of 1979 recommended the creation of NABARD, a much earlier and different exercise.

common_traps: D. Subbarao was the Governor at the time, which makes his name look plausible; the committee is named after its chairman, Y.H. Malegam.

topic_name: Solar and renewable energy schemes in agriculture
short_explanation: PM-KUSUM exists to give farmers clean, dependable energy — solar pumps and solar plants on farmland that displace diesel and let the farmer sell surplus power — so it adds to farm income as well as de-dieselising irrigation.
explanation_text: The scheme has three components. Component A supports small decentralised grid-connected solar plants, up to 2 MW, on a farmer's barren or fallow land, with the power sold to the discom. Component B funds standalone off-grid solar pumps in place of diesel pumps. Component C solarises existing grid-connected pumps, so the farmer uses what is needed for irrigation and sells the rest. Income from power sale is what distinguishes KUSUM from a plain subsidy for pumps.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Cutting emissions from power plants is an effect the scheme contributes to, not its objective; KUSUM works on farm pumps and farmland, not on thermal generation.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The 175 GW renewable target belongs to the national renewable energy programme; KUSUM adds to it but was not framed as the way to meet it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Farm mechanisation is a different line of support; KUSUM deals with pumping and power sale, not with motorising farm operations.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The stem asks for the objective of the scheme, and A, B and D are consequences or unrelated aims rather than the stated objective.

key_note: A and B are genuine effects of the scheme, which makes 'all of the above' tempting. The scheme document states the objective as energy and water security for farmers together with additional income, which is what option C says.

topic_name: Pandemic relief packages and worker support
short_explanation: The insurance scheme for health workers fighting COVID-19, announced in March 2020 under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan package, gave a ₹50 lakh personal accident cover to healthcare providers — including sanitation staff, ASHA workers, paramedics and doctors — drafted for COVID care.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ₹10 lakh is not the cover announced; the figure was ₹50 lakh.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹20 lakh is not the cover; no likely reading of the announcement gives it.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹25 lakh is not the cover announced under this scheme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: ₹55 lakh is a near-miss on the announced figure of ₹50 lakh.

topic_name: Kisan Credit Card and agricultural credit
short_explanation: The Kisan Credit Card is a single flexible short-term credit line for the whole crop cycle — cultivation, post-harvest expenses, produce marketing, a household consumption component and maintenance of farm assets — so every purpose listed qualifies.
explanation_text: The KCC was designed in 1998 to replace repeated loan applications with one revolving limit, drawn and repaid as the season requires. The limit is worked out from the scale of finance for the crop and the area cultivated, with additions for consumption needs, asset maintenance and a term-loan component for allied activities. Interest subvention of 2% plus a further 3% for prompt repayment brings the effective rate on loans up to ₹3 lakh down to 4%. Since 2018-19 the card has been extended to animal husbandry and fisheries, and it is issued as a RuPay card so the farmer can draw at an ATM or a business correspondent.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Post-harvest expenses are covered, but so are the other three purposes.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Produce marketing loans are covered, but they are only one of the permitted purposes.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The household consumption requirement is a recognised component, but it is not the only one.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Maintenance of farm assets is covered, along with the other three.

short_explanation: The conditions describe Small Finance Banks: licensed to serve the unserved and unbanked, required to raise net worth to ₹200 crore within five years, and obliged to keep at least half the loan book in loans of up to ₹25 lakh.
explanation_text: Small Finance Banks were licensed from 2015 to do full banking — deposits and lending — but for a specific clientele: small business units, small and marginal farmers, micro and small industry and the unorganised sector. Three conditions define them. Priority sector lending must be 75% of adjusted net bank credit, against 40% for a universal bank. At least 50% of the loan portfolio must be loans up to ₹25 lakh. Net worth starts at ₹100 crore and must reach ₹200 crore within five years. Payments banks look similar on financial inclusion but cannot lend at all and face a deposit cap, so a loan-portfolio condition cannot apply to them.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Regional Rural Banks are set up under the RRB Act, 1976 with a sponsor bank and a fixed shareholding pattern; they do not carry these licensing conditions.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Payments banks are barred from lending altogether, so a condition on the composition of the loan portfolio cannot describe them.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Co-operative banks are registered under co-operative law and licensed separately; the ₹200 crore net-worth timetable is not their condition.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Foreign banks operate through branches or wholly owned subsidiaries under a different set of norms and are not a financial-inclusion licence category.

common_traps: Payments banks match condition 1 on financial inclusion, but condition 3 is about a loan portfolio and payments banks cannot lend.

short_explanation: In May 2021 the RBI brought bank lending to retail and wholesale traders, which had earlier been left out, under priority sector lending as part of MSME, so that credit kept flowing to these sectors during the second COVID wave.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Priority sector lending is defined by sector and loan size and is aimed at segments that would otherwise be underserved; corporate houses are not a PSL category.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Payments banks are themselves regulated entities, not a sector to which priority sector credit is directed.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Farmer producer organisations are already eligible under the agriculture category, and well before this extension — so they are not what was newly added.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Co-operative bodies are lenders or societies, not a priority sector category added by this move.

key_note: Option C is genuinely covered by priority sector lending, but under agriculture and long before this circular. The extension the question asks about is the one to retail and wholesale trade.

short_explanation: The draft that became NEP 2020 was prepared by the committee chaired by K. Kasturirangan, the space scientist and former ISRO chairman, which submitted its report in 2019.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: T.S.R. Subramanian chaired the earlier committee on a new education policy, which reported in 2016; its work fed into but did not become NEP 2020.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Uday Kotak chaired SEBI's committee on corporate governance, not an education committee.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Kailash Satyarthi is a child rights activist and Nobel laureate; he did not chair this committee.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: M. Subramaniam did not chair the NEP drafting committee.

common_traps: T.S.R. Subramanian chaired the 2016 education policy committee, which is the near neighbour here; the 2019 draft that became NEP 2020 is Kasturirangan's.

short_explanation: Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund the credit guarantee fee is paid by the government, not by the farmer or the borrower, so that is the statement which is not a feature of the scheme.
explanation_text: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund is a ₹1 lakh crore financing facility for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets — warehouses, grading and sorting units, cold chains, primary processing. The support is on the cost of credit rather than a capital subsidy: 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹2 crore for seven years, a cap on the lending rate so the subvention is not absorbed by the lender, and credit guarantee cover for loans up to ₹2 crore under CGTMSE with the guarantee fee borne by the government. Eligible borrowers include FPOs, primary agricultural credit societies, agri-entrepreneurs, self-help groups and start-ups.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Credit guarantee cover for loans up to ₹2 crore, under CGTMSE, is a genuine feature of the fund.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A cap on the lending rate is a genuine feature, and exists precisely so the interest subvention reaches the borrower.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The ₹2 crore ceiling per project is a real feature of the benefit structure, even if loosely worded here — see the key note.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This cannot hold, since the statement about who pays the guarantee fee is false.

key_note: Option C is loosely worded: ₹2 crore is the ceiling on the interest-subvention and guarantee benefit per project rather than an absolute cap on the loan itself. It is still nearer to a feature than the keyed option, which reverses who bears the guarantee fee.

short_explanation: NEP 2020 sets a gross enrolment ratio in higher education, including vocational education, of 50% by 2035, against 26.3% at the time the policy was written.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2025 is far too early for a target that nearly doubles the enrolment ratio.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2030 is the horizon of the Sustainable Development Goals, which the policy also cites; the GER target itself runs to 2035.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2040 is beyond the policy's stated horizon for this target.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2024 is not a target year in the policy.

common_traps: 2030 is the SDG horizon that NEP aligns to elsewhere, which makes it the natural wrong pick; the 50% GER target is set for 2035.

short_explanation: The Fifteenth Finance Commission's main report, submitted in November 2020, covers the five-year award period beginning 1 April 2021 and running to 2025-26.
explanation_text: Article 280 requires a Finance Commission every five years to recommend how central taxes are shared with the states and what grants-in-aid they receive. The Fifteenth Commission, chaired by N.K. Singh, was constituted in November 2017. Its terms of reference were extended, so it gave two reports: an interim one covering 2020-21 and the main one covering 2021-26. The main report kept the states' share of the divisible pool at 41%, using the 2011 population, area, forest and ecology, income distance, demographic performance and tax effort as the criteria.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 1 April 2020 is the start of the year covered by the Commission's interim report, not of the five-year award period — see the key note.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 1 April 2019 falls before any of the Commission's award periods.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 1 April 2018 is shortly after the Commission was constituted in November 2017, but its recommendations did not begin to apply then.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A defensible date is present among the options.

key_note: The item is loosely worded. The Commission was constituted in November 2017 and its interim report covered 2020-21, which makes 1 April 2020 a competing reading. The key takes the five-year award period of the main report, which commences 1 April 2021.

short_explanation: The Union Budget 2021-22 was presented as resting on six pillars: health and wellbeing; physical and financial capital and infrastructure; inclusive development for aspirational India; reinvigorating human capital; innovation and research and development; and minimum government with maximum governance.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Five understates the count; the budget speech listed six.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Seven overstates the count.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Eight overstates the count.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Nine overstates the count.

short_explanation: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended that states raise health spending to more than 8% of their own budgets by 2022, and that at least two-thirds of the health spend go to primary healthcare.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 3% understates the recommendation, and is closer to what states were then spending than to the target.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 4% is not the recommended share of state budgets.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 5% is not the recommended share.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 6% is not the recommended share; the Commission set the bar at more than 8%.

common_traps: The widely quoted 2.5% figure is public health spending as a share of GDP under the National Health Policy; this question asks for a share of state budgets, which is a different denominator.

topic_name: Pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers
short_explanation: Atal Pension Yojana is open to citizens aged 18 to 40 and pays a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month from age 60, so statements 1 and 2 hold; statement 3 is wrong because on the subscriber's death the spouse may continue the account or receive the same pension.
explanation_text: The contribution is fixed by the pension slab chosen and the age at joining, so someone entering at 18 pays much less each month for the same pension than someone entering at 40. The upper age of 40 exists because the scheme needs a minimum twenty-year contribution period. On the subscriber's death the spouse becomes the default nominee and can either continue contributing in the subscriber's account for the remaining period or take the accumulated corpus; on the death of both, the corpus goes to the nominee. The scheme is administered by PFRDA and accessed through a bank or post office account.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 1 is right, but statement 2 on the ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 pension range is also correct.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 2 is right, but statement 1 on the 18-to-40 age band is also correct.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Statement 3 is wrong — the spouse is the default nominee and may continue the subscription.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Statements 1 and 2 are correct but statement 3 is not, so the three cannot all hold.

topic_name: DAY-NRLM, self-help groups and rural livelihoods
short_explanation: Supporting women's self-help groups, skilling rural youth for livelihoods and moving poor households into gainful self-employment are the three planks of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, DAY-NRLM.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana is a relief package of free foodgrain and cash transfers, not a livelihoods mission.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Atal Pension Yojana is a contributory old-age pension scheme with no SHG or skilling component.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana is a pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: MGNREGA guarantees wage employment on public works; it does not promote self-help groups or self-employment.

common_traps: MGNREGA and NRLM are both flagship rural schemes, but MGNREGA is wage employment on public works while NRLM works through SHGs towards self-employment.

short_explanation: The Union Budget 2021-22 pegged the fiscal deficit at 6.8% of GDP for 2021-22, against a revised estimate of 9.5% for 2020-21, with a glide path to below 4.5% by 2025-26.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 9.2% is close to the revised estimate for the pandemic year 2020-21, which was 9.5%, but it is neither that figure nor the 2021-22 estimate.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 6% is not the budget estimate; the figure presented was 6.8%.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 6.5% is a near-miss on 6.8%.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 7% rounds the estimate up; the budget figure was 6.8%.

common_traps: 9.5% was the revised estimate for 2020-21; the question asks for the 2021-22 budget estimate, which is 6.8%.

short_explanation: Budget 2021-22 raised the turnover threshold for compulsory tax audit from ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore, but only for businesses where at least 95% of receipts and payments are made digitally.
explanation_text: The base threshold for tax audit under Section 44AB is ₹1 crore. In 2020 it was raised to ₹5 crore for businesses whose cash receipts and cash payments were each no more than 5% of the total, and in 2021 that relaxed threshold was moved up to ₹10 crore. The relief is therefore conditional, not general: a business that deals substantially in cash stays on the ₹1 crore threshold. Structuring it this way makes the compliance saving an incentive to go digital rather than a blanket concession.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹25 crore overstates the new threshold; the increase announced was to ₹10 crore.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹50 crore is not the audit threshold under Section 44AB.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹75 crore is not the audit threshold.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: ₹100 crore is not the audit threshold.

common_traps: The ₹10 crore threshold applies only where 95% or more of receipts and payments are non-cash; a cash-heavy business does not get it.

short_explanation: PMAY-Urban was launched on 25 June 2015, not 2014, which makes that the incorrect statement; the other four describe the mission correctly.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Support for houses up to 30 square metres of carpet area is a genuine provision for EWS houses under the in-situ redevelopment and beneficiary-led verticals.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The mission does run through four verticals — in-situ slum redevelopment, credit-linked subsidy, affordable housing in partnership and beneficiary-led construction.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Housing for all by 2022 is the mission's stated goal.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This cannot hold, since the launch year stated in option C is wrong.

common_traps: The stem asks for the incorrect statement; the other four are all real features, so a reader scanning for something true will pick one of them.

topic_name: Social legislation on women, children and the elderly
short_explanation: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 a child is a male who has not completed 21 years and a female who has not completed 18 years.
explanation_text: The Act replaced the 1929 Child Marriage Restraint Act and changed the remedy as much as the definition. A child marriage is voidable at the option of the contracting party who was a child, on a petition filed up to two years after attaining majority; a marriage is void outright where the child was taken away by force, enticement or trafficking. States must appoint Child Marriage Prohibition Officers, and courts can issue injunctions to stop a marriage before it takes place. Maintenance and residence for the female contracting party, and legitimacy of children born of such a marriage, are protected whatever the outcome.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 15 years for a girl is the old threshold used in other contexts, not the Act's definition, which is 18.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 14 and 18 are both below the Act's definitions.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 21 for boys is right, but a girl is a child until 18, not 15.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Neither figure matches the Act.

topic_name: Multilateral development banks and the IMF
short_explanation: The New Development Bank's membership and lending are not confined to BRICS — Bangladesh, the UAE and Egypt were admitted from 2021 — so the statement that it cannot lend outside BRICS is the incorrect one.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The bank was indeed established by the BRICS countries, agreed at the Fortaleza summit in 2014.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: It is headquartered in Shanghai, with a regional centre in Johannesburg.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The initial authorised capital was $100 billion, of which $50 billion was initially subscribed, equally among the five founders.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: K.V. Kamath was the bank's first president, from 2015.

common_traps: The stem asks for the incorrect statement, so the four true facts about the bank are the ones to leave alone.

short_explanation: Afghanistan holds observer status at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation rather than membership; India, Pakistan, China and Tajikistan are all full members.
explanation_text: The SCO grew out of the Shanghai Five of 1996 and was formally established in 2001 with China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan were admitted as full members in 2017, and Iran's accession followed later. Around the members sit observers — Afghanistan, Belarus and Mongolia at the time of this question — and dialogue partners. Observers attend but do not vote, which is the distinction this question turns on.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: India became a full member in 2017.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pakistan became a full member in 2017, alongside India.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: China is a founding member and the organisation is named after Shanghai.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Tajikistan is a founding member from the Shanghai Five.

common_traps: Observer status is not membership — Afghanistan, Belarus and Mongolia were observers, which is easy to read as being in the grouping.

short_explanation: ASEAN's ten members are Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia; India is a dialogue partner, not a member.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Myanmar joined ASEAN in 1997.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Vietnam joined in 1995.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Thailand is one of the five founding members from 1967.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Cambodia joined in 1999, the most recent accession.

common_traps: India takes part in the East Asia Summit, the ASEAN-India summits and RCEP negotiations, which makes it look like a member; it is a dialogue partner.

topic_name: Labour laws, wages and maternity benefit
short_explanation: Minimum wage fixation follows the norms set by the Indian Labour Conference in 1957, which take a daily intake of 2,700 calories per consumption unit for a worker's family of three consumption units.
explanation_text: The 1957 norms build the wage from a basket rather than from a wage index. They assume a standard working-class family of three consumption units, a net intake of 2,700 calories per consumption unit per day, 72 yards of cloth a year for the family, rent at the minimum provided under government housing, and fuel, lighting and other miscellaneous items at 20% of the total. The Supreme Court in the Raptakos Brett case added a further 25% for children's education, medical needs, recreation and provision for old age and marriage. These components together are what a 'need-based minimum wage' means in Indian labour law.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2,200 calories is a poverty-line style intake norm, not the minimum-wage norm of 2,700.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2,500 calories is not the figure adopted by the Indian Labour Conference.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2,600 calories is a near-miss on the 2,700 norm.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2,650 calories is a near-miss on the 2,700 norm.

topic_name: Balance of payments and the external sector
short_explanation: The balance of payments is the account in which a country records its transactions with the rest of the world, and its current account is where exports of goods and services are set against imports.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: There is no document called a National Trade Policy that records this netting; trade policy sets rules, it does not account for flows.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The World Trade Report is a WTO analytical publication on global trade trends, not a record of India's own external transactions.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The annual budget records the government's receipts and expenditure, which is a domestic fiscal account.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The Economic Survey reviews the economy and comments on the external sector, but the account itself is the balance of payments.

key_note: Strictly, the difference between exports and imports of goods and services is the trade balance, which sits inside the current account of the balance of payments; the balance of payments is the wider account including capital and financial flows. Among the five options it is the only one that records these transactions at all, so the key is defensible.

short_explanation: The Banks Board Bureau recommended candidates for the posts of Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, and other whole-time directors, of public sector banks; the government then made the appointment.
explanation_text: The Bureau was set up in 2016 on the lines suggested by the P.J. Nayak committee, to take the selection of public sector bank leadership out of routine ministerial process and put it before a body with banking expertise. Its remit covered PSBs, public sector insurers and other financial institutions, and extended beyond selection to advising on succession planning and governance. Its recommendations went to the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet for the final decision. In 2022 it was reconstituted as the Financial Services Institutions Bureau after a court held that it could not select insurance company directors.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Finance Ministry processes the appointment through the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, but the recommendation came from the Bureau.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: IBPS conducts common recruitment examinations for clerical and officer cadres; it has no role in selecting bank chiefs.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The RBI regulates and supervises banks and approves private bank CEO appointments, but does not select public sector bank heads.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The Financial Stability and Development Council is an inter-regulatory forum on financial stability, not an appointments body.

key_note: As of 2021 the recommending body was the Banks Board Bureau; it was reconstituted as the Financial Services Institutions Bureau in 2022, so a current-affairs version of this question would read differently.

short_explanation: Retail inflation is measured by the Consumer Price Index, which tracks the prices households actually pay and is the anchor for the RBI's inflation-targeting framework.
explanation_text: CPI and WPI measure different stages of the same economy. CPI Combined, compiled by the National Statistical Office, weights a household consumption basket in which food and beverages alone account for about 46%, and includes services such as housing, education and health. WPI, compiled by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, covers transactions at the wholesale or producer stage, excludes services altogether and carries a large manufactured-products weight. Since 2016 the monetary policy framework targets CPI inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percentage points, which is why CPI is the number the RBI reacts to.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Wholesale Price Index measures price change at the wholesale or producer stage and excludes services, so it is not retail inflation.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Index of Industrial Production measures the volume of industrial output, not prices.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Real GDP measures output at constant prices; it is not an inflation indicator.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Nominal GDP measures output at current prices; the gap between it and real GDP gives the deflator, which is still not the retail inflation measure.

common_traps: WPI is inflation at the wholesale stage. Retail inflation, the number quoted in monetary policy, is CPI.

short_explanation: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members — 15 elected by the Lok Sabha and 7 by the Rajya Sabha, each for a one-year term.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Only 7 of the 22 members come from the Rajya Sabha; the other 15 are elected by the Lok Sabha.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: This statement is also true — examining the CAG's audit reports is the committee's central function. See the key note.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: This statement is also true — by convention followed since 1967 the chairperson is drawn from the opposition. See the key note.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This statement was also true at the time — Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury chaired the committee in 2021. See the key note.

key_note: The item is defective: options C, D and E were all true statements as well, so a stem asking for 'the correct statement' has four correct answers. Only option B is unambiguously false. The key takes A, which is accurate, so it is defensible, but the stem should have asked which statement is incorrect.

short_explanation: The Food and Agriculture Organization is headquartered in Rome, not Geneva, so that is the statement which is not correct.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Qu Dongyu has been Director-General since 2019, so this statement is correct.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The membership figure stated is correct as the question puts it — see the key note.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The FAO is a specialised agency of the United Nations, so this statement is correct.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A statement that is not correct is present, so this cannot hold.

key_note: The FAO's own count is 195 members — 194 member nations plus the European Union, with two associate members — so option C is slightly loose. It is not the statement the question is after, since the headquarters claim is plainly wrong.

short_explanation: Beej Bachao Andolan, the seed-saving movement begun in Tehri Garhwal in 1986, is associated with Vijay Jardhari, who walked the hills collecting and reviving traditional crop varieties.
explanation_text: The movement grew out of Chipko, but its target was different. Where Chipko resisted commercial felling, Beej Bachao Andolan resisted the replacement of local seed by a narrow set of high-yielding varieties. Its central practice is baranaja, the twelve-grain mixed cropping system of the Garhwal hills in which pulses, millets, oilseeds and creepers are grown together on the same plot so that soil fertility, fodder and a household's nutrition are all served at once. Jardhari's collection ran to hundreds of rice and rajma varieties kept in circulation through farmer-to-farmer exchange rather than a formal gene bank.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pema Khandu is a political figure from Arunachal Pradesh with no connection to this movement.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Chandi Prasad Bhatt is a leader of the Chipko movement, not of Beej Bachao Andolan.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Sunderlal Bahuguna is the other well-known Chipko figure; the seed movement is a separate campaign.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A correct name is present among the options.

common_traps: Bhatt and Bahuguna belong to Chipko in the same hills. Beej Bachao Andolan grew out of that milieu but is a distinct movement with a distinct leader.

short_explanation: Article 24 prohibits the employment of any child below 14 years in a factory, mine or other hazardous occupation.
explanation_text: Articles 23 and 24 together form the Right against Exploitation. Article 23 bans traffic in human beings, begar and other forms of forced labour; Article 24 bans hazardous child labour. Article 24 is absolute for the listed settings but does not prohibit all child work, which is why the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act and its 2016 amendment were needed to extend the bar to all employment below 14 and to hazardous work for adolescents aged 14 to 18.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Article 20 gives protection in respect of conviction for offences — no ex post facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Article 22 gives protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Article 23 prohibits trafficking and forced labour — the other half of the Right against Exploitation, but not the child labour provision.

common_traps: Article 23 sits immediately before Article 24 and covers the same fundamental right, so the two are easy to swap; trafficking and forced labour is 23, hazardous child labour is 24.

short_explanation: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists 22 languages.
explanation_text: The Schedule began with 14 languages. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment in 1967. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment in 1992, taking the count to 18. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003, taking it to 22. Inclusion matters because Article 351 requires Hindi to draw on these languages for its vocabulary, and because candidates may write public examinations in any of them.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 18 was the count between 1992 and 2003, before Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 25 overstates the count; no amendment has taken the Schedule past 22.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 16 does not match any stage of the Schedule.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 23 is a near-miss; the Schedule stands at 22.

common_traps: 18 was the correct answer for the decade before 2003, so older material still carries it.

topic_name: Panchayati Raj institutions and rural governance
short_explanation: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 24 April, marking the day the 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force in 1993.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 22 March is World Water Day, not Panchayati Raj Day.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 20 April is not the date; the 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 5 June is World Environment Day.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 23 December is observed as Kisan Diwas, the birth anniversary of Chaudhary Charan Singh.

topic_name: DAY-NRLM, self-help groups and rural livelihoods
short_explanation: Under DAY-NRLM a women's self-help group in the designated districts borrows at 7% and receives a further 3% interest subvention on prompt repayment, which brings the effective cost of credit down to 4%.
explanation_text: The subvention works in two different ways depending on the district. In the 250 Category I districts, banks lend to women's SHGs at 7% up to ₹3 lakh and are reimbursed the difference between their lending rate and 7%, with an additional 3% subvention paid to the SHG on prompt repayment — the effective 4%. In the remaining Category II districts the subvention is administered by the state rural livelihoods missions rather than reimbursed to banks. Either way the prompt-repayment incentive is the 3% component, and it is conditional on the account staying regular.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 7% is the concessional rate at which the SHG borrows, not the subvention on top of it.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 9% is closer to a normal commercial lending rate than to the subvention.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 5% is not the subvention rate under the mission.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 10% is not the subvention rate; the prompt-repayment incentive is 3%.

common_traps: 7% is the rate the SHG pays and 3% is the additional subvention for prompt repayment — the question asks for the subvention, not the lending rate.
key_note: The 3% figure is the additional prompt-repayment subvention. Read as 'the concession versus the normal lending rate' the number would be larger, so the framing matters.

topic_name: Kisan Credit Card and agricultural credit targets
short_explanation: Household expenditure is the one item in this list that the Kisan Credit Card circular does not name as a purpose; the scheme's own wording covers crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses, produce marketing loan, maintenance of farm assets and allied activities, and investment credit.
explanation_text: The KCC single window is built as a revolving cash credit limit fixed on the scale of finance for the crop and the area cultivated, drawn and repaid any number of times within the year. Its purposes are set out in the RBI master circular, and the interest subvention plus prompt repayment incentive apply to the crop loan portion up to the prescribed ceiling. The card was later extended to animal husbandry and fisheries.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Post-harvest expenses are explicitly covered, which is what lets the farmer hold produce instead of distress-selling.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Short term credit for raising crops is the core purpose of the card.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Produce marketing loan is a listed purpose, granted against produce held after harvest.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Working capital for maintenance of farm assets and for allied activities such as dairy or fisheries is a listed purpose.

common_traps: The stem asks which is NOT covered, so a reader who scans for a true statement will pick a covered item.
key_note: The RBI master circular does list 'consumption requirements of farmer household' as a KCC purpose, so household needs are not wholly outside the scheme; the key stands only because the loose phrase 'household expenditure' is not one of the scheme's stated purposes while the other four are quoted almost verbatim from it. Treat this as a loosely drafted item.

short_explanation: Catfish are potamodromous: they complete their whole life cycle in fresh water and migrate only within rivers and lakes, typically upstream to spawn.
explanation_text: Migratory fish are grouped by the waters they cross. Diadromous fish move between the sea and fresh water, and split into anadromous, which grow in the sea and breed in fresh water, and catadromous, which grow in fresh water and breed in the sea. Potamodromous fish stay entirely within fresh water, and oceanodromous fish entirely within the sea. Most Indian carps, including catla and rohu, are potamodromous, moving upstream with the first monsoon flood to breed.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Salmon is the standard anadromous example, growing in the sea and running up rivers to spawn.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Eel is the standard catadromous example, growing in fresh water and breeding in the sea.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Lamprey species of this kind are anadromous, breeding in fresh water after life at sea.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Grouper is a marine fish and moves within the sea, so it is oceanodromous, not potamodromous.

common_traps: Anadromous and catadromous are easy to reverse; salmon runs up the river to breed, the eel runs down to the sea.

short_explanation: The National Forest Policy of 1988 sets the national goal at 33 per cent of the geographical area under forest or tree cover.
explanation_text: The same policy splits the target by terrain: about 60 per cent in the hills, to hold soil and protect catchments, and about 20 per cent in the plains. Actual forest cover reported by the Forest Survey of India is around 21 to 22 per cent, and forest plus tree cover about 24 to 25 per cent, so the 33 per cent figure is a goal and not a current reading.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 27 per cent is not a policy figure; it sits between the actual cover and the target.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 25 per cent is close to India's actual forest and tree cover together, not the policy goal.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 20 per cent is the policy's sub-target for the plains, not the national figure.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 40 per cent is not a target in any Indian forest policy.

common_traps: 20 per cent is a real number from the same policy, but it applies only to the plains.

short_explanation: e-Choupal is ITC's village internet kiosk network, begun in 2000, which gives farmers prices, weather and agronomy advice directly and lets ITC buy produce from them without the chain of intermediaries.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: e-RaKAM is a government-side electronic auction platform for agricultural produce, run with MSTC and the Central Railside Warehouse Company.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: e-NAM is the government's national electronic market linking regulated mandis, not a company initiative.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: e-Clinic is not an ITC agricultural initiative.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: e-Commerce is a generic term for online trade, not the name of any initiative.

short_explanation: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was set up in 1995-96 with NABARD, to lend to state governments for rural infrastructure projects left unfinished for want of funds.
explanation_text: RIDF is funded by the shortfall in banks' priority sector lending: a scheduled commercial bank that misses its agriculture or priority sector target deposits the shortfall with NABARD, and NABARD on-lends it to states for irrigation, rural roads and bridges, drinking water, watershed development and similar assets. It is renewed and re-corpused in each Union Budget, which is why RIDF tranche numbers keep rising.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 1991 is the year of the economic reforms, not of RIDF; NABARD itself was set up in 1982.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 1999 is not the constitution year; by then RIDF was already several tranches old.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2000 is too late by five years.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2005 is the year of major financial inclusion moves, not of RIDF.

topic_name: Operational land holdings and farm size classification
short_explanation: A small farmer is one operating between 1 and 2 hectares; below 1 hectare the holding is marginal.
explanation_text: The Agriculture Census classes holdings as marginal below 1 hectare, small 1 to 2 hectares, semi-medium 2 to 4, medium 4 to 10, and large above 10 hectares. Small and marginal holdings together are more than 85 per cent of all holdings in India, which is why credit, insurance and subsidy schemes are usually designed around the small-and-marginal group.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Below 1 hectare is the marginal farmer class.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2 to 4 hectares is semi-medium.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 4 to 10 hectares is medium.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Above 10 hectares is large.

common_traps: Small and marginal are routinely used as one phrase, but the categories are separate and the boundary is 1 hectare.

topic_name: Irrigation projects and command area classification
short_explanation: A medium irrigation project is one with a cultivable command area between 2,000 and 10,000 hectares.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Below 2,000 hectares is a minor irrigation project.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Above 10,000 hectares is a major project.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 5,000 to 10,000 hectares is part of the medium range, not the whole of it, so it cannot be the definition.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 10 to 100 hectares is far too small to be a defined project class.

common_traps: Option D lies inside the correct range and reads plausibly; the class boundary starts at 2,000 hectares, not 5,000.

short_explanation: Maharashtra has the largest number of Farmer Producer Organisations in the country, built up over years of promotion by the state, SFAC and NABARD.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Madhya Pradesh has a large FPO base but fewer than Maharashtra.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Karnataka has an active FPO programme, still behind Maharashtra in numbers.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Uttar Pradesh has many FPOs under the newer scheme but did not lead on the count at the time of this paper.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: West Bengal is not among the leading states by FPO count.

short_explanation: Alley cropping is the agroforestry system in which trees or shrubs are grown in hedgerows and the arable crop is raised in the alleys between them.
explanation_text: The hedgerows, usually fast-growing leguminous species such as Leucaena or Gliricidia, are cut back regularly and the loppings are spread in the alleys as green manure and mulch. That returns nitrogen and organic matter to the crop while the roots hold the soil, which is why alley cropping is recommended on sloping and degraded land.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Avenue planting means trees along roads, canals and field boundaries, with no crop grown in defined alleys between hedgerows.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Border crops are rows of a crop planted around the edge of a field, often as a barrier, and involve no tree hedgerow.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Ley farming alternates arable crops with a pasture or grass phase in time, not trees and crops together in space.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Skip cropping means leaving rows or a season out to conserve moisture; it involves no trees.

short_explanation: Cow dung is the only organic material in the list; it is a bulky organic manure supplying nutrients and organic matter as it decomposes, while the rest are manufactured inorganic fertilisers.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Ammonium nitrate is a synthetic nitrogenous fertiliser.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: DAP, di-ammonium phosphate, is a manufactured fertiliser supplying nitrogen and phosphorus.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: SSP, single super phosphate, is a manufactured phosphatic fertiliser that also carries sulphur and calcium.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: DCP, di-calcium phosphate, is an inorganic phosphate compound.

key_note: Strictly cow dung is a manure rather than a fertiliser, since its nutrient content is low and variable; the question uses the words loosely.

short_explanation: The Fourth All India Handloom Census of 2019-20 found that about 88.7 per cent of weaver households are in rural areas, with the remainder in towns.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 11.3 per cent is the urban share, the complement of the correct figure.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 66.3 per cent understates the rural concentration reported by the census.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 36.1 per cent is far below the reported rural share.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 69.8 per cent is not a census figure for rural weaver households.

common_traps: 11.3 per cent is the urban complement of the answer and is the easiest wrong pick if the question is read as asking about towns.

short_explanation: A wheel hoe is a manually pushed implement used for weeding and for intercultural work such as loosening the soil crust between crop rows, so both the listed uses apply.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Weeding is one of its uses, but it is not the only one, so this is incomplete.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Intercultural operation is also a use, and again incomplete on its own.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A wheel hoe does not place and cover seed; sowing needs a seed drill or a dibbler.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: It is not a fertiliser applicator, though the soil loosening it does may be followed by top dressing.

key_note: Weeding is itself an intercultural operation, so the two options overlap; the combined option is the only one that is not incomplete.

topic_name: Food security and the public distribution system
short_explanation: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana gave 5 kg of foodgrain per person per month free, over and above the regular ration, to NFSA beneficiaries from March 2020 during the pandemic.
explanation_text: The regular entitlement under the National Food Security Act is 5 kg per person per month for priority households at subsidised prices, and 35 kg per household per month for Antyodaya households. PMGKAY did not replace that; it doubled the priority household's grain by adding a free 5 kg on top, and the scheme was extended in phases well beyond its first three months.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The National Rural Livelihood Mission organises rural women into self-help groups for livelihood support; it distributes no foodgrain.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Targeted Public Distribution System is the base system through which the regular entitlement is delivered, not the additional free allocation.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Antyodaya Anna Yojana covers the poorest households with 35 kg per household per month, a household entitlement, not a per-person top-up.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The regular NFSA entitlement is also 5 kg per person per month, so the number alone does not identify the scheme; the word additionally does.

short_explanation: Hens kept for egg production are layers; birds raised for meat are broilers.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A broiler is a bird reared for meat, marketed at about six weeks.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Grower is an age stage, roughly eight to twenty weeks, covering birds not yet in lay.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A pullet is a young female bird before it begins laying.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A cockerel is a young male bird.

short_explanation: Salting, drying, smoking and pickling are together called curing, the traditional low-cost methods of preserving fish by removing water or adding salt, smoke or acid so that spoilage organisms cannot grow.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Canning seals fish in a container and heat-sterilises it; it is an industrial process, not a traditional one.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Conditioning is not a fish preservation class.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Irradiation kills spoilage organisms with ionising radiation and is a modern technique.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Pasteurisation is mild heat treatment, used for products like crab meat, not the traditional group named here.

short_explanation: Vegetables are the largest group of commodities traded through e-NAM, the electronic national agriculture market that links regulated mandis on a single trading platform.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pulses trade on e-NAM but in much smaller quantity than vegetables.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Oilseeds are a significant traded group, still below vegetables.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Fruits are traded, but vegetable arrivals at mandis are far larger.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Cereals move largely through procurement at minimum support price rather than through e-NAM auctions.

key_note: The ranking of commodities traded on e-NAM shifts from year to year and the keyed answer should be checked against the e-NAM trade data for the year in question before this explanation is published.

short_explanation: Mulching is covering the soil surface with crop residue, straw or plastic so that evaporation from the surface falls and the moisture stays available to the crop.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Contingent cropping is the fallback crop plan used when the monsoon fails or is delayed.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Restorative cropping means growing soil-improving crops such as legumes to rebuild fertility.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Cover cropping grows a living crop to protect the soil; the stem describes dead residue spread on the surface.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Only one of the listed practices matches the stem, so a combined option cannot be right.

common_traps: Cover cropping and mulching both protect the surface; the difference is a living crop versus dead residue laid on top.

topic_name: Soil types and their distribution in India
short_explanation: Red soil gets its colour from iron oxide diffused widely through the soil mass, formed by the weathering of old crystalline and metamorphic rocks of the peninsula.
explanation_text: Red soils cover much of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, eastern Madhya Pradesh and parts of Odisha and Chhattisgarh. They are generally light in texture, low in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus, and slightly acidic, so they need manuring and irrigation to give good yields. Laterite soil is also iron-rich and red, but its colour comes from intense leaching under heavy seasonal rainfall, which strips silica and leaves iron and aluminium oxides concentrated at the surface rather than diffused.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Black soil owes its colour to titaniferous magnetite and humus in the weathered Deccan lava, not to diffused iron oxide.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Alluvial soil is transported river deposit, and its colour depends on the sediment, not on iron oxide diffusion.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Regur is simply another name for black cotton soil, so it repeats option A.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Laterite soil is iron-rich too, but it is formed by intense leaching that concentrates iron and aluminium oxides, not by wide diffusion of iron oxide.

common_traps: Laterite is the trap, since it is also red and iron-rich; and options A and D name the same soil, so neither can be the single answer.

short_explanation: Atal Bhujal Yojana aims at improving groundwater management in water-stressed blocks, by getting the community to prepare and act on its own water budget and water security plan.
explanation_text: The scheme runs in identified water-stressed blocks in seven states including Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, under the Ministry of Jal Shakti with World Bank assistance. Half the outlay is an incentive component paid to states on results such as measured water level data, public disclosure of it, and preparation of water security plans, which makes it a demand-side behaviour scheme rather than a construction scheme.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Raising water use efficiency by a fixed percentage is a target of the National Water Mission, not the stated objective of this scheme.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Restoring the ecological balance of catchments through in-situ moisture conservation is the objective of watershed development programmes.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Basin-level integrated water resources management is a National Water Mission goal covering surface and ground water together, while Atal Bhujal Yojana is specifically a groundwater scheme at block level.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Only the first objective belongs to this scheme, so the combined option fails.

short_explanation: A hygrometer measures atmospheric humidity; the wet and dry bulb pair used in agro-meteorological observatories is its common field form.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A pyranometer measures incoming solar radiation on a horizontal surface.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A pycnometer measures density or specific gravity of a liquid or a solid.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A tensiometer measures soil moisture tension, that is how tightly water is held in the soil.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A piezometer measures groundwater pressure and water level in a well or aquifer.

short_explanation: The Emissions Gap Report 2020 of UNEP estimated that global carbon dioxide emissions would fall by about 7 per cent in 2020 because of the pandemic shutdowns.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2 per cent understates the pandemic year's fall.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 5 per cent is close to the reported drop but not the figure the report gave.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 10 per cent overstates it; no assessment put the 2020 fall in double digits.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 1.5 per cent is an arbitrary figure here; 1.5 degrees is the Paris temperature goal, not an emissions change.

short_explanation: Growing two or more crops together on the same field with no definite row arrangement is mixed cropping; when the same crops are grown together in a defined row pattern it becomes intercropping.
explanation_text: Mixed cropping is the older, subsistence-oriented practice: the seed is mixed and broadcast, the aim is insurance against total failure rather than maximum yield, and the produce is often used together as a mixed grain. Intercropping is deliberate, with a fixed row ratio such as two rows of groundnut to one of pigeonpea, so that each crop can be managed and harvested separately.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Sequential cropping grows crops one after another on the same land in a year, not at the same time.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Multistoreyed cropping arranges crops of different heights in tiers, as in a coconut garden, which is a definite arrangement.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Parallel cropping means component crops whose growth habits and demands barely compete, and it is still a form of intercropping with a pattern.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Ratoon cropping takes a second harvest from the regrowth of the stubble of the first, as in sugarcane.

common_traps: Mixed cropping and intercropping are separated only by whether there is a definite row pattern; the stem's phrase without any definite row pattern is the deciding clause.

short_explanation: Wallowing is the buffalo's habit of rolling in mud or water; it is how the animal loses heat, since buffaloes have few sweat glands and dark skin.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Weaning is separating the young animal from its mother's milk and moving it to other feed.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Brooding is providing warmth and care to newly hatched chicks.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Crutching is shearing the wool around the hindquarters of a sheep for hygiene.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water drop by drop directly to the root zone through emitters, and soluble fertiliser can be injected into the same line, which is called fertigation.
explanation_text: Because water is applied only over the root zone and not over the whole field, drip cuts evaporation and deep percolation and typically raises water use efficiency to around ninety per cent against forty to fifty for surface methods. It suits widely spaced crops such as orchards, sugarcane, cotton and vegetables, and is supported as micro-irrigation under the Per Drop More Crop component of PMKSY.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Sprinkler irrigation throws water over the canopy as artificial rain, wetting the whole area rather than the root zone.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The check basin method floods small level basins and is a surface method.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Corrugation runs water down small closely spaced channels for close-growing crops.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The furrow method carries water in furrows between ridges, wetting a broad strip of soil.

short_explanation: The SUJALAM campaign for ODF Plus, which set out to build a million soak pits for greywater management, is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
explanation_text: Open defecation free status is only the first stage. ODF Plus adds solid and liquid waste management, so that a village that has stopped open defecation also handles its greywater and solid waste; soak pits are the simplest greywater answer, letting kitchen and bath water percolate instead of pooling in the street. The Swachh Bharat Mission Grameen, which carries this work, moved from the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation to the Ministry of Jal Shakti when that ministry was formed in 2019.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Ministry of Rural Development ran rural sanitation in earlier years, but the department was moved to Jal Shakti.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Health and Family Welfare handles public health services, not the rural sanitation mission.

option_rationales.label: D
