option_rationales.rationale: Kerala's cooperative movement is deep, particularly in credit and consumer societies, but Maharashtra has more societies.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Uttarakhand is a small state with a correspondingly small number of societies.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Tamil Nadu has a large cooperative network but stands behind Maharashtra in number.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: India's FDI policy opens each of these farm activities to 100% foreign investment under the automatic route, so no single option can be the answer.
explanation_text: Agriculture is not open to FDI in general — only the activities the policy lists. Floriculture, horticulture, apiculture and the cultivation of vegetables and mushrooms are allowed 100% under the automatic route when carried on under controlled conditions, as are pisciculture, aquaculture and animal husbandry, the development and production of seeds and planting material, and services related to the agro and allied sectors. The plantation sector is opened by name: tea, coffee, rubber, cardamom, palm oil tree and olive oil tree plantations. Anything outside those heads, including ordinary crop farming and the holding of farm land, remains closed to foreign investment.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Horticulture is indeed permitted at 100% under the automatic route, but so are the other three activities listed, so picking it alone understates the policy.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Coffee production is open to 100% FDI as one of the plantation crops named in the policy; it is not the only qualifying activity here.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Palm oil tree plantation is one of the plantations opened by name, yet the other options are covered on the same terms.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Pisciculture is allowed 100% through the automatic route along with aquaculture and animal husbandry, so it cannot be the sole answer.

common_traps: "100% under the automatic route" does not mean agriculture as a whole is open to FDI — only the activities the policy names, and several of them only under controlled conditions.

short_explanation: India has about 14,500 kilometres of navigable inland waterways, and the plan referred to is to develop these and link them to strategic locations on international maritime trade routes.
explanation_text: The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 waterways as national waterways, of which only a handful carry meaningful cargo today. The Inland Waterways Authority of India, under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, develops them, and the Jal Marg Vikas Project on National Waterway 1 - the Haldia to Varanasi stretch of the Ganga - is the flagship, built with World Bank support. The case for waterways is cost: moving a tonne a kilometre by river uses less fuel and money than road or rail, though it is slower and depends on an assured depth of water.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary figure; the navigable length usually quoted is about 14,500 km.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary figure; the navigable length usually quoted is about 14,500 km.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary figure; the navigable length usually quoted is about 14,500 km.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: 14,500 km is the navigable length; 111 is the number of national waterways declared under the 2016 Act.
key_note: The stem is garbled - it reads as though waterways will be 'built' - but the figure asked for is the navigable length, about 14,500 km.

short_explanation: Licensed opium poppy cultivation is permitted only in notified tracts of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, so Rajasthan completes the set. Licences are issued crop year by crop year by the Central Bureau of Narcotics under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Gujarat has no notified opium tracts; cultivation is confined to Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Tamil Nadu is not among the notified states for licensed poppy cultivation.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Karnataka is not a notified opium-growing state; poppy found there is illicit and liable to destruction.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Kerala is not notified for opium cultivation under the licensing system.

topic_name: Employees' provident fund, ESI and statutory social security
short_explanation: The Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme was framed in 1976 under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and gives EPF members a death cover linked to their provident fund balance.
explanation_text: EDLI is one of the three schemes EPFO administers, alongside the EPF Scheme of 1952 and the Employees' Pension Scheme of 1995. The employee pays nothing towards it: the employer contributes 0.5% of wages, subject to the wage ceiling, into the insurance fund. If a member dies while in service, the nominee receives an assurance benefit worked out from the last drawn wages and the average provident fund balance, subject to a minimum and a maximum fixed by notification. Coverage is automatic — no separate enrolment, no medical test.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: No EPFO scheme dates from 1978; EDLI was notified two years earlier, in 1976.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 1979 is after the scheme was already running; the deposit-linked insurance cover dates from 1976.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 1980 belongs to no EPFO scheme — of the three, EDLI is the 1976 one, the Provident Fund Scheme dates from 1952 and the Pension Scheme from 1995.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Mission Shakti is the Women and Child Development Ministry's umbrella programme for women's safety and empowerment, approved for the 15th Finance Commission cycle that runs from 2021-22 to 2025-26.
explanation_text: It gathers older women-centred schemes into two verticals. Sambal covers safety and protection — One Stop Centres, the women's helpline, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Nari Adalats. Samarthya covers empowerment and support — Shakti Sadan and Sakhi Niwas, creches, the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana and assistance to working women. Reading the end year off the Finance Commission cycle is the reliable way to remember it: the 15th Commission's award period itself ends in 2025-26, and umbrella schemes approved inside that period are co-terminous with it.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2024-25 falls a year short of the 15th Finance Commission award period the scheme is tied to.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2026-27 runs past the award period, which closes in 2025-26.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2027-28 is two years beyond the cycle the scheme was approved for.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: MSME gross value added worked out to about 30% of India's GDP in 2018-19, the share the MSME Ministry's annual report carries for that year.
explanation_text: Three MSME shares circulate and they are not interchangeable. The share of GVA in GDP is around 30%. The share of MSME manufacturing output in total manufacturing output is around 36%. The share of MSME-related products in India's exports is in the 45-49% range. All three have moved between years, so each should be quoted with its year attached rather than as a standing fact.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 25% understates the sector; the figure reported for 2018-19 is about 30%.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 31% is a near neighbour rather than an obvious error, because the ministry's own table shows a shade over 30 — but the keyed value is 30%.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 35% is closer to the MSME share of manufacturing output than to its share of GDP.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 40% is in the territory of the MSME share of exports, not of GDP.

common_traps: Share of GDP, share of manufacturing output and share of exports are three different MSME numbers; a candidate who has memorised the export share will reach for 40%.
key_note: The MSME Ministry's table gives roughly 30.5% for 2018-19, which the key rounds to 30%. That rounding is what leaves 31% looking defensible, so the exact reported figure is worth checking against the annual report.

topic_name: School education schemes and curriculum frameworks
short_explanation: SARTHAQ is the Education Ministry's implementation plan for school education under the National Education Policy 2020, mapping the policy's recommendations to specific tasks, timelines and responsible agencies.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The plan sits with the Department of School Education and Literacy; it carries no finance-sector mandate.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Nothing in SARTHAQ concerns horticulture — the name unpacks to students' and teachers' advancement through quality education.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: SARTHAQ has no connection with securities markets.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The scheme is an education-sector implementation plan, not an insurance programme.

short_explanation: Minimum Support Price is announced for 22 mandated crops — 14 kharif, 6 rabi and 2 commercial — on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
explanation_text: The 14 kharif crops are paddy, jowar, bajra, maize, ragi, tur, moong, urad, groundnut, soyabean, sunflower, sesamum, nigerseed and cotton. The 6 rabi crops are wheat, barley, gram, masur, rapeseed-mustard and safflower. The 2 commercial crops are copra and raw jute. CACP recommends the prices, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approves them, and since 2018-19 the declared policy is to fix MSP at not less than 1.5 times the A2+FL cost of production.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 12, 5 and 4 adds to 21 and splits the list wrongly; the kharif group alone has 14 crops.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 16, 7 and 5 inflates every group — there are 22 mandated crops in all, not 28.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 18, 8 and 4 would make 30 crops, well beyond the mandated list.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Sugarcane is not one of the 22. It receives a Fair and Remunerative Price under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, which is a different instrument from MSP.

short_explanation: Section 10 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 establishes the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters affecting the rights of consumers as a class.
explanation_text: CCPA is the enforcement arm the 1986 Act never had. It can act on a complaint or on its own motion, order the recall of unsafe goods, order refunds and the discontinuation of unfair trade practices, and impose penalties for misleading advertisements — up to ₹10 lakh and two years for a first offence, and up to ₹50 lakh and five years on repetition, with power to bar an endorser from making endorsements for one to three years. Individual buyer-seller disputes still go to the District, State and National Consumer Commissions; CCPA deals with class-wide harm.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Section 9 precedes the establishing provision and does not create the Authority.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Section 11 deals with the Authority's composition and the terms of its members, not with bringing it into existence.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Section 12 concerns how the Authority is to function rather than its establishment.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Section 15 deals with the Authority's Investigation Wing under a Director General, which exists only because Section 10 has already created the Authority.

short_explanation: The All India Survey on Higher Education for 2019-20 reports a gross enrolment ratio of about 23 for Scheduled Caste students in the 18-23 age group, against 27.1 for all students.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 22.2 sits below the range the survey reports for Scheduled Caste enrolment in this round.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 23.4 is the closest rival and appears in some readings of the same report; the key takes 23.2.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 24.2 overstates Scheduled Caste enrolment, which stays roughly four points under the all-student ratio of 27.1.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 25.12 is close to neither the Scheduled Caste ratio nor the all-student ratio for 2019-20.

key_note: AISHE 2019-20 gives an all-India GER of 27.1, with Scheduled Castes around 23 and Scheduled Tribes around 18. Whether the Scheduled Caste figure in the published table is 23.2 or 23.4 could not be settled from subject knowledge and should be verified against the report before this explanation is released.

topic_name: Monetary policy framework and inflation targeting
short_explanation: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework the consumer price inflation target is 4% with a tolerance band of two percentage points either side, so the upper limit is 6%.
explanation_text: The target was notified by the central government in consultation with the RBI in 2016 and renewed on the same terms for April 2021 to March 2026. It is set on headline CPI (Combined), not on core inflation or WPI. The Monetary Policy Committee is treated as having failed to meet the target if average inflation stays outside the 2-6% band for three consecutive quarters, and on failure the RBI must report to the government stating the reasons, the remedial action it proposes and the time it expects to need to return inside the band.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 4% is the central target itself, not the outer edge of the tolerance band.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 4.5% appears nowhere in the framework; the band is defined as 4% plus or minus 2 percentage points.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 5% lies inside the band rather than at its ceiling.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The target (4%) and the upper tolerance limit (6%) are different numbers; a question asking for the 'highest band' wants the tolerance ceiling.

topic_name: Life and accident insurance schemes for the poor
short_explanation: The annual premium under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana was revised from ₹12 to ₹20 with effect from 1 June 2022 — the first change since the scheme started in 2015.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ₹15 was not notified at any stage; the revision went straight from ₹12 to ₹20.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹18 is a plausible-looking intermediate rate, but no such premium was fixed.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹19 belongs to no notification under the scheme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: ₹25 overshoots the revised rate of ₹20; the larger jump that year was in PMJJBY, whose premium moved from ₹330 to ₹436.

key_note: PMSBY covers accidental death and total disability for ₹2 lakh and partial disability for ₹1 lakh, for bank or post-office account holders aged 18 to 70, with the premium auto-debited each year in May.

short_explanation: Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 runs through the Anganwadi network, whose supplementary nutrition entitlement covers children up to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers as a universal group; the key treats adolescent girls of the north-east as the category outside that core list.
explanation_text: POSHAN 2.0 merges three earlier programmes from 2021-22 — the Anganwadi Services scheme, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls — under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, with a single supply chain, a common nutrition norm and the Poshan Tracker for monitoring. Children of 0-6 years, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled everywhere the Anganwadi network reaches. Adolescent girls enter only through the Scheme for Adolescent Girls component, which is restricted by age to 14-18 years and by geography to notified areas, and that restriction is what this question turns on.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Children from birth to six years are the central beneficiary group of Anganwadi Services under POSHAN 2.0.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pregnant women receive supplementary nutrition, health check-ups and counselling under the scheme.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Lactating mothers are covered on the same footing as pregnant women.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This would be the answer only if every group listed were an unqualified beneficiary; the key rests on the adolescent-girl component being restricted rather than universal.

common_traps: The stem asks which group is NOT eligible. Three of the four named groups are plainly covered, so the question is really about which category carries a restriction.
key_note: The competing reading is strong. The Scheme for Adolescent Girls inside Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 expressly covers girls of 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern states, which would make option E the better answer. The scheme guidelines should be checked before this row is published.

short_explanation: Net direct tax collection for 2021-22 came to about ₹14.1 lakh crore, comfortably above the revised estimate for the year.
explanation_text: Two figures circulate for the same year and they are not interchangeable. Gross direct tax collection in 2021-22 was roughly ₹16.3 lakh crore; after refunds of about ₹2.2 lakh crore the net figure is about ₹14.1 lakh crore, and it is the net figure that enters the government's receipts. 'Direct taxes' here means corporation tax plus personal income tax, including the securities transaction tax; GST, customs and excise are indirect taxes and are counted on a separate line.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ₹10 lakh crore is below even the budget estimate for direct taxes that year, which was about ₹11 lakh crore.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹12 lakh crore is close to the revised estimate for 2021-22, not to the actual net collection of about ₹14.1 lakh crore.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹13 lakh crore falls between the revised estimate and the actual; the collection reported was about ₹14.1 lakh crore.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: ₹16 lakh crore is the gross collection before refunds — the net collection, which is what is reported as the year's take, is about ₹14.1 lakh crore.

common_traps: Gross collection and net collection differ by the refunds issued — roughly ₹2.2 lakh crore in 2021-22 — so both ₹16 lakh crore and ₹14 lakh crore can be found in press reports of the same year.

short_explanation: Tamil Nadu headed the larger-state group in the fourth State Food Safety Index, released by FSSAI in June 2022 for 2021-22.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Kerala ranks among the better performers but did not lead the fourth edition of the index.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Gujarat topped the earlier editions of the index and came second in this one, which is exactly what makes it the tempting answer.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Andhra Pradesh does not lead the larger-state ranking in this edition.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Gujarat was the repeat topper of the earlier editions; the fourth index is the one where Tamil Nadu moved to the top, so the year matters.
key_note: The index scores states on five parameters — human resources and institutional data, compliance, food testing infrastructure, training and capacity building, and consumer empowerment — and ranks large states, small states and union territories in separate groups.

short_explanation: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides LPG connections to women from poor households and carries no age condition, so it is the one scheme here that is not aimed at senior citizens.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana supplies assisted-living devices free of cost to senior citizens from BPL households.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The National Social Assistance Programme includes the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme for people aged 60 and above.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana is a pension policy sold to people aged 60 and above.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The stem asks which scheme is NOT for senior citizens; three of the four options are old-age schemes, so a hurried reader who matches on 'Pradhan Mantri' can pick the wrong one.

topic_name: Life and accident insurance schemes for the poor
short_explanation: Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana is a pension plan for people aged 60 and above and is operated by the Life Insurance Corporation alone.
explanation_text: PMVVY pays a fixed return — 7.4% a year for policies bought in the 2020-22 window — over a ten-year term, with pension payable monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly as the subscriber chooses. The maximum purchase price per senior citizen is ₹15 lakh. Because the assured return is held above prevailing market rates, the government meets the difference as a subsidy to LIC, and that fiscal backing is precisely why the scheme is sold exclusively through LIC rather than through insurers generally.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: PM Ujjwala Yojana is run by the oil marketing companies under the Petroleum Ministry, not by an insurer.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: PM Samarth is a skilling scheme in the textiles sector, with no insurance element.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: PM Gram Adarsh Yojana is a village-development scheme for SC-majority villages under the Social Justice Ministry.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

topic_name: Clean cooking fuel and energy access schemes
short_explanation: From May 2022 Ujjwala beneficiaries receive a targeted subsidy of ₹200 on each 14.2 kg cylinder for up to 12 refills in a year, credited to their bank account.
explanation_text: The subsidy is transferred rather than netted off at the counter: the consumer pays the market price to the distributor and the amount is credited by direct benefit transfer, which keeps the payment traceable to the beneficiary. It is restricted to PMUY households — other LPG consumers buy at market price — and the ceiling of 12 refills a year is what bounds the fiscal outgo. The scheme itself, launched in 2016 under the Petroleum Ministry, gives a deposit-free connection with the first refill and stove support.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹300 per cylinder is the rate set by a later revision, not the one in force when this paper was set.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹350 with 10 refills misstates both halves: the rate was ₹200 and the annual cap 12 cylinders.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹400 doubles the notified per-cylinder subsidy, though the 12-refill cap in this option is right.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The per-cylinder subsidy was later raised to ₹300; ₹200 is the figure correct for 2022, so this row should be read with its year attached.

topic_name: National Social Assistance Programme and family benefits
short_explanation: The National Family Benefit Scheme pays a one-time lump sum to a poor household when its primary breadwinner dies, whatever the cause of death.
explanation_text: NFBS is one of the five components of the National Social Assistance Programme, alongside the old-age, widow and disability pensions and the Annapurna scheme, and it is administered by the Rural Development Ministry. It applies to BPL households where the breadwinner — the member whose earnings largely supported the family — dies between the ages of 18 and 59, and the grant goes to the surviving head of the household. The amount was ₹10,000 when the scheme began and was later raised to ₹20,000, which is why the figure in this stem reads low.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is a contributory life cover of ₹2 lakh for which the member pays an annual premium; it is insurance, not a family-benefit grant.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana pays only on accidental death or disability, so it cannot answer a stem that says 'irrespective of the cause of death'.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is a financial-inclusion scheme for opening bank accounts; any cover under it rides on the RuPay card rather than being a death grant.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The ₹10,000 in the stem is the original NFBS amount; the benefit now stands at ₹20,000, so the scheme name is right even though the figure is dated.

short_explanation: MFIN's Micrometer for the fourth quarter of 2021-22 ranks Tamil Nadu first by microfinance portfolio, with Bihar second and West Bengal third.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Gujarat is not in the leading group on portfolio size; Bihar holds second place in this quarter.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Kerala and Uttarakhand are small microfinance markets and do not appear near the top of the ranking.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Tamil Nadu is the state the question has already set aside as first, so it cannot also be second.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: Micrometer ranks states by gross loan portfolio across all lender types, and the order shifts between quarters, so this ranking belongs to Q4 of 2021-22 specifically.

short_explanation: The World Bank approved a $250 million programme in 2022 to help India reduce deaths and injuries from road crashes, working through a group of seven states.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: $150 million is well short of the approved amount of $250 million.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: $175 million corresponds to no tranche of this operation; the approval was for $250 million.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: $200 million is the nearest round figure below the approval, but the sanctioned amount is $250 million.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: $255 million is a near-miss on the round figure; the approved amount is exactly $250 million.

key_note: The programme supports state road-safety agencies, safer corridors, enforcement and post-crash trauma care, and is results-based rather than a straight construction loan.

topic_name: Census and demographic profile of India
short_explanation: Census 2011 counts cultivators and agricultural labourers together at 54.6% — that is 54.6% of India's workers, not of its whole population.
explanation_text: The census records about 118.6 million cultivators and 144.3 million agricultural labourers out of roughly 481 million workers. Set that against agriculture's share of gross value added, which runs around 17-18%: more than half the workforce produces under a fifth of the output, and that gap is the standard way the low productivity of Indian agriculture is stated. The share of the total population engaged in agriculture is much lower, because children, students, homemakers and the elderly all sit in that denominator.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 50.3% understates the census count of cultivators plus agricultural labourers.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 51.5% is below the reported share; the two farm categories together make 54.6% of workers.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 56.4% overstates it — the census figure is 54.6%, and the higher number is closer to the rural share of the workforce than to the agricultural share.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The stem says 'total population' but the 54.6% figure is a share of total workers. Read it as the workforce share, which is how the census reports it.
key_note: The stem's wording is loose: 54.6% is the share of main and marginal workers engaged in cultivation and agricultural labour, not of the population.

topic_name: Census and demographic profile of India
short_explanation: Census 2011 places 68.84% of India's population in rural areas — about 83.3 crore people out of roughly 121 crore.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 45.23% is far below the census share; the rural population is more than two-thirds of the total.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 49.33% would make India half urban, which the 2011 census does not show.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 55.35% still understates the rural share of 68.84%.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 69.45% is close enough to survive a quick glance, but the census figure is 68.84%.

common_traps: 68.84% and 69.45% differ by only half a point; the census number to carry is 68.84% rural against 31.16% urban.

short_explanation: The International Financial Services Centres Authority is the single regulator for financial products in the GIFT City IFSC, and its Fund Management Regulations of 2022 brought angel schemes and accredited angel investors within its rules — the reading this key takes.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: SEBI regulates angel funds in the domestic market as a sub-category of Category I Alternative Investment Funds; it is excluded here only on the narrow IFSC reading of the question.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: RBI's writ covers banks, NBFCs and foreign-exchange rules, not the registration of angel funds.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: There is no regulator called the Department of Finance; the Department of Economic Affairs frames policy but does not register or supervise funds.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: This key is doubtful. Angel funds in India are registered and regulated by SEBI under Chapter III-A of the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, with IFSCA covering only vehicles set up inside the IFSC. Unless the question is read as being about GIFT City, SEBI is the better answer, and the official key should be verified before publication.

short_explanation: Women accounted for about 54.5% of the person-days generated under MGNREGA in 2021-22, far above the one-third share the Act requires.
explanation_text: Section 6 read with Schedule II of the Act reserves at least a third of the work for women and requires equal wages for men and women. Actual participation has stayed above half for several years, helped by work being offered within five kilometres of the village, by crèche and shade provisions at the worksite, and by the absence of the travel and entry barriers that keep women out of other wage work. The share is measured in person-days of employment generated, not in the number of job cards issued.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 45.6% is below the level women's participation has held for several years running.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 50.9% is plausible in shape but under the reported figure of 54.54% for 2021-22.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 57.60% overstates the year; participation has stayed in the mid-fifties rather than approaching sixty.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: One-third is the statutory minimum, not the achieved share. A question asking what women's participation 'remains at' wants the actual figure.

topic_name: Life and accident insurance schemes for the poor
short_explanation: The annual premium for the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana rose from ₹330 to ₹436 with effect from 1 June 2022.
explanation_text: PMJJBY is a one-year renewable term cover of ₹2 lakh for bank and post-office account holders aged 18 to 50, continuing until 55, with the premium auto-debited each May. The revised rate works out to about ₹1.25 per ₹1,000 of cover a year and was the first change since the scheme began in 2015; it was driven by claims experience, since claims under the scheme had run well above the premium collected. The companion accident cover PMSBY moved from ₹12 to ₹20 on the same date.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹440 is the nearest round number above the notified rate, but the premium is ₹436.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹450 overstates the revision; the rate fixed was ₹436.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹452 corresponds to no notification under the scheme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: ₹462 is well above the revised premium of ₹436.

short_explanation: SATAT is a compressed-biogas initiative run by the oil marketing companies under the Petroleum Ministry, so it is not one of the schemes folded into PM Virasat ka Samvardhan.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Seekho aur Kamao is the Minority Affairs Ministry's skill-development scheme for minority youth and is one of the components merged into PM VIKAS.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: USTTAD upgrades the skills of traditional artisans and craftspeople from minority communities and is part of the merged scheme.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Hamari Dharohar supports the preservation of the cultural heritage of minority communities and is a PM VIKAS component.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Nai Roshni trains minority women in leadership and Nai Manzil combines schooling with skilling for dropouts; both are inside PM VIKAS.

common_traps: The stem asks which is NOT a component. Four options are Minority Affairs Ministry schemes; the odd one belongs to the energy sector.

short_explanation: The Union Budget for 2021-22 raised the corpus of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund from ₹30,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore.
explanation_text: RIDF is held with NABARD and is funded from the shortfalls banks run against their priority-sector lending targets — the deficient amount is deposited into the fund instead of being lent directly. NABARD then on-lends it to state governments and state-owned corporations for rural infrastructure: minor irrigation, rural roads and bridges, drinking water supply, watershed development and soil conservation. Each year opens a fresh tranche, so the figure must always be quoted with its year.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹42,000 crore is above the enhanced corpus; the budget figure for 2021-22 is ₹40,000 crore.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹45,000 crore overstates the allocation by a quarter.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹46,000 crore is well past the announced corpus for the year.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

topic_name: Drinking water supply and Jal Jeevan Mission
short_explanation: Jal Jeevan Mission, launched in August 2019, set 2024 as the year by which every rural household should have a functional household tap connection.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2023 falls a year short of the deadline written into the mission.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2025 is past the mission's target year; it is the horizon used by other programmes such as Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2026 belongs to no Jal Jeevan Mission commitment.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2028 is four years beyond the stated target of 2024.

key_note: The mission is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, and the service standard is 55 litres per person per day of potable water at the household tap on a regular and long-term basis.

short_explanation: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was carved out of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in January 2006, to give minority welfare and development a dedicated ministry.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2004 precedes the separation; minority affairs were still handled within the Social Justice Ministry.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2005 is the year before the carve-out.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2007 is when the ministry's flagship pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes began, not when it was created.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2008 is two years after the ministry was set up.

short_explanation: Article 41 directs the state, within the limits of its economic capacity and development, to make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Article 42 provides for just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Article 45 originally required free and compulsory education up to the age of 14 and now provides for early childhood care and education for children below six.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Article 51 deals with the promotion of international peace and security.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Article 61 sets out the procedure for the impeachment of the President and is not a Directive Principle at all.

key_note: Article 41 is the Directive Principle usually cited as the constitutional anchor for employment guarantee and social assistance programmes such as MGNREGA and the National Social Assistance Programme, both of which are framed as economic-capacity-limited entitlements.

short_explanation: The Aspirational Districts Programme ranks districts on five themes — health and nutrition, education, agriculture and water resources, financial inclusion and skill development, and basic infrastructure. There is no separate 'banking system' theme.
explanation_text: NITI Aayog's composite score is weighted: health and nutrition 30%, education 30%, agriculture and water resources 20%, financial inclusion and skill development 10%, and basic infrastructure 10%, built from 49 indicators. Banking does appear in the scoring, but inside the financial-inclusion theme through indicators such as accounts opened under Jan Dhan and enrolment in the micro-insurance and pension schemes — which is exactly why this option looks plausible. The programme covers 112 districts and ranks them on incremental improvement rather than on their absolute level, so a poor district that improves fast can top the delta ranking.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Health and nutrition is a theme and carries the largest weight, 30%.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Agriculture and water resources is a theme, weighted 20%.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Financial inclusion and skill development is a theme, weighted 10% — and it is where banking indicators actually sit.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Basic infrastructure is the fifth theme, weighted 10%.

common_traps: The stem asks which is NOT a parameter, and the wrong option is not absurd: banking indicators exist inside the financial-inclusion theme, they simply are not a theme of their own.

topic_name: Crop production estimates and agricultural statistics
short_explanation: Under FASAL the India Meteorological Department in New Delhi produces the multiple in-season forecasts of crop yield, using agrometeorological and statistical models that read weather data against crop condition.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The Survey of India is the national mapping and surveying agency and has no crop-forecasting role.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Geological Survey of India works on geology and mineral resources, not on crop yields.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The Department of Agriculture runs the crop-estimation system and issues the advance estimates of production, but the repeated in-season yield forecasts under FASAL come from IMD.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: FASAL has two strands: the econometric and agrometeorological forecasts from IMD, and the remote-sensing based estimates from the Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre under the Agriculture Ministry. The stem asks for the agency generating the multiple seasonal yield forecasts, which is IMD.

short_explanation: The 2022-23 budget put about ₹19,000 crore against PMGSY, roughly 36% more than the ₹14,000 crore the scheme was revised to for 2021-22.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 30% understates the jump from about ₹14,000 crore to about ₹19,000 crore.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 32% is below the increase the two allocations imply.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 33% would correspond to a rise of a third, slightly less than the actual step-up.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 40% overstates it; a 40% rise on ₹14,000 crore would take the allocation to ₹19,600 crore.

key_note: The percentage depends on the base chosen: measured against the 2021-22 revised estimate of about ₹14,000 crore the increase is about 36%, while against the original budget estimate for that year it is smaller. The keyed figure uses the revised estimate.

short_explanation: The World Bank has supported PMGSY through a series of loans since the scheme's early years, and the key puts its cumulative investment at about $2.1 billion.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: $1.5 billion is below every cumulative figure the Bank quotes for its PMGSY lending.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: $2.5 billion is above the cumulative amount; the key takes $2.1 billion.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: $2.9 billion overstates the Bank's total commitment to the programme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The World Bank's own notes on PMGSY have more often cited roughly $1.8 billion of cumulative lending since 2004. The $2.1 billion figure could not be corroborated from subject knowledge and should be checked against the Bank's project page before this row is published.

topic_name: National family health surveys and health indicators
short_explanation: The fifth National Family Health Survey, covering 2019-21, reports about 70% of the population living in households with an improved sanitation facility, against roughly 49% in NFHS-4.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 65% is below the NFHS-5 reading; the survey records about 70%.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 60% would be a much smaller gain over the 49% of NFHS-4 than the survey shows.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 72% is the closest rival, but the figure reported is about 70%.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 78% overstates the improvement recorded between the two survey rounds.

topic_name: Irrigation, water resources and river linking
short_explanation: India's annual per capita water availability has fallen from about 5,177 cubic metres in 1951 to roughly a quarter of that today, a decline of about 75%.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 70% corresponds to an earlier end year, when availability was still around 1,545 cubic metres.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 72% sits between the readings for the 2010s and the early 2020s rather than matching the keyed figure.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 80% overstates the fall; even the projection for 2050, about 1,140 cubic metres, is a decline of a little under 80%.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 85% is beyond any of the published projections, including those for mid-century.

key_note: The standard pair of figures is 5,177 cubic metres per person in 1951 against about 1,486 in 2021 — roughly a 71% fall — with 1,341 projected for 2025, about 74%. The keyed 75% is a rounding of that range, so the source year behind it should be confirmed before publication.

topic_name: Pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers
short_explanation: The National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons assures ₹3,000 a month once the subscriber turns 60.
explanation_text: The scheme, also called the Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maandhan Yojana, is open to shopkeepers, retail traders and self-employed people aged 18 to 40 with annual turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, who are not income-tax payers and not already covered by EPFO, ESIC or NPS. The subscriber's monthly contribution is matched rupee for rupee by the central government, and the contribution rises with the age of entry, so joining late costs more. It is built on the same template as PM-SYM for unorganised workers and PM-KMY for small and marginal farmers, and all three assure ₹3,000 a month — one figure covers the set.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ₹2,500 is not the assured amount under any of the Maandhan pension schemes.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹4,000 exceeds the assured pension; the guarantee is ₹3,000 a month.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹1,500 is half the assured amount.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹2,000 falls short of the ₹3,000 guaranteed on attaining 60.

topic_name: Census and demographic profile of India
short_explanation: The sex ratio at birth recorded in the health management information system rose from 918 in 2014-15 to 937 in 2020-21, and that is the gain the government cites for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.
explanation_text: Three sex ratios get mixed up and they come from different sources. The overall sex ratio from Census 2011 is 943 females per 1,000 males. The sex ratio at birth from the Sample Registration System runs in the 900s and is published as a three-year average. The figure in this question is the sex ratio at birth from HMIS returns, reported by the Women and Child Development Ministry for the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao districts, and it is the series that moves from 918 to 937.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 914 is below the baseline the ministry reports for 2014-15.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 910 belongs to other rounds of the sex-ratio-at-birth series, not to the 2014-15 baseline.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 900 is well under the reported starting point of 918.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 909 is a plausible-looking sex ratio at birth but not the baseline year figure used here.

common_traps: Sex ratio at birth is not the overall sex ratio. Census 2011's 943 is the overall figure; the 918-to-937 movement is a birth-ratio series.

short_explanation: CMIE's Consumer Pyramids household survey put the rural labour force participation rate at about 40.9% over January to April 2022, a little above the all-India rate.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 30.45 is far below the rural reading and closer to urban participation in CMIE's series.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 38.6 is below the rural figure the key takes for this period.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 39.5 is near the all-India rate in some months of the period rather than the rural rate.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: CMIE's LFPR is a monthly series that moves by a point or more between months, so this figure should be tied to the exact release before publication. CMIE also measures participation on a different definition from the official Periodic Labour Force Survey, whose rural LFPR is substantially higher, so the two are not comparable.

topic_name: Pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers
short_explanation: The National Pension Scheme for Traders assures ₹3,000 a month from the age of 60, with the central government matching the subscriber's monthly contribution rupee for rupee.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ₹2,500 is not the guaranteed amount under this scheme.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹4,000 is above the assured pension of ₹3,000.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹1,500 is half the guaranteed monthly pension.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹2,000 falls short of the ₹3,000 assured on attaining 60.

key_note: This item repeats Q.155 of the same paper word for word, including the options, so both rows must carry the same answer.

short_explanation: Watershed management works on a drainage basin — conserving soil and moisture, moderating floods and sedimentation, and easing pressure on land, water and vegetation. Sewerage control is an urban sanitation function and does not belong to that set of objectives.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Controlling pollution in the catchment, especially from agricultural and surface runoff, is a standard watershed objective.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Reducing the over-exploitation of soil, water and vegetation is central to the watershed approach.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Water storage, flood moderation and checking sedimentation are the classic objectives of treating a watershed.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Improved vegetation cover and restored water bodies support wildlife, and habitat protection is listed among watershed objectives.

common_traps: The stem asks which is NOT an objective. Four options are genuine watershed goals, so the answer is the one that belongs to municipal sanitation rather than to catchment treatment.

short_explanation: On NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index the poorest states run Bihar first, Jharkhand second and Uttar Pradesh third.
explanation_text: The national MPI follows the Alkire-Foster method with twelve indicators across three dimensions — health (nutrition, child and adolescent mortality, maternal health), education (years of schooling, school attendance) and standard of living (cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, bank account). A household counts as multidimensionally poor if it is deprived in at least a third of the weighted indicators. The first national report was built on NFHS-4 data from 2015-16, so the ranking belongs to that round; Bihar had the highest headcount ratio, above half its population.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Madhya Pradesh comes fourth on this ranking, just behind Uttar Pradesh.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Karnataka sits well outside the poorest group on the index.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Uttarakhand has a far lower multidimensional poverty headcount than the states at the top of the list.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana pays ₹5,000 to a pregnant and lactating mother for her first living child; that is the total entitlement, released in instalments, rather than the size of each instalment.
explanation_text: The ₹5,000 came in three instalments — ₹1,000 on early registration of the pregnancy, ₹2,000 after at least one antenatal check-up, and ₹2,000 after the birth is registered and the child's first cycle of immunisation begins. Added to the roughly ₹1,000 a woman receives for an institutional delivery under the Janani Suraksha Yojana, the figure often quoted is about ₹6,000, which is where the neighbouring option comes from. The scheme is a maternity benefit meant to compensate partly for wage loss and to encourage institutional care; it was later restructured into fewer instalments under Mission Shakti.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ₹4,000 is neither the total entitlement nor any single instalment under the scheme.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹4,500 corresponds to no instalment structure the scheme has used.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹6,000 is PMMVY plus the Janani Suraksha Yojana incentive, not the PMMVY entitlement on its own.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: ₹6,500 exceeds even the combined figure that includes the institutional delivery incentive.

common_traps: The stem says 'in each instalment' but ₹5,000 is the total cash benefit; the instalments are ₹1,000, ₹2,000 and ₹2,000.
key_note: The stem is loosely drafted. ₹5,000 is the scheme's total cash benefit, so the question should be answered as asking for the PMMVY entitlement rather than for a single instalment.

short_explanation: RBI's Financial Inclusion Index is built from three sub-indices — Access, Usage and Quality — so all three of the listed items belong.
explanation_text: The three dimensions carry different weights: Access 35%, Usage 45% and Quality 20%, drawn together from 97 indicators. The index runs from 0 to 100, where 0 means complete exclusion and 100 full inclusion, and it is published annually for the year ending March. It has no base year — it is constructed afresh each year — so the level is what is read, not a growth rate. Quality is the dimension that captures financial literacy, consumer protection and inequalities in service, which is what separates this index from a simple count of accounts opened.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Access alone leaves out Usage and Quality, both of which are sub-indices.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Usage alone is the heaviest weighted dimension but not the whole index.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Quality alone is the smallest of the three dimensions and cannot stand for the index.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Access and Usage together still omit Quality, the dimension that carries literacy and consumer protection.

short_explanation: The National Career Service portal was launched in July 2015 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, linking jobseekers, employers, career counsellors and training providers on a single platform in place of the old employment-exchange model.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2016 is a year after the portal went live.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2017 postdates the launch by two years.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2018 is the period of the scheme's expansion through model career centres, not of its launch.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2019 is well after the portal was already operating.

topic_name: Tribal welfare and particularly vulnerable tribal groups
short_explanation: Seventy-five communities are notified as Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, spread across 18 states and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
explanation_text: The category grew out of the Dhebar Commission's work and was created during the fifth five-year plan, then renamed from Primitive Tribal Groups to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups in 2006 to drop the pejorative label. A group is identified on four criteria: a pre-agricultural level of technology, a stagnant or declining population, extremely low literacy, and a subsistence economy. Odisha has the largest number of such groups, and the Development of PVTGs scheme of the Tribal Affairs Ministry funds habitat-specific plans covering housing, health, education and livelihoods.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 70 falls short of the notified count of 75.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 73 is close but below the notified number.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 76 is one above the notified count.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 78 overstates the number of notified groups.

topic_name: Drinking water supply and Jal Jeevan Mission
short_explanation: Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 was launched in October 2021 for five years, running to 2025-26, with garbage-free cities as its stated goal.
explanation_text: The second phase moves past toilet construction, which was the focus of the first. It targets complete faecal sludge and septage management, wastewater treatment and reuse in cities, source segregation of waste, and the remediation of legacy dumpsites. It runs alongside AMRUT 2.0, which handles urban water supply and sewerage over the same period, and alongside the rural counterpart SBM-Grameen phase II, which works on solid and liquid waste management in villages.

option_rationales.label: A

topic_name: Production economics and factors of production
short_explanation: Drawing more output from each unit of land, labour or capital already in use - working the same factors harder - is agricultural intensification.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Diversification spreads production across more crops or enterprises; it changes the mix, not the output per unit of input.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Agri exclusivity is not a term in production economics.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The keyed rate of Rs 5,500 a quintal is the minimum support price announced for lentil (masur) for the rabi marketing season 2022-23, the rate current when this paper was set.
explanation_text: MSP is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices and approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, with rabi prices announced ahead of the sowing that feeds the following marketing season. Lentil has moved up steadily - roughly Rs 4,800 for RMS 2020-21, Rs 5,100 for RMS 2021-22 and Rs 5,500 for RMS 2022-23 - so the season label attached to a figure matters as much as the figure.

option_rationales.rationale: Rs 2,015 reads like a year rather than a price; no pulse has carried an MSP this low in recent years.

option_rationales.label: B

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 5,400 is a near-miss on the keyed figure and matches no announced lentil rate.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 4,500 sits below the lentil rate for any of the seasons in question.

Verify both against the CACP price policy statement before publication - the item may need its season label corrected rather than its key.

short_explanation: A young female buffalo that has not yet calved is a heifer calf: heifer marks the sex and the fact that she has never calved, calf marks her age.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Buffalo calf names the young animal without saying whether it is male or female.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Calf is broader still, fixing neither sex nor species.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Heifer is the near neighbour - it covers any female that has not yet calved, including a grown animal about to join the milking herd, so on its own it does not convey youth.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Heifer and heifer calf differ by age, not by sex; the young one is the heifer calf.
key_note: Option D is a reasonable competing reading, since a heifer is by definition a female that has not calved. The key takes the tighter sense in which 'young female' means the animal still at the calf stage.

short_explanation: Apna Khet Apna Kaam is Rajasthan's MGNREGA initiative under which works are taken up on the private land of small, marginal, SC, ST and BPL farmers, so a labourer earns his wage while improving his own holding.

option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: MGNREGA's Schedule I already permits works on the individual land of listed categories; states brand their versions differently, and Rajasthan's is Apna Khet Apna Kaam.

short_explanation: PM-KISAN pays Rs 6,000 a year to landholding farmer families in three four-monthly instalments of Rs 2,000, credited directly to the beneficiary's bank account.
explanation_text: The scheme was launched in February 2019 with effect from 1 December 2018, and was extended from small and marginal farmers to all landholding farmer families soon after. It is a central sector scheme, funded entirely by the Union, and payment runs through direct benefit transfer against land records and Aadhaar, so the state's role is verification rather than disbursal.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana is the contributory pension scheme paying Rs 3,000 a month after the age of 60, not an annual income transfer.

option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is crop insurance; it pays against assessed crop loss, not as a fixed yearly sum.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana funds irrigation and micro-irrigation works, not cash to farmers.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: PM-KISAN and PM-KMY sound alike: the first is the Rs 6,000 income transfer, the second the old-age pension.

short_explanation: A ewe carries her lambs for about 150 days, give or take five - roughly five months.
explanation_text: The farm-animal figures worth holding together: cow about 280 days, buffalo about 310, mare about 340, sow 114, and sheep and goat both about 150. Read them in groups - the small ruminants sit together at five months, the large ruminants at nine to eleven.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 280 plus or minus 3 days is the cow.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 310 plus or minus 5 days is the buffalo, about a month longer than the cow.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 180 plus or minus 2 days matches no farm species; it falls in the gap between the small and the large ruminants.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The release of the ovum from the mature Graafian follicle, when the follicle ruptures and the egg passes into the oviduct, is ovulation.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Post-oestrus names a period of the cycle, not the event of egg release.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Pro-oestrus is the build-up phase before heat, when the follicle is still growing.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Met-oestrus is the phase in which ovulation occurs in the cow, about 12 to 14 hours after standing heat ends, but it names the phase rather than the act.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Met-oestrus is when ovulation happens in cattle; the stem asks for the name of the event itself.
key_note: The stem is worded backwards - ovulation is release of the egg from the follicle, not separation of the follicle from the egg - but only one option names the event at all.

short_explanation: Agriculture Education Day is observed on 3 December, the birth anniversary of Dr Rajendra Prasad, India's first President, who also held the agriculture portfolio in the first Union cabinet.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: C.C. Singh is not a figure linked to this observance.

option_rationales.label: C

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

option_rationales.label: E

short_explanation: TRYSEM - Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment, launched in 1979 - gave rural youth from below-poverty-line families trade and skill training so that they could set up their own enterprise. It was a skill programme, not a provider of education facilities.
explanation_text: TRYSEM ran as a component of the Integrated Rural Development Programme, taking youth aged 18 to 35 from BPL households through trade training tied to a credit-and-subsidy package for starting the venture. In 1999 it was merged, along with IRDP and DWCRA, into the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana, which later became the National Rural Livelihoods Mission.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Women's empowerment was the mandate of DWCRA, Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas, a separate IRDP component.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: This is the defensible answer: TRYSEM's whole purpose was skill training for rural youth leading to self-employment.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: No health service delivery formed part of TRYSEM.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Rural housing ran through the Indira Awaas Yojana, and TRYSEM had no urban component at all.

key_note: The keyed option, education facilities, describes neither TRYSEM's design nor its delivery - it funded trade training with a credit and subsidy package, not schools or education infrastructure. Option B states exactly what the programme did and should be the key.

short_explanation: Agronomy is the field that covers crop production together with the management of the soil, water and inputs that carry the crop - tillage, irrigation, nutrients, weeds and protection chemicals.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Soil science studies the soil itself, its formation, chemistry and physics, without the crop-production side.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Entomology is the study of insects.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Pathology studies plant diseases and the organisms that cause them.

short_explanation: Organic farming is the production system that excludes synthetic fertilisers, pesticides, growth regulators, genetically modified organisms and livestock feed additives, relying instead on rotations, residues, manures, biofertilisers and biological pest control.
explanation_text: In India the standard is the National Programme for Organic Production, run by APEDA, which certifies through accredited agencies for export, while domestic and smallholder produce is certified under the Participatory Guarantee System. Public support runs mainly through the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana and, in the north-east, the Mission Organic Value Chain Development. The defining test is what the system excludes, not simply that manure is used.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Commercial farming describes production for the market at scale and says nothing about which inputs are permitted.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Extensive farming means low input per unit area spread over a large area - again a matter of intensity, not of input type.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; only one of the listed systems matches the definition.

short_explanation: The White Leghorn is the Italian breed here - the name is the anglicised form of Livorno - and it is the base of almost every commercial white-egg layer strain.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Plymouth Rock is an American dual-purpose breed.

option_rationales.label: B

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: This pairs the Leghorn with Aseel, an Indian game breed; it is not the name of any breed.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: New Hampshire is American, developed out of the Rhode Island Red.

short_explanation: Floriculture is the branch of ornamental horticulture dealing with flowers and foliage plants - their cultivation, marketing and arrangement.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Olericulture is vegetable growing.

option_rationales.label: C

short_explanation: Ripening is the set of changes - softening, colour break, sugar and aroma development - that turn a mature fruit into an edible one.
explanation_text: Maturity and ripening are not the same thing. A fruit is mature when it has reached the stage at which it can ripen properly after harvest; ripening is what follows, on the plant or off it. Climacteric fruits such as banana, mango and papaya show a respiration and ethylene surge, so they can be picked mature and ripened later; non-climacteric fruits such as grape and citrus will not ripen further once picked and must be harvested ripe.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Degreening only strips chlorophyll from the peel, usually with ethylene in citrus and banana; the colour changes but the flesh is not ripened.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Curing is the drying and wound healing given to onion, potato, ginger and turmeric before storage.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Ethylene is the hormone that triggers ripening, not the process itself.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Defreezing is not a post-harvest term.

short_explanation: Grape is raised commercially from rooted hardwood cuttings - dormant, pencil-thick canes of the previous season's growth, which strike roots readily in a nursery bed.
explanation_text: Because the vine roots so easily from cuttings, grafting is used only where the rootstock does a job the scion cannot: Dogridge and Salt Creek are used in peninsular India against nematodes, drought and salinity. Where no such stress exists, the own-rooted hardwood cutting is the cheapest route and true to type, which is why it is the standard method.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Epicotyl grafting is the mango method, done on a germinating seedling about a fortnight old.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Layering is used in guava, litchi and jasmine, where the shoot is rooted while still attached to the parent plant.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: T budding is used in rose, citrus and the stone fruits.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Veneer grafting is used in mango, sapota and cashew.

short_explanation: Oxytocin released when the calf suckles or the udder is prepared makes the myoepithelial cells around the alveoli contract, pushing milk down into the cistern - milk let-down.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Mammogenesis is the development of the gland, long before any milking.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Squeezing describes the milker's hand, not the physiological response.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Ejaculation has nothing to do with the mammary gland.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: Let-down lasts only about five to eight minutes after the oxytocin release, so milking must start promptly; fright releases adrenaline, which blocks the reflex. That is the practical reason for quiet handling at milking.

short_explanation: Mammogenesis is the growth and development of the mammary gland itself, which is completed before milk secretion begins.
explanation_text: Lactation runs in four steps. Mammogenesis builds the gland; lactogenesis starts milk secretion around calving; galactopoiesis keeps that secretion going through the lactation; and milk let-down, under oxytocin, moves milk from the alveoli to the cistern where it can be drawn. The first two are gland building and secretion starting, once per lactation; the last is a reflex repeated at every milking.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Lactation is the whole period of milk production, not the building of the gland.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Milking is the act of removing the milk.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Let-down is the oxytocin reflex that moves stored milk into the cistern.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Lactogenesis is the onset of milk secretion, which follows gland development.

topic_name: Plant nutrients, their functions and deficiency symptoms
short_explanation: Symptoms that begin on the lower, older leaves and work upward, with bronzing and scorching before the tissue dries, point to potassium deficiency.
explanation_text: Which leaves show the damage tells you whether the nutrient moves inside the plant. Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium are withdrawn from old leaves to feed new growth, so their deficiencies appear at the bottom and climb. Calcium, boron and iron move poorly, so their deficiencies show first in the youngest leaves and growing points. Within the mobile group, potassium is the one that scorches and bronzes the leaf margin.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Phosphorus deficiency does give purpling of older leaves and stems, but it stunts growth without the marginal scorching and bronzing described here.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole older leaf evenly, starting at the tip, rather than between the veins, and never bronzes it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; the symptom picture describes one nutrient.

common_traps: Damage on the lower leaves means a mobile nutrient - nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium or magnesium - never calcium, boron or iron.
key_note: The purple colour in the stem is more typical of phosphorus; the clues that decide for potassium are the bottom-to-top progression with bronzing and drying of the margins.

short_explanation: The Marine Products Export Development Authority, set up in 1972 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and headquartered at Kochi, is the nodal body for developing the seafood industry and regulating exports of marine products.
explanation_text: Separate the fisheries bodies by what they do. MPEDA develops and regulates marine exports - registration of processing plants and farms, quality control, and market promotion abroad. The National Fisheries Development Board, under the Department of Fisheries, funds and promotes production, aquaculture and infrastructure. APEDA, MPEDA's sibling under Commerce, handles agricultural and processed food exports and expressly leaves marine products to MPEDA.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: APEDA promotes exports of agricultural and processed foods; marine products are carved out of its mandate and given to MPEDA.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: NAFED is a cooperative marketing federation that procures pulses, oilseeds and onions within the country.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The National Fisheries Development Board promotes fisheries production and infrastructure, but export regulation is not its function.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: CRTRI is not a fisheries body; the nearest real names are research institutes such as CTRI for tobacco and CTCRI for tuber crops.

short_explanation: Cyprinus carpio, the common carp, is the exotic species that has adapted fully to Indian waters and is farmed here alongside the indigenous carps.
explanation_text: Composite fish culture stocks species that feed at different levels so that one pond yields more. Three are Indian major carps - catla at the surface, rohu in the middle column, mrigal on the bottom - and three are exotics: silver carp on phytoplankton, grass carp on aquatic weed, and common carp as a bottom-feeding omnivore. The exotics were brought in to fill feeding niches the Indian majors leave open.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Catla catla is an Indian major carp, native to the Gangetic system.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Labeo rohita, rohu, is likewise an Indian major carp.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Labeo calbasu is an indigenous minor carp of Indian rivers.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Osteobrama belangeri, the pengba, is native to Manipur and is the subject of conservation work, not an introduction.

short_explanation: A runner is a modified stem that creeps horizontally over the soil surface and roots at the nodes, giving a new plant at each - as in strawberry, doob grass and Oxalis.
explanation_text: Group the stem modifications by where they run. Creeping at or just above the surface: runner, stolon, offset and sucker, which differ in how far they travel and whether they start above or below the soil.
