Wholly underground: rhizome in ginger and turmeric, tuber in potato, corm in colocasia and bulb in onion. A runner mainly spreads the plant sideways; a rhizome mainly stores food and carries the plant through the off-season.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A sucker arises from the underground base of the stem and grows obliquely upward into a new shoot, as in banana and chrysanthemum.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: An offset is a short, thick runner of a single internode, found in aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and Pistia.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A rhizome is the underground horizontal stem; it fits the second half of the stem's wording but not the creeping on the ground.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; the four terms differ in position and structure and cannot all answer one definition.

common_traps: A runner creeps on the surface and a rhizome runs underground; the stem's wording blurs the two.
key_note: The phrase 'or below the ground' fits a rhizome better than a runner, so option D is a reasonable competing reading. The key takes 'grow horizontally' in the surface-creeping sense, which is the standard definition of a runner.

short_explanation: e-NAM, the National Agriculture Market, is the pan-India electronic portal that networks existing APMC mandis into a single national market for agricultural commodities.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: e-market is a generic phrase, not the name of a portal.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: E-kisan is not the national trading platform.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: E-mandi is used loosely for state-level mandi software, not for the national portal.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; only one of these names belongs to the pan-India portal.

short_explanation: An agrisilvipastoral system carries crops, forest trees and grazing animals on the same land - agri-silviculture combined with silvi-pasture.
explanation_text: Read the compound names part by part: agri is arable crops, silvi is forest trees, horti is fruit trees, and pastoral is pasture with grazing livestock. The name then tells you the components exactly, so agri-silviculture is crops with trees, silvipasture is trees with pasture, and agri-horti-silviculture is crops with both fruit and forest trees. Home gardens and the traditional hill systems are the familiar Indian examples of the multi-component form.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Agri-horti-pastoral puts fruit trees, not forest trees, with crops and grazing.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Agri-pastoral is crops with grazing animals and has no tree component at all.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Horti-pastoral is fruit trees with pasture and carries no arable crop.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Silvipasture is trees with pasture - half of the system described, with the crop missing.

topic_name: Soil physical properties and soil moisture
short_explanation: When the macropores have drained under gravity and water remains in the micropores, the soil stands at field capacity - the upper limit of water it holds against gravity, and the starting point for irrigation scheduling.
explanation_text: Fix the three landmarks by tension. Saturation is every pore full. Field capacity, at about one-third bar, is reached a day or two after rain or irrigation, once free drainage stops. The permanent wilting point, at about 15 bar, is where the plant can no longer pull water out. What lies between field capacity and wilting point is the available water, and irrigation is scheduled to refill it before a set share of it has been used.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Maximum retention capacity, or saturation, is when every pore including the macropores is full - the state right after heavy rain, before drainage.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Permanent wilting percentage is the lower limit, where the water left is held too tightly for the plant to use.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Hygroscopic water is the thin film held on particle surfaces at very high tension and is unavailable to plants.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Capillary water names the water held in the micropores, but that is a class of soil water rather than the condition of the soil the stem describes.

common_traps: Capillary water and field capacity refer to the same water; only field capacity names the soil's condition after drainage.

short_explanation: Census 2011 recorded 68.84 per cent of India's population as rural, about 83.3 crore people, against 31.16 per cent urban.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 62.17 per cent matches no census reading of the rural share.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 54.12 per cent would imply a near-even rural-urban split, which India has not reached.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 36.51 per cent is closer to the urban side of the split, and even there the recorded figure is 31.16 per cent.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

topic_name: Crop diseases and their causal agents
short_explanation: Gummosis is the citrus disease in which the bark cracks near the collar and amber gum oozes out; it is caused by Phytophthora attacking the trunk at or below the bud union.
explanation_text: Phytophthora nicotianae and P. citrophthora enter through wet, injured bark, so the disease follows deep planting, basin irrigation that wets the trunk, and poorly drained soil. Control is cultural first - bud high above the ground, keep irrigation water off the trunk, drain the orchard - and then curative: scrape out the lesion and paint it with Bordeaux paste, with a metalaxyl-based drench where infection is heavy.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Citrus canker is bacterial, caused by Xanthomonas, and shows raised corky lesions with a yellow halo on leaves, twigs and fruit rather than gum flow from the trunk.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Sooty mould is a black surface growth on the honeydew left by aphids and whitefly; it shades the leaf but does not damage bark.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Bacterial blast attacks petioles and twigs in cold, wet, windy weather and causes black lesions, not gumming.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Citrus scab produces warty, corky outgrowths on leaves and fruit.

topic_name: Agriculture's contribution to gross value added
short_explanation: The Economic Survey 2021-22 put agriculture and allied sectors at 18.8 per cent of Gross Value Added for 2021-22.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 7.9 per cent is far below any recent reading for the sector.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 15.5 per cent understates the Survey's figure.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 17.2 per cent is near the level the share had fallen to before the pandemic, not the 2021-22 reading.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 12.7 per cent matches no reported share for agriculture and allied sectors.

key_note: The same figure appears earlier in this paper (Q.7) and is keyed identically to 18.8 per cent.

short_explanation: Livestock's share in the Gross Value Added of agriculture and allied sectors rose from 24.32 per cent in 2014-15 to 28.63 per cent in 2018-19, measured at constant prices.
explanation_text: Read the figure as a share of agricultural GVA, not of the whole economy - livestock is roughly four per cent of total GVA. The share keeps climbing because milk, meat and egg output grow at seven to eight per cent a year while crop output grows slowly, and because livestock income is spread across small and landless households. That is why NABARD refinance and the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund lean towards the sector.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 24.34 per cent is a near-repeat of the 2014-15 starting figure and would mean almost no change over four years.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 25.26 per cent understates the rise.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 25.76 per cent likewise falls short of the reported 2018-19 share.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 27.82 per cent is the closest of the wrong values; the reported share is 28.63 per cent.

key_note: The pair of figures comes from the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying's reporting of livestock GVA at constant prices; check the edition before quoting the share in learner material.

short_explanation: Depreciation accrues with time whether or not the tractor turns a wheel, so it is a fixed cost; fuel, repairs and maintenance rise and fall with the hours worked and are variable.
explanation_text: In farm power economics the fixed costs are depreciation, interest on the money tied up in the machine, taxes, insurance and shelter. They are incurred even if the tractor stands idle all year, which is why low annual use makes a tractor expensive per hour. Variable costs are fuel and lubricants, repairs and maintenance, and the operator's wage. Break-even use is found by spreading the fixed cost over more hours until the cost per hour falls below the custom hire rate.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Maintenance - servicing, filters, greasing - is scheduled by hours run and so varies with use.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Fuel and oil are consumed only while the tractor works and are the clearest variable cost.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Repairs arise from wear, which accumulates with hours of operation.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: Some texts group the fixed costs under the mnemonic DIRTI and fold repairs into it; the standard tractor-economics split used here keeps repairs and maintenance with the use-dependent costs.

short_explanation: Biofertilisers are preparations of living microorganisms - nitrogen fixers, phosphate solubilisers and mycorrhizae - that raise nutrient availability in the soil and promote plant growth.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Chemical fertilisers supply nutrients directly as salts and contain no living organism.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Green manures are green plant biomass ploughed in; they add organic matter and nitrogen but are not a microbial inoculant.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Mulch crops cover the soil to conserve moisture and check weeds.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; only one of the listed inputs carries microorganisms.

key_note: The common ones worth naming: Rhizobium for legumes, Azotobacter and Azospirillum for cereals, blue-green algae and Azolla in rice, phosphate-solubilising bacteria, and mycorrhiza. They are living products, so shelf life and storage decide whether they work.

short_explanation: Sprinkler irrigation throws water through the air as a spray that lands like rainfall, so the field needs no levelling or bunding and undulating land can be irrigated as it lies.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Drip delivers water drop by drop at the root zone through emitters; nothing resembles rainfall and the surface between plants stays dry.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Flooding runs water over the levelled field surface and needs bunds and land shaping.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The ring basin is a small basin built around a fruit tree - a surface method, not a spray.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The check basin divides a level field into small bunded plots, which is the very bunding the stem says is avoided.

short_explanation: Bench terracing cuts a sloping field into a series of level steps and is the standard conservation measure for cultivated hill land on slopes up to about 33 per cent, beyond which it becomes too costly and the land is better put under trees or grass.
explanation_text: The measure is chosen by the slope. Up to about six per cent, contour farming and contour bunding are enough and the field stays in one plane. From roughly six to sixteen per cent, graded bunds carry excess runoff away at a safe grade in high-rainfall tracts. Above that and up to about 33 per cent the slope itself has to be reshaped, which is bench terracing. Past 33 per cent, cultivation gives way to horticulture, forestry or pasture.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Graded bunding lays bunds at a slight grade to dispose of runoff safely; it is a gentle-slope measure and does not reshape the land into steps.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Contour farming is the agronomic practice of ploughing, sowing and interculture along the contour. It suits gentle slopes and is what a terrace is built to carry, not the terrace itself.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Contour bunding raises earthen bunds along the contour on gentle slopes in low-rainfall areas; it conserves water rather than cutting steps.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Stone terracing uses loose stone walls where stones are plentiful - a local variant, not the measure defined by the 33 per cent limit.

common_traps: 'Along the contour' tempts contour farming; the slope ceiling of 33 per cent is the clue that fixes bench terracing.
key_note: Contour farming is a fair literal reading of 'along the contour of sloping land', but the 33 per cent ceiling is the textbook criterion for bench terracing, so the key is defensible.

short_explanation: A chicken egg hatches after about 21 days under the hen or in the incubator, and a broiler is a chicken — the 21 days is the incubation of the egg, not the rearing period of the bird.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 15 days is shorter than any poultry species; even quail, the quickest, need about 17-18 days.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 18 days is the day the eggs are shifted from the setter to the hatcher, not the day of hatch. It is the commonest wrong pick.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No common poultry bird hatches at 25 days; guinea fowl take about 26-28 and ducks 28.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 28 days is duck and turkey incubation — right number, wrong species.

common_traps: Day 18 is the setter-to-hatcher transfer, not the hatch.
Ducks and turkeys take 28 days; the option is there to pull you across species.

short_explanation: Jasmine is India's leading perfumery flower — its concrete and absolute are solvent-extracted for the fragrance trade and exported, mostly from Tamil Nadu.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Portulaca is a low bedding ornamental grown for colour; there is no fragrance industry behind it.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Michelia champaca does yield a perfumery oil, but it is a minor trade beside jasmine, which is the flower India actually produces and exports for perfume.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Marigold is grown for loose flowers and for xanthophyll pigment used in poultry feed, not for perfume.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The stem asks for a botanical name but every option is a common name; champa is a genuine, if much smaller, perfumery plant and is the nearest competing reading.

topic_name: Soil physical properties and soil moisture
short_explanation: Sandy soil is coarse-textured with wide pores, so water drains straight through and very little is held back for the crop — such fields need light but frequent irrigation.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Clay is a heavy soil with very high retention; the problem there is drainage and aeration, not frequent irrigation.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Silt holds water well and behaves as a medium to heavy soil.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Loam is the balanced soil — good retention with good drainage — and is not the light, droughty one the stem describes.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

topic_name: Soil physical properties and soil moisture
short_explanation: Hygroscopic water is the very thin film adsorbed so tightly onto the surface of soil colloids that roots cannot pull it away; it behaves almost like a solid and moves only as vapour.
explanation_text: Soil water is classified by how tightly it is held. Water above field capacity is gravitational and drains away within a day or two, taking nutrients with it. Between field capacity (about one-third atmosphere tension) and the permanent wilting point (about 15 atmospheres) sits capillary water, held in the pores — this is the part the crop actually uses. Below the wilting point, at roughly 31 atmospheres and beyond, what remains is hygroscopic water, unavailable to plants however long the root sits next to it.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Gravitational water is the free water above field capacity that drains out under gravity; it is the easiest water to lose, not the hardest.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Capillary water is held in the soil pores against gravity and is the fraction the crop draws on.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The permanent wilting point is a moisture level, not a form of held water — and at that point capillary water is only just exhausted.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Field capacity is also a moisture level, marking the water left after free drainage has stopped.

common_traps: Field capacity and PWP are moisture levels; the stem asks for a form of soil water.

topic_name: Crop diseases and their causal agents
short_explanation: Banana bunchy top virus is carried by the banana aphid, Pentalonia nigronervosa, which acquires it from an infected plant and then transmits it for the rest of its life.
explanation_text: Transmission is persistent and circulative: the aphid needs hours of feeding to pick the virus up, cannot pass it to its offspring, but once infective stays infective. The second route is planting material — suckers taken from a diseased mat carry the virus into a new field. That is why control is a package rather than a spray: use tissue-culture or certified clean suckers, rogue out infected plants root and corm after killing the aphids on them, and keep the aphid population down.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Thrips transmit tospoviruses — the bud necrosis and spotted wilt group — not BBTV.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Mites transmit a few rod-shaped cereal viruses; banana bunchy top is not among them.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Whitefly is the vector of the begomoviruses, the leaf curl and mosaic group.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Only the aphid transmits BBTV, so a combined option fails.

short_explanation: A broiler is a chicken bred and reared specifically for meat, marketed at about six weeks of age; a layer is kept for eggs.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Layers are egg-type birds, such as White Leghorn crosses, kept through a laying cycle of roughly a year.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Geese are a separate waterfowl species, not the name for a meat chicken.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Only the broiler fits the stem, so a combined option fails.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The substance described — the flower's natural perfume held together with plant waxes, albuminous matter and pigment — is a perfumery concrete, the solvent extract from which the absolute is later washed out. No option names it: the five choices are insect names belonging to a pest question.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A yellow spot beetle is an insect; it cannot be a wax-like flower extract.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Defoliator thrips is again an insect name and does not answer the stem.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Strictly the closest choice, since none of the named options is the concrete — but the paper keys the beetle, so this cannot be relied on either.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Cannot apply; the options are unrelated insect names and none answers the stem.

key_note: The option block here is identical to the grape defoliator question in the same paper (Q.193), so this row looks like a mis-paired stem rather than a hard question. Taken on its own, the stem's answer is 'concrete': solvent extraction of flowers yields the concrete (essential oil plus waxes, albumin and colouring matter), and alcohol washing of the concrete yields the absolute. Check against the original question paper before publication and repair either the stem or the options.

short_explanation: Criss-crossing alternates the sire breed from generation to generation — hybrid females are mated to males of one parent breed, their daughters to males of the other, and so on — which keeps hybrid vigour alive in the herd.
explanation_text: It is the simplest rotational crossbreeding system. Straight crossbreeding gives a burst of heterosis in the first generation and then loses it; criss-crossing holds roughly two-thirds of that heterosis permanently by never letting the female line settle into one breed. Extending the rotation to three breeds retains a little more. Contrast this with grading up or back-crossing, where the aim is the opposite: to move the herd steadily towards one breed's genotype.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Back-crossing mates the hybrid to one parent breed repeatedly, to recover that breed's genome; there is no alternation of sires.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A test cross mates an animal to a homozygous recessive to find out whether it carries a hidden recessive gene.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Out-crossing stays inside one breed, mating unrelated animals; no second breed enters.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

topic_name: Crop diseases and their causal agents
short_explanation: Damping off hits papaya in the nursery: seedlings rot at the collar, topple over and die in spreading patches. None of the five options describes that — they describe leaf and fruit spotting on grown plants.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Brown to black sunken spots on the fruit is anthracnose, a fruit and post-harvest disease, not a seedling one.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Water-soaked sunken spots on the fruit again describe anthracnose on ripening papaya.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Spot centres turning black and then pink as the fungus sporulates is the classic Colletotrichum description — pink spore masses are its signature.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This is the honest choice, since no option describes damping off, but the paper keys option A, so the row cannot be scored as drafted.

key_note: Damping off of papaya is caused by Pythium aphanidermatum, Phytophthora and Rhizoctonia in wet, crowded nursery beds, and shows as pre-emergence seed rot and post-emergence collar rot and toppling; it never affects mature leaves or fruit. The keyed option, symptoms on green leaves and green immature fruit, describes papaya black spot or powdery mildew. The stem or the option set is defective — verify against the original paper and repair before publication.

short_explanation: Out-crossing is mating within a single breed between animals that share no common ancestor for four to six generations — fresh blood, without leaving the breed.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Criss-crossing uses two or more breeds and alternates the sire breed each generation.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 'Inter-breeding' is not a defined mating system in animal breeding; the recognised term for the practice described is out-crossing.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A test cross mates an animal to a homozygous recessive to reveal whether it carries a recessive gene.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Back-crossing mates a hybrid back to one of its parent breeds, which is a crossbreeding method, not a within-breed one.

common_traps: Out-crossing and criss-crossing sound alike; the dividing line is whether a second breed is brought in.

short_explanation: Coconut is a palm with a single growing point and no cambium, so it cannot be budded, grafted or layered; it is raised only from seed nuts sown in a nursery.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Budding needs a cambium so that bud and stock can knit; a monocot palm has none.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Grafting fails for the same reason — there is no cambial layer to form a union.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Layering needs a branch that can be bent down and rooted; a coconut palm has no branches.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Climate-smart agriculture rests on three pillars: raising productivity and incomes, building resilience to climate shocks, and cutting or removing greenhouse gases where it is possible to do so. Read on the stem as printed, the option that falls outside CSA is FAO's organisation-wide vision of better nutrition, a better environment and a better life for all, which is a broader mandate rather than a CSA component.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Clarifying CSA terminology, its components and how to contextualise them by country is the stated purpose of FAO's CSA Sourcebook, so it sits inside the CSA programme.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: This is FAO's overall vision statement — the 'four betters' of its Strategic Framework — rather than a component of climate-smart agriculture; on the stem as printed it is the option that belongs outside.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Raising production while holding ecological sustainability is simply the productivity pillar stated in other words.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Ecosystem balance belongs to the resilience and environmental side of CSA.

key_note: The keyed option — increased productivity, enhanced resilience and reduced emissions — is the textbook definition of CSA's three pillars, so it cannot be the thing CSA 'does not include'. The item reads as an 'includes' stem with a stray 'not', in which case the key is right and the question is misprinted. Taken exactly as printed, option C is the only choice outside the CSA frame, which is what this draft proposes. Check against the official key before publication.

short_explanation: Strip cropping lays the field out as long narrow bands of alternating crops run across the slope, so that the close-growing strip slows the runoff and catches the soil washing down off the tilled strip above it.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 'Cereal cropping' names a crop group; it says nothing about strip layout or erosion control.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Mulching covers the surface with residue to check raindrop impact — a valuable practice, but not a strip layout.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A cover crop protects the whole field surface between main crops; it is not partitioned into alternating bands.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Sustainable agriculture is defined precisely by this test: meeting today's food and fibre needs without eroding the soil, water and genetic base that later generations will need.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Shifting cultivation clears and burns a patch, crops it until fertility falls, then moves on — the opposite of holding the resource base.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Natural farming is one specific low-input practice, zero-budget natural farming being the Indian example; the stem gives the broad definition, not a named practice.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Permaculture is a design philosophy for perennial, largely self-sustaining systems — again one approach inside the wider idea.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Sequential cropping grows two or more crops one after another on the same field in a year, the next crop going in only after the previous one is harvested — so intensification happens in time alone and the crops never compete.
explanation_text: Multiple cropping splits into two families. In sequential cropping the crops do not overlap: double, triple and quadruple cropping simply count how many are taken in the year. In intercropping they do overlap on the same ground, and the forms are named by the arrangement — mixed, row, strip and relay. Relay is the borderline case: the second crop is sown into the standing first crop, so for a few weeks the two share the field and do compete. The words to test in any stem are therefore 'after harvest' versus 'into the standing crop'.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: In relay cropping the second crop is sown into the standing first crop, so the two overlap and do compete for a while.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Multi-storey cropping stacks crops of different heights at the same time; competition in space is the whole point of it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Ratooning regrows the same crop from the stubble after harvest, so it is not a sequence of different crops.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Relay is the near neighbour — the give-away in the stem is that the succeeding crop goes in only after the preceding one is harvested.

topic_name: Plant nutrients, their functions and deficiency symptoms
short_explanation: Phosphorus shortage shows first on the older lower leaves as an abnormally dark green that turns purple or reddish along the margins — sugars pile up in the leaf and form anthocyanin pigment.
explanation_text: Phosphorus is mobile in the plant, so the plant strips it out of old leaves to feed the growing points: deficiency therefore appears at the bottom of the plant first, along with stunting, thin stems and delayed flowering and maturity. Cold, wet soils bring it on even where soil phosphorus is adequate, because uptake slows. The contrast to hold is with the other mobile nutrients — nitrogen gives uniform pale yellowing of old leaves, potassium gives brown scorch of the margins and tips of old leaves — and with the immobile ones such as calcium and boron, whose symptoms appear on the youngest tissue.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Potassium deficiency scorches the margins and tips of older leaves brown; it does not purple them.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Nitrogen deficiency turns older leaves uniformly pale green to yellow, with no purpling.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Calcium is immobile, so its deficiency strikes the growing points and young leaves — tip burn and hooked tips.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Boron deficiency also shows at the growing point: hollow stem, brown heart, death of the terminal bud.

common_traps: Purpling on the lower leaves is phosphorus; marginal scorch on the lower leaves is potassium.

short_explanation: A method demonstration shows a group how to perform a skill — laying a nursery bed, treating seed with a fungicide, sowing — with the learners watching the steps and then doing them.
explanation_text: The two are easy to separate once the purpose is clear. A method demonstration teaches a skill: it is short, can be held any time, is done by the extension worker before a group, and the test of success is that the farmers can now do it. A result demonstration proves that a practice pays: it runs a full season on a farmer's own field, with a control plot alongside for comparison, and the test of success is that neighbours are convinced enough to adopt. Method teaches the hand; result convinces the mind.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A result demonstration runs a whole season on a farmer's field against a control plot to prove a practice pays; it convinces rather than teaches a skill.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The National Demonstration is a result-type demonstration laid out by scientists on cultivators' fields to show the yield potential of new technology.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Only the method demonstration matches the stem, so a combined option fails.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Teak is Tectona grandis, the premier timber of central and peninsular India, valued for its natural durability and resistance to termites.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Grevillea robusta is silver oak, the shade tree of coffee plantations.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Casuarina equisetifolia is the coastal shelterbelt and pulpwood tree.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Ailanthus is ardu, a fast-growing fodder and matchwood tree.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Terminalia arjuna is arjun, the tasar silkworm host with medicinal bark.

short_explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, launched in 2020 with an outlay of about Rs 20,050 crore, is the fisheries flagship — it targets 22 million tonnes of fish production by 2024-25 and aims to double fish farmers' incomes.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: PM-KISAN is the income support scheme paying Rs 6,000 a year to landholding farmer families.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: PMFBY is the crop insurance scheme.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No fisheries scheme of this name exists; the label echoes the old PMRY self-employment programme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: PMKSY is the irrigation umbrella — Har Khet Ko Pani and per drop more crop — and the acronym is also used for the Kisan Sampada food processing scheme; neither is fisheries.

topic_name: Crop diseases and their causal agents
short_explanation: A whitish-grey powdery coating on the upper leaf surface and on the fruit of grape and rose is powdery mildew — the fungus grows on the surface of the tissue and its dusty spore chains give the coating its look.
explanation_text: The two mildews are separated by where the growth sits and what weather brings it. Powdery mildew of grape (Erysiphe necator, older name Uncinula necator) and of rose (Podosphaera pannosa) grows superficially, mostly on the upper surface, thrives in warm dry weather with humid nights and needs no free water, and is controlled with sulphur or a triazole. Downy mildew of grape (Plasmopara viticola) grows inside the leaf, shows as oily yellow patches on the upper surface with a white downy growth confined to the underside, needs rain or leaf wetness to infect, and is controlled with copper, as in Bordeaux mixture.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: This is precisely the disease the stem describes — superficial whitish-grey powder on the upper surface of grape and rose — and it is the answer this draft proposes.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Anthracnose makes sunken dark spots with raised margins, the bird's-eye spot of grape, not a powdery film.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Collar rot attacks the stem at soil level and girdles it; it is not a foliar coating.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A correct answer is present among the choices.

key_note: The keyed option, downy mildew, contradicts its own stem. Downy mildew never gives a powdery coating on the upper surface: it gives oil spots above and a white downy fungal growth on the lower surface only. Every phrase in the stem — whitish-grey powdery coating, chlorotic spots on the upper leaf surface becoming whitish lesions, grape and rose — is the standard textbook description of powdery mildew. The spellings in the options ('Downey', 'Powdery') suggest the two were simply transposed. Publish only after the official key has been checked.

short_explanation: A sucker is a shoot that arises from the base of the main stem, at or below ground level, and can be lifted with its own roots and planted — banana is propagated this way.
explanation_text: The underground and basal structures used in propagation are worth keeping apart. A sucker rises from the base of the main stem or from the root system. An offset is a short, thickened lateral shoot from a rosette or bulb, as in date palm and pineapple. A runner creeps along the soil surface and roots at the nodes, as in strawberry and mint. A rhizome is a horizontal underground stem, as in ginger, turmeric and banana's own corm. A tuber is a swollen underground stem carrying eyes, as in potato.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: An offset is a short, thickened lateral from a rosette or bulb — the date palm and pineapple type — rather than a shoot from the base of a main stem.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A rhizome is a horizontal underground stem, as in ginger and turmeric.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A runner creeps along the soil surface and roots where its nodes touch down, as in strawberry.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A tuber is a swollen underground stem with eyes, as in potato.

common_traps: Offset and sucker are the closest pair: the sucker comes from the base of a main stem, the offset from a rosette or bulb.

short_explanation: Pollen reaching the stigma of the same flower, of another flower on the same plant, or of a plant of the same clone is self-pollination — genetically all of these are the same individual.
explanation_text: Within selfing, transfer inside one flower is autogamy and transfer between two flowers of the same plant is geitonogamy; transfer between different plants is xenogamy, that is cross-pollination. A clone is a vegetatively multiplied copy of one plant, so pollen moving between two plants of the same clone is still selfing even though two separate plants are involved — this matters in orchard planning, where a block of one clonal variety may set no fruit without a pollinizer. Cleistogamy, where the flower never opens, enforces selfing absolutely, as in wheat and groundnut.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Cross-pollination requires pollen from a genetically different plant of the same species.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 'Mixed pollination' is not a recognised category.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 'Often cross-pollinated' describes a crop's habit — roughly 5 to 30 per cent natural outcrossing, as in cotton and sorghum — not a single act of pollen transfer.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Valentine's Day, 14 February, is the single largest day for cut-rose sales in the world and sets the annual peak for Indian rose growers and exporters.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Rose Day, 7 February, opens Valentine's week and does lift sales, but the peak falls on the 14th.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Mother's Day is a large flower day, but carnations and mixed bouquets dominate it and the volume stays below Valentine's.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Father's Day is a minor occasion for cut flowers.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Christmas demand runs to poinsettia, foliage and wreaths rather than cut roses.

short_explanation: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices recommends the minimum support prices; the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs then approves them and the Ministry announces them.
explanation_text: CACP was set up in 1965 (as the Agricultural Prices Commission) and is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, advisory in character — its recommendations do not bind the government. It covers 22 mandated crops of the kharif and rabi seasons plus the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane, and builds its recommendation on cost concepts: A2 is paid-out cost, A2+FL adds imputed family labour, and C2 adds the rental value of owned land and interest on owned capital. Since 2018-19 the announced MSPs have been set at a minimum of one and a half times A2+FL.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ICAR runs agricultural research and education; it has no price-fixing role.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Ministry houses CACP and processes and announces the decision, but the recommendation itself comes from the Commission.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The Department administers procurement and the price support operations; it does not make the price recommendation.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Recommend, approve and announce are three different steps: CACP recommends, the CCEA approves, the Ministry announces.

short_explanation: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and issues the instructions the rest of the cell follows, so growth and development are directed from there.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The cytoplasm is the medium the organelles sit in and where many reactions run; it does not carry the genetic instructions.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Ribosomes assemble proteins, but to the instructions the nucleus sends out to them.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Mitochondria supply the ATP that powers growth; they provide the energy, not the control.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The stem is loosely worded — every organelle contributes to growth in some way. The point being tested is that the nucleus carries the genetic material and controls cell activity.

short_explanation: Ram lambs are normally castrated between two and four weeks of age — late enough for the testes to be clearly descended, early enough that the setback to growth and the risk of bleeding stay small.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Rubber-ring castration is sometimes done in the first week, but the standard recommendation for ram lambs sits a little later, once the testes are properly down.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Close to the window but earlier than the usual recommendation; this is the commonest near-miss on this item.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Castration this late means more pain, more bleeding and a larger check to growth.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: By this age the ram is approaching puberty and castration becomes a surgical risk best avoided.

common_traps: Option B sits just outside the keyed window — read the whole range, not the first number.
key_note: Recommended windows differ by method and by text: elastrator rings are often applied in the first week, while Burdizzo or open surgical castration is put at two to four weeks. The keyed two to four weeks is the standard Indian sheep-husbandry figure, but if the course reference uses one to two weeks this item should be checked against it.

short_explanation: The minimum support price for tur (arhar) in the 2022-23 kharif marketing season was Rs 6,600 a quintal, Rs 300 above the Rs 6,300 of the previous season.
explanation_text: MSP is the floor the government commits to buy at, recommended by CACP and approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs before the sowing season, so that farmers know the price when they decide what to plant. For kharif 2022-23 the largest absolute increases went to the pulses and oilseeds the country imports — sesamum and moong took the biggest raises — as part of the push to lift domestic pulse and oilseed output. Urad was set at the same Rs 6,600 as tur that season.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: No pulse MSP announced for that season reads Rs 6,760; tur was Rs 6,600.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 6,380 is not a tur figure; it sits near the previous season's Rs 6,300 without matching it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary — no tur MSP reads Rs 6,570, and the announced figure is Rs 6,600.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 6,200 is below even the 2021-22 tur MSP of Rs 6,300, and MSPs were not cut.

common_traps: Fix the season before the figure: tur was Rs 6,300 in 2021-22, Rs 6,600 in 2022-23 and Rs 7,000 in 2023-24.

short_explanation: The Krishi Vigyan Kendra is the district-level farm science centre inside the national agricultural research system; its job is to assess and refine technology for local conditions and demonstrate it on farmers' fields.
explanation_text: The first KVK was set up at Puducherry in 1974 on the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee's recommendation. KVKs are funded entirely by ICAR and supervised through the Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes, and are hosted by state agricultural universities, ICAR institutes, NGOs and state departments. Four mandates define them: on-farm testing to assess the location-specificity of a technology, frontline demonstrations to establish its production potential, capacity building of farmers and extension staff, and working as a knowledge and resource centre for the district.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ATMA is the district extension-reform body under the Department of Agriculture; it coordinates extension delivery rather than sitting inside the research system.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: An ATIC is the single-window information, diagnostic and input counter at a research institute or agricultural university.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Neither ATMA nor ATIC carries the technology assessment and refinement mandate, so a combined option fails.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Pond water for fish culture must stay on the neutral to mildly alkaline side; of the ranges offered, only 6.5 to 10 covers the productive band, and the working optimum is about 7.5 to 8.5.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Strongly acid water — below about 4.5 is the acid death range for fish.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Strongly alkaline; above about 11 is the alkaline death range.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Still acid enough to stop reproduction and slow growth badly.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: Most fisheries texts give 6.5 to 9.0 as the suitable range and 7.5 to 8.5 as the optimum for carp culture; the keyed 6.5 to 10 is the wider tolerable band. It is the only option lying in the workable region, so the key stands as the intended answer.

short_explanation: A silvipastoral system grows trees together with grasses or fodder crops and livestock — the ground cover holds the soil and supplies mulch while the trees give fodder, fuel and shade.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Taungya grows agricultural crops between young forest plantings for the first few years until the canopy closes; it is an agri-silvicultural arrangement, not a fodder and pasture one.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Woody hedgerows on the contour, as in alley cropping, do check erosion, but the stem's fodder and ground-cover description points to the silvipastoral system.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Shifting cultivation is slash and burn, which increases erosion rather than checking it.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Aqua-forestry combines trees with fish culture, the tree leaves serving as feed.

key_note: The stem reads 'long fodder crops', evidently a typo for 'along with fodder crops'; taken that way the trees-plus-pasture-plus-livestock system is the intended answer.

short_explanation: PMAY-Gramin fixed the minimum unit size at 25 square metres, raised from the 20 square metres of the old Indira Awaas Yojana, and the unit must include a hygienic cooking space.
explanation_text: The other parameters travel with it. Unit assistance is Rs 1.20 lakh in the plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly states, the north-east, and difficult and IAP districts, shared between centre and state 60:40 in the plains and 90:10 in the north-eastern and Himalayan states. The beneficiary also gets 90 to 95 days of unskilled wage labour under MGNREGS and Rs 12,000 for a toilet through Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin or another source, and the money is paid into the beneficiary's account in instalments tied to verified construction stages. Beneficiaries are selected from the SECC 2011 housing deprivation data, validated by the Gram Sabha, with the Awaas+ survey added later.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 20 square metres was the Indira Awaas Yojana size that PMAY-G replaced.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The notified floor is 25 square metres; a household may build larger at its own cost, but 30 is not the scheme figure.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary; the notified minimum is 25 square metres.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary; the notified minimum is 25 square metres.

common_traps: 20 square metres is the old IAY figure and is the standard trap on this item.

short_explanation: Nucleus seed is the small quantity of absolutely pure seed the breeder maintains by hand; breeder seed is multiplied from it, so it stands at the head of the entire seed chain.
explanation_text: The chain runs nucleus seed, then breeder seed, then foundation seed, then certified seed, with genetic purity falling by a defined tolerance at each step and quantity rising. Nucleus seed is produced and maintained by the originating breeder. Breeder seed carries a golden-yellow tag and is produced under the breeder's direct supervision against indents. Foundation seed, a white tag, is produced by the National Seeds Corporation, state seed corporations and state farms. Certified seed, an azure-blue tag, is grown by registered growers for sale to farmers; truthfully labelled seed carries an opal-green label and is self-certified by the producer.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Breeder seed is the next link down — produced from nucleus seed under the breeder's supervision — whereas the stem describes the seed used to produce breeder seed.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Foundation seed is the progeny of breeder seed, produced by NSC, state seed corporations and state farms.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Certified seed is the final multiplication, grown by registered growers for sale to cultivators.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The give-away is 'used for the production of breeder seed' — the answer must sit one step above breeder seed, not at it.

short_explanation: Chewing beetles feed on grape leaves from the sprouting stage onward and in a heavy attack strip the vine bare — defoliation of grape is a beetle problem, because only chewing mouthparts can remove leaf tissue.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Thrips rasp the surface and cause silvering and scarring of leaves and berries; they cannot chew a leaf away.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Aphids are sap suckers — they curl leaves and leave honeydew and sooty mould, not holes.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Jassids or leafhoppers also suck sap, giving hopper burn at the leaf margins rather than defoliation.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: 'Defoliator beetle' is a descriptive label rather than a species name; on grape it covers the flea beetle Scelodonta strigicollis and the night-feeding chafers.

short_explanation: Community forestry puts the village at the centre: the local community, the forest department and NGOs manage the forest together and share the timber and fuelwood it yields.
explanation_text: The National Commission on Agriculture, 1976, coined social forestry as the umbrella and split it into farm forestry, where an individual farmer plants on his own holding; extension forestry, planting on roadsides, canal banks, railway strips and wastelands; and community or village forestry, raised on community land for the community's own fuel, fodder and small timber. Joint Forest Management, from the 1988 policy and the 1990 circular, is the institutional form this takes on state forest land, with the village forest committee sharing usufruct in return for protection.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Social forestry is the wider programme of raising trees on wastelands, roadsides and canal banks for village needs; community forestry is one category inside it.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Extension forestry plants trees on strips and lands not previously under forest — along roads, canals and railway lines.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Farm forestry is an individual farmer raising trees on his own holding, with no community management at all.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The stem is garbled ('fir the timber, wood collection'); read as joint community, government and NGO management of a forest for timber and fuelwood, community forestry is the term.

short_explanation: Precision farming uses sensors, satellite positioning and analysis tools to read the variation within a single field and treat each part according to its own need, instead of blanket-treating the whole field.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Plantation farming is large-scale single-crop estate agriculture — tea, coffee, rubber — a farm type, not a technology.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Commercial farming simply means growing for the market rather than for home consumption.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No-till is one conservation practice, sowing without ploughing; it implies no sensing or spatial analysis.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

topic_name: Agriculture's contribution to gross value added
short_explanation: Agriculture and allied activities contribute a little under a fifth of India's gross value added while supporting a far larger share of the workforce; the estimate this item cites puts the figure at 18.4 per cent.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 20.2 per cent is the share widely quoted for 2020-21, the pandemic year when agriculture grew while the rest of the economy contracted, so its share rose.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 18.8 per cent is the figure the Economic Survey 2021-22 gives for 2021-22, and is the closest competing reading of this stem.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No published estimate of the agriculture GVA share for the years around this paper reads 19.6 per cent.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Far below the actual share; agriculture's contribution has not fallen to 15 per cent of GVA.

key_note: The stem does not say which year's first estimates it means, and the year decides the answer: about 20.2 per cent for 2020-21, 18.8 per cent for 2021-22 in the Economic Survey 2021-22, and 18.3 per cent for 2022-23 in the Economic Survey 2022-23. The keyed 18.4 per cent could not be tied to a named release. Check the year and the source release before publication, and add the year to the stem.

short_explanation: In a lift irrigation scheme the pump must first raise water from the source up to itself and then push it on to the delivery point, so the total head is the suction head plus the delivery head.
explanation_text: In design the figure used is the total dynamic head: static suction lift plus static delivery head plus the friction and velocity losses in the pipes, valves and bends. Suction lift is limited to roughly six to seven metres in practice, because atmospheric pressure is all that pushes water up the suction pipe and cavitation sets in beyond that — which is why pumps on deep sources are placed low or submersibles are used. Power follows directly: the water horsepower is the product of density, gravity, discharge and total head, divided by the combined pump and motor efficiency.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Suction head alone covers only the lift from the water surface to the pump centre, not the delivery side.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Delivery head alone covers only the part above the pump, ignoring the lift from the source.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Losses are added to the static head, never subtracted, and there is no separate potential head to add on top of the suction and delivery heads.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: Strictly, the total dynamic head also adds friction and velocity losses; the option set offers only the static sum, so the keyed option is the intended answer.

topic_name: Crop production statistics and leading states
short_explanation: The third advance estimates for 2021-22 put total foodgrain production at a record 314.51 million tonnes, a few million tonnes above the previous year.
explanation_text: Foodgrain estimates come out in rounds — first, second, third and fourth advance estimates and then the final estimate — and each round revises the last as more state returns come in, so the round matters as much as the number. In this particular year the wheat figure was cut in the third round after the heat wave of March 2022 shortened grain filling in the north-west, while rice and coarse cereals held up; the final estimate for 2021-22 came in higher again, at about 315.7 million tonnes.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 308.65 million tonnes sits near the earlier years' level, not the 2021-22 third round.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 305.6 million tonnes is below the previous year's output, and foodgrain production did not fall in 2021-22.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 315.67 is very close to the fourth advance and final estimate of about 315.7 million tonnes — the standard trap on this item, right number but the wrong round.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 320.15 million tonnes is above every estimate released for 2021-22; output crossed 315 million tonnes but not 320.

common_traps: The round decides the number: the third advance estimate reads 314.51 mt while the final estimate is about 315.7 mt.

short_explanation: A watershed is the whole area that drains to one common outlet, and treating that drainage unit as a single unit of planning — from ridge to valley — is what watershed management means.
explanation_text: The ridge-to-valley sequence is the operating principle: work begins on the upper slopes, where runoff starts, and moves down, because treating the valley first only silts up whatever is built there. Arable land gets contour bunding, field bunding and graded bunds; non-arable land gets staggered trenches, gully plugs, check dams and vegetative barriers; and water harvesting structures come at the bottom of the sequence. The main programme vehicle is the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY, now Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 2.0, run by the Department of Land Resources.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Rainwater harvesting collects and stores runoff for use; it is one activity inside a watershed programme, not the drainage unit itself.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The hygroscopic coefficient is a soil moisture constant and has nothing to do with drainage areas.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A correct answer is present among the choices.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The three terms are not interchangeable, so a combined choice fails.

key_note: As printed the stem defines a watershed, while the keyed option names watershed management. The key stands because it is the only option in the right field, but the stem would be better worded as 'a watershed is ...'.

short_explanation: The Soil Health Card scheme tests a farmer's soil and issues a card showing its nutrient status with crop-wise fertiliser recommendations; repeated cycle after cycle, it shows how the soil is responding to management.
explanation_text: Launched in February 2015, the scheme issues a card once every cycle of two to three years per holding, so that change over time can be read rather than a single snapshot. Twelve parameters are reported: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium; sulphur; the micronutrients zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron; and pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon. Samples are drawn on a grid — commonly 2.5 hectares in irrigated areas and 10 hectares in rainfed areas — and tested in static, mobile or village-level laboratories, many of them run by rural entrepreneurs and self-help groups.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana is the contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: eNAM is the electronic national agriculture market linking regulated mandis for online trade.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana supports organic farming clusters; it draws on soil health thinking but does not test soil and issue the card.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The National Centre for Sustainable Aquaculture, set up by MPEDA in 2007, is its outreach arm: it organises small shrimp farmers into aqua societies or clusters and takes better management practices to them.
explanation_text: The cluster is the point. Individual small farmers cannot manage shrimp disease alone, because water in a creek system is shared — one farmer stocking infected seed or discharging a diseased pond puts the whole stretch at risk. NaCSA groups them into societies that agree a common crop calendar, buy specific-pathogen-free seed together, follow agreed water and health management, and keep the pond records that let the produce be traced. Traceability is what keeps Indian shrimp acceptable in the European Union and United States markets, which is MPEDA's export mandate under the Ministry of Commerce.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: APEDA promotes exports of processed food and agricultural products; marine products are carved out and sit with MPEDA.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: PMMSY is the central fisheries scheme, not an MPEDA outreach body.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: CFTRI at Mysuru is a CSIR food technology laboratory.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: CMFRI at Kochi is the ICAR marine fisheries research institute; it does research, not MPEDA's farmer cluster extension.

common_traps: APEDA and MPEDA split the export promotion mandate; marine products go to MPEDA.

short_explanation: The Krishi Vigyan Kendra is the district farm science centre inside the national agricultural research system, set up to assess and refine technology for local conditions and to demonstrate it on farmers' fields.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: ATMA coordinates district extension under the Department of Agriculture and is not part of the research system.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: e-Shram is the Labour Ministry's national database of unorganised workers.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: E-Shakti is NABARD's project for digitising self-help group books of account.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: This repeats Q.191 of the same paper with a shorter stem and different distractors.

short_explanation: Rural India carries the bulk of the country's workers, and the share this item asks for is 33.69 per cent. The stem does not state what that percentage is taken of, which is the weakness of the question.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary as printed; no standard Census 2011 rural workforce ratio reads 30.98 per cent.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Closer to the rural work participation rate, which Census 2011 puts at about 41.8 per cent, but that is a different ratio from the one keyed.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Arbitrary; it sits near the key only to make the choice harder.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Close to rural workers as a share of the total population — about 348.6 million of 1,210.8 million — but that is again not the ratio the key uses.

key_note: Census 2011 gives 481.7 million total workers, a national work participation rate of 39.8 per cent, a rural work participation rate of about 41.8 per cent, and roughly 348.6 million rural workers, which is about 72 per cent of all workers and about 29 per cent of the total population. The keyed 33.69 per cent could not be matched to any of these standard Census 2011 ratios. The base and the source table must be checked before this row is published, and the stem should state what the percentage is of.

topic_name: Farmer welfare schemes and grievance portals
short_explanation: Kisan Call Centres answer farmers' questions in their own language on the toll-free number 1800-180-1551, acting as a single point of contact for farm problems; they have run under the Ministry of Agriculture since 2004.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: e-Krishi Samvad is ICAR's online portal for routing farmer queries to its institutes — a genuine service, but a web interface rather than the all-purpose telephone helpline the stem describes.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A krishi mela is a farm fair, an event rather than a query-handling service.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A correct answer is present among the choices.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The options are not interchangeable, so a combined choice fails.

key_note: The stem — a scheme for the solution of all the problems of farmers — is very loosely worded, and option B is a real ICAR query service, so it is the nearest competing reading. Kisan Call Centres is the item the stem is pointing at.

short_explanation: PMGSY-III, approved in 2019, is the consolidation phase of the rural roads programme: it upgrades existing through routes and major rural links so that villages connect to gramin agricultural markets, higher secondary schools and hospitals.
explanation_text: The three phases build on one another. PMGSY-I, from 2000, provided a first all-weather connection to unconnected habitations above the population threshold — 500 in the plains, 250 in hill, tribal and desert areas. PMGSY-II took up upgradation of the existing rural network. PMGSY-III consolidates about 1,25,000 km of through routes and major rural links, with the cost shared 60:40 between centre and states and 90:10 for the north-eastern and Himalayan states. The programme is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No scheme of this name exists; the rural roads programme is PMGSY.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: PMAY-Gramin is the rural housing scheme.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: PMAY-Urban is the urban housing mission.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The Indian major carps are catla, rohu and mrigal — indigenous river carps that form the base of composite fish culture — and catla is one of them.
explanation_text: Composite fish culture stocks species that feed at different levels so that the whole pond is used without the fish competing. Catla takes zooplankton at the surface, rohu feeds in the column, and mrigal is a bottom feeder; three exotics are commonly added — silver carp at the surface on phytoplankton, grass carp on aquatic weeds, and common carp on the bottom detritus. Keeping the Indian three apart from the exotic three is the distinction most questions on this topic turn on.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Rohu is equally an Indian major carp, so as a single choice it is as defensible as the key; this is a drafting defect in the question rather than a wrong option.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Cyprinus carpio, the common carp, is an exotic introduced species, not an Indian major carp.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A correct answer is present among the choices.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 'All of these' fails only because common carp is exotic; the other two are genuine Indian major carps.

common_traps: Common carp being exotic is what kills 'all of these' - check that option before rejecting it on the Indian species.

short_explanation: Under DAY-NRLM a self-help group borrowing up to Rs 3 lakh pays 7 per cent; on prompt repayment the centre gives a further 3 per cent subvention, which brings the effective cost down to 4 per cent a year.
explanation_text: The subvention works in two layers. Banks lend to eligible women's SHGs at 7 per cent on loans up to Rs 3 lakh, and the difference between that and the bank's own lending rate is met by the centre. On top of that, a group that repays on time gets an additional 3 per cent, paid into its account, so the group that keeps its discipline effectively borrows at 4 per cent. The point of the design is behavioural: the extra 3 per cent is a reward for repayment conduct, not a general discount, which is why NRLM links it to the group's grading and bookkeeping.

common_traps: The stem gives the answer away: the subvention must be whatever takes 7 per cent down to 4 per cent.

E is the son of B, so B is a mother in this house and is the one F is brother to, making A and B husband and wife. D and G are sisters, so A and B have three children: E, D and G. A is the father of C's spouse, and A's only son is E, so C is married to E — the second couple, and everyone still sits inside the two generations the question allows.

Its first role is descriptive: it is the macro indicator of how retail prices are moving. Its second role is statutory: since the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, the 4 per cent target with a two-point band on either side is set and monitored on CPI Combined inflation. Deflation of national accounts aggregates in India is done mainly with wholesale-price-based and implicit price deflators, which is why the third use is kept out here.

topic_name: Quadratic equations — root comparison (x vs y)
short_explanation: The first equation gives x = 2 or 4 and the second gives y = -3 or 2; no pairing puts x below y and one pairing ties, so x is at least y.
explanation_text: Comparing two quadratics means comparing every root of the first with every root of the second — four pairings here. A single relation is announced only when all four point the same way. If some pairings give x above y and others give x below, the relation cannot be determined. Equality in one pairing and 'greater' in the rest is exactly what produces the weak sign rather than the strict one.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A strict x > y fails at the pairing x = 2 against y = 2, where the two are equal.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Every pairing is decided and none runs the other way, so the relation is fixed rather than indeterminate.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: x below y never happens; the smallest x, 2, already matches the larger y.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: x at most y fails at x = 4 against y = 2.

solution_steps: x² - 6x + 8 = 0 factors as (x - 2)(x - 4) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 4.
y² + y - 6 = 0 factors as (y + 3)(y - 2) = 0, so y = -3 or y = 2.
Pairings: 2 against -3 and 4 against -3 both give x above y; 4 against 2 gives x above y; 2 against 2 gives equality.
No pairing gives x below y, and one gives equality, so x is at least y.
formula_used: For ax² + bx + c = 0, split b into two parts whose product is a × c.

topic_name: Root cause analysis and problem-solving tools
short_explanation: Pareto analysis is the 80:20 tool: it ranks the causes of a problem by how much each contributes and shows that a small number of them produce most of the effect.
explanation_text: In practice, list the causes, measure each one by frequency or by cost, sort them in descending order and read the cumulative line. The few causes that account for roughly 80 per cent of the damage are the 'vital few' and get attention first. Pareto analysis prioritises — it tells a manager which problem to attack, not why the problem happens.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Root cause analysis digs beneath one problem to find the underlying cause; it does not weigh causes against one another by share of the total.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Ishikawa or fishbone diagram groups possible causes by category — people, method, machine, material — but attaches no numbers to them.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Five Whys follows a single chain of causes by asking 'why' repeatedly; there is no 80:20 arithmetic anywhere in it.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Brainstorming generates ideas and options; it neither measures nor ranks their contribution.

common_traps: Root cause analysis, Ishikawa and Five Whys all hunt for causes. Only Pareto weighs them by how much of the outcome each one explains.

short_explanation: Rill erosion is the stage where runoff concentrates into many small finger-like channels across the field; these can still be smoothed out by ordinary tillage.
explanation_text: Water erosion runs through a sequence. Splash erosion detaches soil, sheet erosion removes a thin uniform layer from the whole surface, rill erosion concentrates the flow into numerous shallow finger-like channels, and when those channels deepen and join beyond the reach of ordinary implements they become gullies. The working test in the field is exactly that: if ploughing can erase the channel it is a rill, if it cannot it is a gully.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Sheet erosion removes a thin layer uniformly from the surface; no channels have formed yet.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Gully erosion is the later stage, when rills deepen and widen past the point where tillage can erase them.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Saltation is a mode of wind transport, in which particles bounce along the surface.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Suspension is also wind transport, carrying the finest particles in the air stream.

common_traps: Rill and gully differ by whether normal tillage can still smooth the channel out, not by shape alone.

short_explanation: Only statement 4 is correct: PM-KISAN pays 6,000 rupees a year directly into the beneficiary's bank account in three equal instalments of 2,000 rupees. The family definition, the treatment of institutional landholders and the land-record condition are all stated wrongly.
explanation_text: Under PM-KISAN a 'family' is husband, wife and minor children only, so adult children and parents form separate families and can hold their own entitlement. Institutional landholders are expressly excluded, as are income-tax payers, serving and retired government officials, professionals such as doctors and lawyers, and pensioners drawing 10,000 rupees a month or more. On land records, the general rule is that the name must appear in the records, but Manipur, Nagaland and Jharkhand have community or lineage-based tenure and use certified alternatives, so 'in all States' overstates it.

option_rationales.label: D

common_traps: The family unit under PM-KISAN stops at minor children. Parents, parents-in-law and adult children are not part of it, which is exactly what statement 1 reverses.
