topic_name: Quadratic equations — root comparison (x vs y)
short_explanation: x comes out as 1 or 11 and y as -4 or 11; x = 1 sits below y = 11 while x = 11 sits above y = -4, so the two cannot be ordered.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: x > y fails at x = 1 against y = 11.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: x at least y fails at the same pairing, x = 1 against y = 11.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: x < y fails at x = 11 against y = -4.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: x at most y fails at x = 11 against y = -4.

solution_steps: x² - 12x + 11 = 0 factors as (x - 1)(x - 11) = 0, so x = 1 or 11.
y² - 7y - 44 = 0 factors as (y - 11)(y + 4) = 0, so y = 11 or -4.
x = 1 against y = 11 gives x below y; x = 11 against y = -4 gives x above y.
Both directions occur, so no single relation holds.
formula_used: For ax² + bx + c = 0, split b into two parts whose product is a × c.
common_traps: Both equations share the root 11, which tempts a quick 'x = y'; the other two roots, 1 and -4, are what break the order.

short_explanation: Confirmation bias is the pull towards evidence that agrees with what one already believes, so the counter is to set personal preference aside and test the belief against evidence on its own terms.
explanation_text: Objectivity here is a procedure, not a mood. State the belief as a hypothesis, look deliberately for evidence that would disprove it, ask a colleague to argue the opposite case, and decide in advance what evidence would make you change your mind. Each of those steps removes the decision from the pull of what one already thinks.

explanation_text: Credulity is the noun — the willingness to believe. Credulous is the adjective describing the person who believes too readily. The idiom needs a noun after 'stretching', so only the noun form fits both the grammar and the sense; an adjective or an adverb in that slot leaves the participle without an object.

short_explanation: A private or incognito window keeps all three out of the permanent record — form entries, browsing history and cookies, the last of which work during the session and are thrown away when the window closes.
explanation_text: Incognito mode changes what the browser writes to the local machine, and nothing more. Within the session cookies still function, so sites can keep a person signed in; when the last incognito window closes, those cookies, the typed form data and that session's page history are all discarded. What it does not hide is the traffic itself — an employer, a school network, an internet service provider and the sites visited can all still see the activity, and any file deliberately downloaded stays on the disk.

short_explanation: Section 7(1) of the RTI Act gives the Public Information Officer 30 days from receipt of the request to decide it, either supplying the information or rejecting it on a stated exemption ground.
explanation_text: Around that 30-day clock sit a few variations worth holding: 48 hours where the information concerns the life or liberty of a person; 35 days where the request came in through an Assistant Public Information Officer, who gets five extra days to route it; and 40 days where a third party's interest has to be heard under Section 11. If the officer misses the deadline the request is deemed refused and the information must then be supplied free of any fee.

option_rationales.rationale: 21 days is not a limit under the RTI Act.

option_rationales.label: E

short_explanation: Minimum Support Prices are recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices, which works out cost estimates and price advice for 22 mandated crops; the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs then approves and announces them.
explanation_text: The MSP chain has three distinct steps, and the question turns on which of them the word recommended names. CACP, set up in 1965 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, gathers cost of cultivation data from the states and recommends a price for each mandated crop, working from the A2 plus family labour cost concept with a margin over it. The Department of Agriculture circulates that recommendation to states and ministries. CCEA, chaired by the Prime Minister, takes the final decision, and the government announces the price. So the recommending body is CACP and the approving body is CCEA.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: There is no Agricultural Credit Policy Council behind MSP; agricultural credit policy sits with RBI and NABARD.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: This is in fact the body that recommends MSP - see the key note, since the paper's key names CCEA instead.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: FSSAI sets food safety standards under the Health Ministry and has no role in price support.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: CACP recommends, CCEA approves; the verb in the stem decides the answer.
key_note: The paper keys CCEA. CCEA approves and announces MSP but does not recommend it - the recommending body is CACP. Read loosely as which body decides MSP, CCEA fits; as written, with the verb recommended, option B is correct.

topic_name: Number series — arithmetic and difference patterns
short_explanation: Every term is 18 times a prime — 18×2, 18×3, 18×5, 18×7, 18×11 — so the next is 18 × 13 = 234.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 242, which is not even a multiple of 18; the pattern fixes the term at 18 × 13 = 234.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 228, which is also not a multiple of 18; the working gives 234.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 210, again not a multiple of 18; the working gives 234.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 216 is 18 × 12, which takes the next whole number instead of the next prime.

solution_steps: Those quotients are the primes in order.
The next prime is 13, so the next term is 18 × 13 = 234.
common_traps: The differences 18, 36, 36, 72 look irregular and lead nowhere; dividing through by 18 is what exposes the pattern.

short_explanation: PM Vishwakarma gives a registered artisan a toolkit incentive of 15,000 rupees and collateral-free credit in two tranches; the first Enterprise Development Loan is up to 1 lakh rupees, repayable over 18 months.
explanation_text: The credit comes as a ladder, not a lump. Tranche one is up to 1 lakh rupees over 18 months; tranche two, up to 2 lakh rupees over 30 months, opens only for artisans with a clean repayment record on the first loan who have adopted digital transactions and completed advanced training. The beneficiary pays a concessional 5 per cent, with the rest of the interest subvented by the government, and the loans carry a credit guarantee. The scheme was launched on 17 September 2023 by the MSME ministry with an outlay of about 13,000 crore rupees across 18 traditional trades.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No tranche of 1.5 lakh rupees exists, and 12 months is shorter than the 18 given for the first loan.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2 lakh rupees is the second tranche, not the first, and that one runs 30 months rather than 16.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 3 lakh rupees is above even the two tranches added together, and 21 months matches no tenor in the scheme.

option_rationales.label: D

short_explanation: A dog whistle is coded language that a target group hears as prejudice, so the politics rests on bigotry and the weapon deployed is rhetoric.

option_rationales.label: A

topic_name: Pioneers and landmarks in computing history
short_explanation: Enigma was the rotor cipher machine the German forces used to encrypt their wartime signals, and breaking its traffic became a central Allied effort.

option_rationales.label: B

option_rationales.label: E

key_note: Enigma is a cipher machine rather than a computer in the modern sense; the stem's phrase 'computer device' is loose but points unambiguously at Enigma.

short_explanation: The Delphi method polls a panel of experts anonymously through rounds of structured questionnaires, feeding back the summarised replies each round until the estimates converge.
explanation_text: Anonymity is the whole point. It strips out rank, personality and the pull of the loudest voice, so what survives is judgement rather than group pressure. Delphi is used where hard data is thin and expert opinion is the best available input — technology adoption, long-horizon demand, policy risk.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Linear programming optimises a mathematical objective subject to constraints; no panel and no questionnaires are involved.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: PERT maps the activities of a project and estimates the time along the critical path.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Cost-benefit analysis compares the money value of costs against gains; it is not a method of gathering expert opinion.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The subject 'A 54-year-old man' is singular, so the auxiliary must be 'has', and the man is the one arrested, which needs the passive 'has been arrested for'.
explanation_text: Two rules meet in this blank. Subject-verb agreement fixes 'has' — the plural-looking '14 women' later in the sentence is not the subject. Voice fixes 'been arrested': the man receives the action, he does not perform it. The preposition 'for' then introduces the ground of the arrest.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Agreement is right but the voice is wrong — 'has arrested for' says the man arrested somebody else.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Wrong on both counts: a plural verb with a singular subject, and active voice where the passive is needed.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The past perfect would place this arrest before some other past event; the sentence reports one recent event, for which the present perfect is correct.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The original reads 'have been arrested' with a singular subject, so an improvement is required.

common_traps: '14 women' sits close to the verb and tempts a plural; under the proximity trap the verb still agrees with the real subject, 'A 54-year-old man'.

short_explanation: Each step multiplies by 1, 2, 3, ... and adds 3, 4, 5, ... — so after 15 × 1 + 3 = 18 the next term should be 18 × 2 + 4 = 40, not 42.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 125 is right: the corrected 40 × 3 + 5 = 125.

solution_steps: 15 × 1 + 3 = 18, which matches the series.
18 × 2 + 4 = 40, but the series prints 42.
Every later term is right, so the single wrong term is 42, which should read 40.
common_traps: Every later term follows correctly from the corrected 40, so the error sits early in the series rather than at the tail where it is usually hunted.

short_explanation: When the outcome is uncertain but the downside is small, no single approach is compulsory — caution, more information, a wider set of options or a quick intuitive call are all acceptable, because a wrong choice costs little.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Caution is one workable response, but the stem rules none of the other three out.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Gathering information is legitimate, though with minimal risk the effort may not repay itself; it is still only part of the list.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Considering all options is sound practice and again only one of the four approaches offered.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: An intuitive call is reasonable when little is at stake, yet the key treats all four as permissible rather than this one alone.

key_note: The item is loosely drafted. Most decision-making texts would say that low risk is precisely when intuition suffices and exhaustive information-gathering is wasteful, which makes D the tighter single answer. The key is defensible only on the reading that with minimal risk none of the four approaches is ruled out.

topic_name: File formats, encoding standards and multimedia
short_explanation: ASCII is the American Standard Code for Information Interchange, the scheme that gives every letter, digit and control character a number.
explanation_text: ASCII fixes 128 characters in 7 bits — the English letters in both cases, the ten digits, punctuation and a set of control codes. Eight-bit extensions push the count to 256 to carry accented letters and box-drawing characters. Unicode later took over for scripts beyond English, but kept its first 128 code points identical to ASCII, which is why plain ASCII text is still valid Unicode.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Not a real standard; the expansion is invented.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Not a real body; the expansion is invented.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Not a real standard; the expansion is invented.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: MGNREGA requires work to be given within five kilometres of the applicant's village; where it is given beyond that, the worker is paid an extra 10 per cent of the wage to cover travel and living costs.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 5 per cent halves the statutory top-up and 8 km is not the radius used anywhere in the Act's schedules.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 15 per cent and 10 km both overstate; the pair fixed in the Act is 10 per cent beyond 5 km.

option_rationales.label: D

option_rationales.label: E

short_explanation: Food grains keep safely when their moisture is held at roughly 10 to 14 per cent; above that, storage fungi and insects multiply and the grain heats and spoils.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 13-18% runs well past the safe limit - grain above about 14% moisture invites mould.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 15-16% is too wet for a godown and is closer to the moisture of freshly harvested paddy.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 18-19% is field moisture; grain at this level must be dried before it is binned.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 18-20% is wetter still and would spoil within weeks in ordinary storage.

key_note: Handbooks usually quote about 12% as the safe storage figure for cereals and 9-10% for oilseeds; the key's 10-14% is the broad cereal band.

short_explanation: Ploughing is primary tillage - the first deep operation, done after harvest or before the season, that cuts, breaks and inverts the soil.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Secondary tillage follows ploughing - harrowing, planking and levelling break the clods that primary tillage leaves.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Blind tillage is done after sowing but before the crop emerges, to kill early weeds and break the surface crust.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Clean tillage means keeping the field free of all vegetation; it describes the aim, not the order or depth of the operation.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: 'Had a heated debate' is already correct — simple past for a finished event, with 'heated' the established adjective for an angry argument.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The present tense clashes with 'recently', which reports an event already over.

short_explanation: PM SHRI, approved in September 2022, upgrades more than 14,500 existing government schools into exemplar schools showcasing NEP 2020; central support runs five years, from 2022-23 to 2026-27, after which the States and UTs must hold the benchmark on their own.

short_explanation: A puddler is the implement used to churn soil under standing water before paddy transplanting, producing the soft mud with low percolation that a puddled rice field needs.

option_rationales.rationale: A harrow is a secondary tillage implement for breaking clods in a dry or moist field, not for working under standing water.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A scraper moves and levels earth; it does not puddle soil.

option_rationales.label: D

short_explanation: Two years of compound interest at 10% adds 21% of the principal, so ₹5,880 fixes the principal at ₹28,000; two years of simple interest on that is 20%, or ₹5,600.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ₹6,400 is two years' simple interest on a principal of ₹32,000, a guessed round figure; the 21% compound factor fixes the principal at ₹28,000.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: ₹6,000 is two years' simple interest on ₹30,000, again a guessed principal rather than the one 0.21 × P = 5,880 gives.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: ₹7,200 is two years' simple interest on ₹36,000, far above the principal the compound figure allows.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

solution_steps: Two-year compound factor at 10%: 1.1 × 1.1 = 1.21, so the interest is 0.21 of the principal.
Simple interest for 2 years at 10% = 28,000 × 10 × 2 / 100 = ₹5,600.
formula_used: CI for 2 years = P[(1 + r/100)² - 1]; SI = P × r × t / 100.
common_traps: For two years the compound and simple interests stand in the fixed ratio 21 : 20, so ₹5,880 × 20/21 reaches ₹5,600 in a single step.

short_explanation: 'Only a few footballs are cricket' guarantees that part of footballs stands outside cricket, so the second conclusion holds; nothing forces any light to be cricket, because light sits inside lamp and the cricket that is lamp need not reach it.
explanation_text: 'Only lamp is light' reverses into 'all light is lamp' — the word 'only' marks the larger class, not the smaller. So light lies wholly inside lamp. 'Some cricket is lamp' puts part of cricket inside lamp as well, but that part can sit in the stretch of lamp that is not light, which is why the first conclusion cannot be drawn. 'Only a few footballs are cricket' is the standard restricted form: some footballs are cricket and some footballs are not, and the second half of that is exactly what the second conclusion says.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The first conclusion is not forced — the cricket lying inside lamp need not overlap light at all.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The first conclusion fails, so the pair cannot both follow.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The second conclusion is contained directly in 'only a few footballs are cricket', which splits footballs into a cricket part and a non-cricket part.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: An either-or answer is for two conclusions that cannot both be false and cannot both be true; here the second is definitely true on its own.

common_traps: 'Only lamp is light' means all light is lamp, not all lamp is light.
key_note: Read as a possibility — 'few light CAN be cricket' — the first conclusion would also stand, since nothing stops light from lying inside the cricket part of lamp, and the answer would be 'both'. The key treats it as a definite claim, and the next question in the paper uses the same definite reading, so the two are at least consistent with each other.

short_explanation: Alt + Tab cycles through the open applications — hold Alt to move along the list and release it to land on the chosen window.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Ctrl + Shift + Tab moves backwards through tabs inside a browser or document, not between applications.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Windows + Tab opens Task View, a full overview of windows and virtual desktops, rather than a quick toggle.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Windows + M minimises every open window.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Ctrl + Alt + Delete opens the security options screen.

short_explanation: Content analysis works on material that must first be in hand — transcripts, complaints, reports, social posts — so gathering that body of content comes before coding, analysis and interpretation.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Analysis operates on material already collected and coded, so it cannot be the first step.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A hypothesis may frame the study, but the stem asks for the first step of content analysis itself, which the key treats as getting the content.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Sampling selects from a body of material, and that presumes the material is already available.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Interpretation is the last step — it reads meaning out of the completed analysis.

key_note: Some research-methods texts place sampling before collection, on the view that one decides what to include and then collects only that. The key is defensible on the ordinary reading that nothing can be sampled or coded until the content has been gathered.

topic_name: Soil physical properties and soil moisture
short_explanation: Clay has the lowest particle density of the separates listed, because clay minerals such as kaolinite and montmorillonite pack less densely than the quartz that dominates sand and silt.
explanation_text: Particle density is the mass of the solid particles divided by the volume of the solids alone, leaving pore space out of the reckoning. For most mineral soils it sits near 2.65 g/cm3, the density of quartz, which is why the sand and silt fractions cluster at that value. Clay-sized material is made largely of secondary layer silicates that hold water between their sheets and are lighter, so clay runs lower, around 2.2 to 2.6 g/cm3. Keep this apart from bulk density, which includes pore space and is low in clay soils for a different reason - their high porosity.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Sandy soil is mostly quartz, whose particle density is about 2.65 g/cm3 - among the highest here.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Fine sand is still quartz; grain size changes bulk density, not the density of the mineral itself.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Silt is also made of primary minerals, so its particle density stays close to that of sand.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Loam is a mixture of sand, silt and clay, so it falls between the extremes rather than at the bottom.

common_traps: Particle density excludes pore space, bulk density includes it; the two questions have different reasoning even when the answer is clay.
key_note: Many texts treat particle density as near-constant at 2.65 g/cm3 for mineral soils; the key relies on the lower values reported for clay minerals.

short_explanation: Some good are actor and no actor is player, so that stretch of good lies outside player and the first conclusion holds. Nothing ties movies to actor, so the second does not.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Movies overlap good and good overlaps actor, but the two overlaps can be different parts of good, so no movie need be an actor.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The second conclusion is not forced, so the pair cannot both follow.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The first conclusion does follow: the good that is actor cannot be player, because no actor is player.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: An either-or answer needs two conclusions that cannot both be false; here the first is definitely true.

short_explanation: 63 litres split 3 : 4 is 27 litres of water and 36 of milk; only water is added, so the unchanged 36 litres of milk becomes two of five parts and the mixture ends at 90 litres.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 54 litres is the water in the final mixture, not the mixture itself.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 36 litres is the milk, which stays constant throughout.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 63 litres is the starting mixture, before any water is poured in.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 81 litres; holding the milk at 36 litres as two of five parts fixes the total at 90.

solution_steps: Water = 63 × 3/7 = 27 litres; milk = 63 × 4/7 = 36 litres.
Adding water leaves the milk at 36 litres.
In the final 3 : 2 water-to-milk mixture, milk is 2 of 5 parts, so one part = 36/2 = 18 litres.
Final mixture = 5 × 18 = 90 litres, of which water is 54 litres — meaning 27 litres were poured in.
formula_used: The component that does not change fixes the scale: final total = unchanged quantity × total parts / its own parts.
common_traps: The question asks for the final mixture, not the water added — that second figure is 27 litres.

short_explanation: Parental controls do all four — capping screen time, blocking unsuitable sites, reporting on activity and, through those, steering children towards steadier habits.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Limiting screen time is one of the four listed benefits, not the whole of them.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Blocking unsuitable sites is one of the four listed benefits.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Monitoring online activity is one of the four listed benefits.

option_rationales.label: D

short_explanation: Rhizobium is the one biofertilizer here confined to legumes - it fixes nitrogen only inside root nodules formed in symbiosis with a legume host, so it does nothing for a non-legume.
explanation_text: Nitrogen-fixing biofertilizers divide by how they live. Rhizobium is symbiotic: it enters the root hairs of a legume, forms nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen inside them, and it is crop specific, so a chickpea strain will not serve wheat. Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living or associative fixers that live in the soil or on the root surface and are recommended for cereals, millets, cotton and vegetables. Blue green algae and Azolla are used in flooded rice, Azolla carrying the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae in its leaf cavities.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Azospirillum is an associative fixer recommended for cereals, sorghum and millets - all non-legumes.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Azotobacter is free-living in the soil and is applied to wheat, rice, cotton and vegetables.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Blue green algae are used in flooded paddy, a non-legume.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Azolla is a water fern used as a nitrogen source in rice, again a non-legume.

common_traps: The stem asks which is NOT used in non-legumes; read as which IS used, the answer flips.

short_explanation: The accident happened on Sunday, so the verb must be the past 'fell', and a child going inside a vessel falls 'into' it, not 'onto' its surface.
explanation_text: 'Into' marks movement that ends inside an enclosed space; 'onto' marks movement that ends on top of a surface. A vessel of hot sambar is a container with contents, so the child fell into it. The two-word 'fall in' states position rather than the movement of entering, which is why 'fall in a vessel' does not carry the same sense.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Keeps the present-tense 'fall' and uses the weaker 'in', which states where the child was rather than the movement inwards.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The tense is corrected, but 'onto' leaves the child on the outside of the vessel.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The preposition is right and the tense is not — the accident is reported as past.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The original carries both faults, present tense and 'onto', so improvement is required.

common_traps: Two errors are planted, tense and preposition. Options B and D each repair only one of them.

short_explanation: Khadi Gramodyog Vikas Yojana is run by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission under the MSME ministry to support khadi artisans and village industries; its beneficiaries fall in the 18 to 55 year age band.

short_explanation: Fish grow well when dissolved oxygen in the pond stays around 6 ppm; below about 3 to 4 ppm feeding and growth slow, and prolonged low oxygen kills.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 7 ppm is comfortable for fish, but the figure usually given as the optimum for pond culture is 6 ppm.

option_rationales.label: D

key_note: Manuals commonly state 5 ppm as the safe minimum and 5-7 ppm as the desirable range; the key picks 6 ppm from inside that band, so treat the exact figure as the paper's.

short_explanation: The ratio condition gives A as 18 and B as 12; an average of 18 across three people means 54 years in all, so C is 24 now and 30 in six years.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 32 adds the 8 years from the ratio clause to C's present age of 24 instead of the 6 years the question asks for.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 36; C is 24 today and only 6 years are added.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 40; the working gives 30.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

solution_steps: Let A = 3k and B = 2k. After 8 years, (3k + 8)/(2k + 8) = 13/10.
Cross-multiplying: 30k + 80 = 26k + 104, so 4k = 24 and k = 6.
A = 18 and B = 12.
Average of A, B and C is 18, so A + B + C = 54 and C = 54 - 30 = 24.
C after 6 years = 24 + 6 = 30 years.
formula_used: Sum of ages = average × number of people.
common_traps: Two different time shifts appear in the question — 8 years inside the ratio clause and 6 years in what is actually asked.

topic_name: Bounded rationality and limits on information processing
short_explanation: Herbert Simon's bounded rationality holds that real decision-makers work with incomplete information, limited attention and limited time, and so settle for a good-enough option rather than the best one.
explanation_text: The contrast is with the fully rational model, which assumes complete information, unlimited processing capacity and a consistent ranking of every alternative. Simon replaced maximising with satisficing: search the options until one clears the acceptability threshold, then stop. The three bounds are information, cognitive capacity and time — time pressure is one of them, which is why it appears as a characteristic rather than as a failing.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Complete information is an assumption of the fully rational model, which bounded rationality exists to reject.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Unlimited cognitive capacity is precisely the bound Simon's model denies.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Bounded rationality describes people as intending to be rational but constrained, not as always rational.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Satisficing — taking the first acceptable option — is the model's core claim, so 'always the best possible decision' is its opposite.

short_explanation: 'Meet with an accident' is the fixed collocation for being involved in one; no other preposition works with 'met' in this sense.
explanation_text: Prepositions in such idioms are settled by usage, not by logic: met with an accident, met with resistance, met with approval. Drop the 'with' and 'met' falls back to its ordinary sense of encountering a person face to face, which is not what happened to the bus.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Without 'with', 'met an accident' reads as encountering something face to face, which is not the sense required.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 'Met to an accident' is not an English collocation.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 'Met of an accident' is not an English collocation either.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The original reads 'met on an accident', which is wrong, so improvement is required.

short_explanation: The order from heaviest runs Y, N, X, M, Z, O, so the second heaviest — the 56 kg person — is N.
explanation_text: 'N is lighter than only Y' fixes Y first and N second. 'X is heavier than 3 persons' leaves exactly two people above X, so X is third. That leaves M, Z and O for the last three places. Z is lighter than M and Z is not the lightest, so M is fourth, Z fifth and O sixth. The two stated weights then attach to the second and the fifth places: N weighs 56 kg and Z weighs 28 kg, and only O's weight stays open, below 28 kg.

option_rationales.label: C

option_rationales.label: E

short_explanation: Mission Shakti is the Women and Child Development Ministry's umbrella scheme for the safety, security and empowerment of women, running from 2021-22 to 2025-26.
explanation_text: Mission Shakti has two arms. Sambal covers safety and security: One Stop Centres, the Women Helpline, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Nari Adalats. Samarthya covers empowerment: Shakti Sadan for women in distress, Sakhi Niwas working women hostels, Palna creches and the maternity benefit scheme PMMVY. It is worth separating from the ministry's other two umbrellas, Mission Vatsalya for child protection and Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 for nutrition.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Mission Vatsalya is the child protection and child welfare umbrella, not the women's scheme.

option_rationales.label: B

short_explanation: Profit follows money multiplied by time: Mano put in ₹3,200 for 40% of the year and Varthan ₹4,800 for the remaining 60%, which is 3200 × 40 against 4800 × 60, or 4 : 9.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 3 : 5; weighting each investment by its own time gives 4 : 9.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 5 : 6; the working gives 4 : 9.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 2 : 5; even the bare capital ratio here is 2 : 3, and the time weighting turns it into 4 : 9.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 1 : 3 comes from reading '40% of the year' as 4 months and the rest as 8: 3,200 × 4 against 4,800 × 8 gives 1 : 3.

solution_steps: Mano's share of the year is 40%, so Varthan's is the remaining 60%.
Varthan's weight = 4,800 × 60 = 2,88,000.
1,28,000 : 2,88,000 divides through to 4 : 9.
formula_used: Profit share is proportional to capital × time invested.
common_traps: 40% of a year is 4.8 months, not 4.

topic_name: Rational decision-making model and its assumptions
short_explanation: The rational model assumes a decision-maker with full information who ranks options consistently and picks the one with the highest utility; letting emotion drive the choice contradicts every part of that.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Perfect information is one of the model's standing assumptions.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Consistency of preferences is assumed — the same ranking holds from one choice to the next.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Transitivity, that preferring A to B and B to C implies preferring A to C, is a core axiom of the model.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Maximising utility is the model's stated objective.

common_traps: The stem asks which assumption does NOT align with the model; four options are genuine assumptions and only one is the odd one out.

topic_name: Irrigation projects and command area classification
short_explanation: A medium irrigation project is one whose culturable command area lies between 2,000 and 10,000 hectares.
explanation_text: Indian irrigation projects are classified by culturable command area - the area that can actually be irrigated. Minor projects command up to 2,000 hectares, medium projects 2,000 to 10,000 hectares, and major projects more than 10,000 hectares. The class is not a label only: it decides which agency plans and funds the work, how it is appraised, and whether state-owned minor and medium works can draw support from NABARD through the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Small project is not a category in the Indian classification.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Minor projects command up to 2,000 hectares, below the range asked about.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Major projects have a culturable command area above 10,000 hectares.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Mini project is not part of the official classification.

common_traps: 2,000 hectares separates minor from medium and 10,000 hectares medium from major.

option_rationales.rationale: Regulating access to a system belongs to sign-in, user accounts and permissions, not to a task manager.

short_explanation: PMGSY builds and upgrades rural roads, and in the Indian road classification 'rural roads' means Other District Roads and Village Roads. Major District Roads sit a tier above and stay with the State PWD.
explanation_text: PMGSY connects eligible unconnected habitations by an all-weather road: 500 or more people in the plains, and 250 or more in hill states, tribal Schedule V areas, the desert areas and selected left-wing-extremism blocks, counted on the 2001 Census. PMGSY-I built new connectivity, PMGSY-II upgraded and consolidated existing rural routes, and PMGSY-III consolidates through routes linking habitations to markets, schools and hospitals.

short_explanation: The two trips give upstream 5 kmph and downstream 35 kmph, so the boat is 20 and the stream 15; raised to 25 and 18 they give 7 upstream and 43 downstream, and 301/7 + 301/43 = 43 + 7 = 50 hours.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 40 hours; the new speeds of 7 and 43 kmph give 43 + 7 = 50.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 45 hours; the working gives 50.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 60 hours is roughly 301/5, the upstream leg alone at the original speed; the question raises both speeds and asks for both legs.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The two given journeys fix the boat and stream speeds exactly, so the time is fully determined.

solution_steps: Upstream speed = 80/16 = 5 kmph; downstream speed = 280/8 = 35 kmph.
Boat speed = (35 + 5)/2 = 20 kmph; stream speed = (35 - 5)/2 = 15 kmph.
After the increases: boat 25 kmph, stream 18 kmph.
New upstream = 25 - 18 = 7 kmph; new downstream = 25 + 18 = 43 kmph.
formula_used: Boat speed = (downstream + upstream)/2; stream speed = (downstream - upstream)/2.
common_traps: The boat gains 5 kmph and the stream 3, so upstream rises by only 2 kmph while downstream rises by 8 — the two legs are not affected equally.

short_explanation: Incognito mode leaves the download out of the browser's history, but the file itself lands in the usual Downloads folder and stays there for anyone using the machine.
explanation_text: The rule is that private browsing controls what the browser remembers, not what the file system keeps. Closing the incognito window clears that session's history, cookies and form entries, and the download will not appear in the browser's download list. The saved file, though, sits on the disk exactly where any other download would — unencrypted, unhidden, and visible to the next person who opens the folder.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Nothing is diverted to a temporary folder; the file goes to the normal download location and survives the session.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Private browsing applies no encryption to downloaded files.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Nothing is uploaded to cloud storage unless the folder happens to be separately synced.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Two different things are at stake — the download entry in the browser's list is cleared, the file on disk is not.

short_explanation: 'Financial heft' means financial weight or clout, which is what a ₹552 crore auction reflects, and it sits naturally beside 'fresh hopes'.

topic_name: Memory types and the memory hierarchy
short_explanation: Among the devices listed, cache is fastest, then ROM, then the hard disk, then the floppy disk, with tape slowest of all.
explanation_text: The memory hierarchy runs from small, fast and costly at the top to large, slow and cheap at the bottom: registers inside the processor, then cache, then main memory, then solid-state or magnetic disk, then removable and archival media. Electronic storage with no moving parts — cache and ROM — always beats anything that has to spin or wind. Tape sits at the very bottom because it is read in sequence rather than by direct access.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: This starts with the floppy disk, one of the slowest items on the list, and buries cache near the end.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: This runs from slow to fast and finishes with cache, the fastest item of all.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: This puts ROM first and cache last, reversing the two.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This opens with the tape drive, the slowest device listed, and names the floppy disk twice.

common_traps: Direction matters — two of the options hold the right idea but list it slowest-first.

short_explanation: The blank is set against 'international in flavour', so it needs the word for home-grown: a league domestic in spirit and international in flavour.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 'Private in spirit' sets up no contrast with 'international'; the sentence opposes home to abroad, not private to public.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 'State in spirit' is not idiomatic, and the contrast intended is national, not provincial.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Close in sense, but 'local' is normally opposed to 'national'; the pair that opposes 'international' at country level is domestic/international.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: 'Local' is the nearest rival and is not absurd. The sentence balances the blank against 'international in flavour', and the standard pairing at national level is domestic/international, which is why the key prefers 'domestic'.

short_explanation: Under Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) Phase-II, up to 5 per cent of the funds for programmatic components may go to Information, Education and Communication and to capacity building, the behaviour-change side of the mission rather than construction.
explanation_text: Phase-II shifted the mission from building toilets to holding ODF status and managing solid and liquid waste, and its cost norms follow that shift. Administrative charges sit under a separate ceiling of about 2 per cent and are not part of the 5 per cent. Community sanitary complexes are a funded construction item with their own unit cost and central-State sharing, so they are financed in their own right rather than out of the soft-component allowance.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: IEC belongs here but the construction of community sanitary complexes is a funded item with its own unit cost.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: IEC and capacity building belong here; adding construction of community sanitary complexes takes it outside the soft-component allowance.

short_explanation: Rounding gives 60 × 40 = 2,400, less 956, plus 46 × 3 = 138 — about 1,582.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 1,434 sits below 1,444, which is what 2,400 - 956 already gives before the last product is added; the third term adds rather than subtracts.

option_rationales.rationale: 1,628 follows from rounding 2.99 up to 4 and taking the last product as 46 × 4 = 184.

short_explanation: Repairs and maintenance is an operating cost of a tractor - it is incurred as the machine works, unlike depreciation, which accrues whether the tractor runs or stands idle.
explanation_text: Farm machinery costs split into fixed and operating. Fixed costs - depreciation, interest on investment, insurance, taxes and shelter - arise from owning the machine, and per hour they fall the more it is used. Operating costs - fuel, lubricants, repairs and maintenance, and the operator's wage - rise with every hour of work. The examinable point is that repairs and maintenance belong on the operating side, even though farmers often meet them as occasional lump sums that feel fixed.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Variable cost is the category maintenance falls into rather than a specific tractor cost item; see the key note.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Depreciation is the standard fixed cost - it accrues with time and ownership, not with hours worked.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Explicit cost means any cost actually paid out, a bookkeeping category that cuts across fixed and operating heads.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Marginal cost is the cost of producing one more unit, an economic concept rather than a machinery cost head.

key_note: Maintenance is itself a variable cost, so option B overlaps with the key; the stem asks for a cost of the tractor, which maintenance names and the category label does not.

short_explanation: If work is not given within 15 days of the demand, Section 7 entitles the applicant to an unemployment allowance of at least a quarter of the minimum wage for the first 30 days of the financial year, and at least half of it for the rest of that year.
explanation_text: Two points make this provision work in practice. The allowance is paid by the State government from its own funds, which is the pressure that pushes States to actually open worksites. And the clock starts from the dated receipt issued against the written work application, so the receipt is the document a worker must insist on; without it there is nothing to prove the 15 days ran out.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: This reverses the order. The rate rises across the year, it does not fall.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Half for the whole year overstates the first 30 days, which carry a quarter.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: One-third appears nowhere in Section 7, and the later rate is half, not a quarter.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A quarter throughout understates the rest of the year, which carries half.

common_traps: The rate rises over the year: a quarter first, half afterwards. Reading it the other way round lands squarely on option A.

short_explanation: D equals R, and R is at least F, which is strictly above M and so above E — that carries D > E. L only reaches as high as R, and F also sits under R, so L and F are never put in order.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: L < N is at most D, which equals R, and F is also at most R; two quantities sitting under the same value have no fixed order between them.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The first conclusion is not established, so the pair cannot both follow.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: This option repeats option C word for word and fails for the same reason.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: O > R > K is at least X, so O > X does hold; the difficulty is that the second conclusion holds as well, and no option offers that pair.

common_traps: A strict O > X does satisfy a claim written with the weak sign; check which convention a paper is using before rejecting such a conclusion.
key_note: Two drafting problems here. Options C and D are printed identically, and the third conclusion is in fact true: O > R > K and K is at least X, so O > X, which satisfies O at least X. With no 'II and III' choice on the list, 'only II' is the closest answer available, and the key follows the stricter setter habit of refusing a weak inequality drawn from a strict one.

short_explanation: BCC stands for blind carbon copy: an address placed there receives the message, but no other recipient can see that it was included.
explanation_text: The three address fields divide by visibility. To names the main recipients; CC, carbon copy, adds others and shows every address to everyone; BCC hides its recipients from all the rest. The wording survives from the carbon paper once used to make duplicate typed copies. In practice BCC is what stops a large mailing list from exposing every subscriber's address to every reader.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Basic carbon copy is not an email term.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Broad carbon copy is not an email term.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Backup carbon copy is not an email term.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Broadcast carbon copy is not an email term, even though BCC is often used for broadcasts.

short_explanation: Rozgar Diwas is held at least once a month at every ward and Gram Panchayat to tell rural households about MGNREGA entitlements: how to register, how to demand work and what they are owed if it is not given.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No Gram Chaupal Diwas is prescribed under MGNREGA; the monthly awareness day is Rozgar Diwas.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Gram Sahyog Diwas is an invented name.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Gram Saarthi Diwas is an invented name.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Gram Sahayak Diwas is an invented name.

short_explanation: The square root of 399.92 is about 20, a third of 18 is 6, and 12.053 × 1.97 is about 24, so the expression comes to 20 - 6 + 24 = 38.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No plausible rounding gives 35; the three parts are about 20, 6 and 24, which give 38.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 41 follows from taking a sixth of 18, which is 3, instead of the third that 33.33% means.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 44 drops the subtraction altogether and leaves 20 + 24.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: No plausible rounding gives 48; the working gives 38.

common_traps: 33.33% is one-third, not one-quarter or one-sixth.

topic_name: Census and demographic profile of India
short_explanation: The Economic Survey 2022-23 puts about 65 per cent of India's population in rural areas and 47 per cent dependent on agriculture for a livelihood, the pairing behind the Survey's argument for rural demand and farm incomes.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 55 per cent understates the rural share, and cottage industry supports nowhere near 47 per cent of the population.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 60 per cent understates the rural share, and forestry is a small livelihood base, not a 47 per cent one.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 70 per cent overstates the rural share on the Survey's own figure, and handloom is a narrow occupation.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 75 per cent overstates the rural share considerably, and khadi is a small sector.

common_traps: The rural share and the agriculture-dependent share are different numbers: about 65 per cent live in rural India, 47 per cent depend on farming. Not everyone in a village farms.

short_explanation: A method demonstration shows a group of farmers how to do something step by step - grafting a shoot, treating seed, calibrating a sprayer - so that they can repeat the skill themselves.
explanation_text: Extension teaching methods are sorted by audience and by purpose. A method demonstration teaches a skill: the worker performs each step in front of the group and the farmers practise it, and it is short and focused on how to do. A result demonstration differs in both length and message - the new practice is grown on a farmer's own field through a season beside the usual practice, and the point is to prove that it works here, not to teach the technique. Farm and home visits and office calls are individual contact methods; group discussion is a group method, but it exchanges opinion rather than demonstrating anything.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A result demonstration runs through a season on a farmer's field to prove a practice pays; it does not teach the steps.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Group discussion exchanges views and arrives at decisions; nothing is demonstrated.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A farm and home visit is an individual contact method, reaching one family at a time.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: An office call is also individual contact, made by the farmer visiting the extension office.

common_traps: Method demonstration teaches how to do it; result demonstration proves that it works.

short_explanation: In each conclusion the two letters come from different branches that meet only at G — P and Y both sit under G, H and A both sit under G, I and V both sit under G — so none of the three is fixed.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: P < Q = G on one side and Y = V < H, at most D, below G on the other put both under G with no link between them.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: H is below G through D, and A is below G directly; two separate branches under the same value fix no order.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: I is at most A, which is below G, and V is below H, which is also below G — again no connection.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Neither of the first two conclusions is established.

short_explanation: The clause concedes two pandemic years and still claims economic strength, so the blank takes a strong positive word: economically robust.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 'Economically mild' says nothing about strength and is not a normal collocation.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Lethargic means sluggish, which contradicts the record auction spend described in the next sentence.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Fragile is the opposite of what 'can cope with two pandemic years and still remain' sets up.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: 'Still remain' after a concession signals a positive word. 'Fragile' and 'lethargic' match the hardship rather than the survival.

topic_name: Long-term growth strategy and policy vision
short_explanation: In the August 2023 address 'Building Blocks for a Sustainable Future', the RBI Governor named six thrust areas for the next 25 years: agriculture, manufacturing, services, demography, technology and startups. Demography is the blank, meaning India's young working-age population treated as a growth lever rather than a headcount.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Artificial intelligence falls inside the 'technology' block already named in the list.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Mining was not one of the six areas.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Automobile is a sub-sector of manufacturing, not a separate thrust area in the speech.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Adding the three pair rates counts each worker twice: 1/30 + 1/15 + 1/40 = 1/8, so together they do 1/16 of the work a day and finish it all in 16 days — three-fourths takes 12.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 10 days; three-fourths of the 16-day whole is 12.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives 14 days; the working gives 12.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 16 days is the time for the whole work, which the question then cuts to three-fourths.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

solution_steps: A and B together do 1/30 of the work a day, B and C 1/15, A and C 1/40.
So A + B + C = 1/16 a day, and the whole work takes 16 days.
Three-fourths of it takes 16 × 3/4 = 12 days.
formula_used: Adding all three pairwise rates counts every worker twice, so halve the sum to get the combined rate.
common_traps: Only three-fourths of the work is asked for, not all of it.

short_explanation: M > F, F is at least E, and E equals U which is at least S which is above Q, so M > Q. J is at least U and S is at most U, so J is at least S. B and G meet only through E, so the third conclusion stays open.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The second conclusion also holds: J is at least U, and S is at most U, so J is at least S.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The first conclusion also holds: M > F, F is at least E = U, U is at least S, and S > Q.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: B > J, which is at least U = E, and G = M > F, which is at least E — both stand above the same value, so no order between B and G is fixed.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Both the first and the second conclusions are established.

short_explanation: The programme is the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission, announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 and launched from Shahdol in July 2023, targeting the tribal-majority districts where the disease is concentrated.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Sickle cell anaemia is a genetic haemoglobin disorder, not a nutritional deficiency, and no mission carries this name.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: An invented title; the mission is framed as an elimination mission, not a strategy document.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: An invented title.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The paragraph the stem points to is not carried in this row. The neighbouring rows of this set name the sickle cell mission and its 2047 target, and the row was answered from that shared premise.

short_explanation: Dangi is the dual-purpose cattle breed of the Nashik and Ahmednagar tract of Maharashtra, valued for working in heavy rainfall and hilly country as well as for milk.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Sahiwal is a milch breed of the Montgomery tract, now found mainly in Punjab and across the border.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Kankrej is dual purpose too, but it belongs to the Rann of Kutch tract of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Red Sindhi is a milch breed originating in Sindh.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Jersey is an exotic dairy breed from the Channel Islands, used in India for crossbreeding.

common_traps: Kankrej is also milch and draught; the Nashik-Ahmednagar origin is what identifies Dangi.

short_explanation: Surviving two pandemic years is called a pointer to the league's marketing viability — its ability to keep paying its way — alongside its strong financial underpinnings.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 'Terminate' is a verb; the slot after 'its marketing' needs a noun.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Discontinuity is a break in continuity, the opposite of what surviving two pandemic years demonstrates.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Functionality is used of whether a machine or a piece of software works; it is not used of a league's commercial standing.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: 'Functionality' is the only rival that is both a noun and positive, so the discriminator is collocation: viability is what a commercial proposition has, functionality is what a device has.

short_explanation: A stylus is a pen-shaped tool used directly on a touchscreen or graphics tablet, for precise selecting, writing and drawing.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Typing is the keyboard's job; a stylus can tap an on-screen keyboard, but that is not what it is for.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Moving a cursor from a desk surface is the mouse's job; a stylus works on the display itself.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Scanning documents is done by a scanner or a camera.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Printing is an output task, and no input device performs it.

common_traps: Moving the cursor sounds close, but it describes an indirect pointing device; a stylus points at the screen directly.

short_explanation: The writer corrects a round ₹552 crore to the exact ₹551.7 crore, and the set phrase for that correction is 'to be precise'.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 'To be relatively' is incomplete — the adverb needs something to be relative to.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 'To be roughly' would announce an approximation, but the figure that follows the blank is the exact one.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: The same fault in adjective form: the sentence moves from the round number towards the exact one, not away from it.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The blank follows the exact figure, not the round one, so the word must announce exactness rather than approximation.

topic_name: Generations of computers and hardware evolution
short_explanation: The transistor replaced the vacuum tube — far smaller, cooler, more reliable and using a fraction of the power — and defines the second generation of computers.
explanation_text: First-generation machines ran on vacuum tubes, which were bulky, burnt out often and threw off a great deal of heat. The transistor, invented at Bell Labs in 1947, did the same switching job in a fraction of the space and power, and gave the second generation its name. Integrated circuits then packed many transistors onto a single chip for the third generation, and the microprocessor put an entire processor on one chip for the fourth. Each of those builds on the transistor rather than replacing the tube directly.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The integrated circuit came later and packs transistors together; it solved the problem of wiring many transistors, not the problem of tubes.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The microprocessor is a fourth-generation step, further along the same line.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A cathode ray tube is a display device, and is itself a kind of vacuum tube.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: A diode conducts in one direction only and cannot switch signals the way a tube or a transistor does.

common_traps: Every option names a genuine milestone; the question asks which one directly answered the tube's failings, which is the very next step and not the later ones.

short_explanation: A broiler is a young meat-type chicken marketed at about 1.5 to 2 kg live weight in six to seven weeks, with tender meat and a pliable breast bone.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Layers are birds kept for egg production, not raised for tender meat.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: A chick is a newly hatched bird of either type.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: A grower is a bird in the intermediate rearing stage of an egg-type flock.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: A hen is an adult female bird, usually a spent layer, and her meat is tough.

short_explanation: Neither statement settles the top floor alone, but together M on an odd floor immediately above K forces K onto 4 and M onto 5, J onto 2, L onto 3 and I three floors away on 6.
explanation_text: From the second statement on its own, L on an odd floor with two floors between L and I allows L on 1 with I on 4, L on 3 with I on 6, or L on 5 with I on 2, and the top floor changes with each. The first statement on its own only keeps M off even floors and J off floor 6. Put the two together: M is odd and sits immediately above K, so K is even, giving either K on 2 with M on 3 or K on 4 with M on 5. If K is on 2 and M on 3, J has to take 4, and the odd floors left for L are 1 and 5, neither of which leaves a free floor three away for I. So K is on 4, M on 5 and J on 2; L takes 3, I takes 6 and N takes 1. I lives at the top.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The first statement leaves M anywhere among floors 1, 3 and 5 and J on either 2 or 4, with floor 6 still unassigned.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The second statement allows three different L-and-I pairings, each putting a different person on top.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Neither statement reaches the answer by itself, so 'either one alone' fails.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Taken together they do settle it: I lives on floor 6.

common_traps: The stem already announces that the second statement alone is not sufficient; the work left is to test the first alone and then the two in combination.

short_explanation: The Global Biofuel Alliance, launched at the New Delhi G20 summit in September 2023, is meant to speed up India's existing biofuel programmes: PM JI-VAN for second-generation ethanol, SATAT for compressed biogas offtake and GOBARdhan for biogas from cattle waste. PM-KUSUM is a solar programme and sits outside biofuels.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Carries PM KUSUM, which is solar pumps and grid-connected solar for farmers, not a biofuel programme.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Carries PM KUSUM and drops PM JI-VAN, the flagship second-generation ethanol scheme.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Carries PM KUSUM and drops SATAT, the compressed biogas offtake programme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: PM-KUSUM is the odd one out, solar rather than bio. Every wrong option here is built by slipping it in.

short_explanation: Article A cost ₹4,500 and sold at a 20% loss for ₹3,600; that ₹3,600 bought article B, which sold at 30% profit for ₹4,680 — ₹180 above the original outlay.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives ₹120; the 0.8 then 1.3 chain gives a 4% gain on ₹4,500, which is ₹180.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives ₹150; the working gives ₹180.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: No likely slip gives ₹200; ₹180 is exactly 4% of ₹4,500.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

solution_steps: Selling price of A = 4,500 × 0.8 = ₹3,600, a loss of ₹900.
Cost of B = ₹3,600; selling price of B = 3,600 × 1.3 = ₹4,680, a profit of ₹1,080.
Money spent at the start = ₹4,500; money in hand at the end = ₹4,680.
Overall gain = 4,680 - 4,500 = ₹180, which is the 4% that 0.8 × 1.3 = 1.04 promises on ₹4,500.
formula_used: Overall factor = (1 - loss rate) × (1 + profit rate); overall gain = original cost × (factor - 1).
common_traps: The 30% profit is taken on the ₹3,600 actually spent on article B, not on article A's ₹4,500 cost price.

short_explanation: All three are part of the mission's preventive arm: screening and testing at scale, awareness work including pre-marital genetic counselling, and strengthened laboratory services for confirmatory diagnosis.
explanation_text: Pre-marital counselling is the piece that looks unusual and is in fact central. Sickle cell disease is recessive: where both parents carry the trait, each child has a one in four chance of the full disease and a one in two chance of being a carrier. Telling a carrier that they are one, before marriage, is the cheapest prevention available. Screening runs through point-of-care solubility tests in the field, confirmed by electrophoresis or HPLC in a laboratory, with results recorded on a sickle cell card the person carries.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Drops laboratory strengthening, which the mission funds precisely because field screening needs confirmatory testing behind it.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Drops the screening and testing leg, which is the mission's largest single activity.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Drops awareness and pre-marital genetic counselling, the preventive step that stops new cases being born.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This says exactly what the keyed option says. Where a paper carries such a duplicate, the option that lists the statements explicitly is the safer pick.

key_note: Options D and E are logically identical, which is a drafting defect in the paper. The key takes the explicit list.

short_explanation: A layer flock stays economical for about 18 months of lay - roughly 72 to 80 weeks of age - after which egg numbers and shell quality fall and the birds are culled.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: At 9 months of lay the flock is still in good production and would not be culled.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 10 months would mean culling birds near their peak persistency.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 11 months is still well inside the profitable laying period.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 12 months of lay falls short of the 72-80 week figure normally used for culling.

key_note: Farms differ with strain and egg price, and many force-moult instead of culling; the 18-month figure corresponds to the usual 72-80 week culling age.

short_explanation: The first statement narrows P to U or X, and the second says only that B is in one of those same two places — which of the pair falls to P is still open, so even together they fall short.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The first statement rules out W and hands Y and V to K and I, but U and X both stay open for P.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The second statement says nothing at all about P.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Neither statement settles the question by itself.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Even combined, P and B are left sharing the same two places with nothing to separate them.

key_note: The stem calls the places countries while listing U, V, W, X and Y as cities; the loose wording does not affect the sufficiency test.

short_explanation: The All-India Index of Industrial Production covers three sectors: mining, manufacturing and electricity. Gas and water supply are not part of it.
explanation_text: The IIP has a 2011-12 base and manufacturing dominates it, carrying roughly 77.6 per cent of the weight against about 14.4 per cent for mining and 8 per cent for electricity. Alongside that sectoral cut the index is also published on a use-based classification: primary goods, capital goods, intermediate goods, infrastructure and construction goods, consumer durables and consumer non-durables. That second cut is what analysts read for the state of investment demand versus household demand.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Carries gas and water supply, which the index excludes, and drops electricity, which it includes.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Carries gas and water supply and drops mining.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Carries gas and water supply and drops manufacturing, the largest component by far.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: The stem still calls the compiling agency the CSO. Since the 2019 merger of the CSO and the NSSO, the IIP is released by the National Statistical Office.

short_explanation: Franchises spend at an auction to strengthen their squads, and 'bolster' is the verb regularly used for reinforcing a team with added players.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Undermine means to weaken — the opposite of what spending ₹552 crore on players achieves.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Enhance means to improve the quality of something and is normally used of a quality or an experience, not of adding players to a squad.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Validate means to confirm that something is sound; a squad is not validated by buying a bouquet of players.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: 'Enhance' is the closest rival and is not wrong in tone. 'Bolster' is preferred because it means to add strength or support, which is precisely what buying players with varied skill sets does to a squad.

short_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 hold: the first phase screens the zero to 18 age group through schools and anganwadis, and the mission targets about 7 crore people for screening and counselling over three and a half years. Statement 2 fails on its number.
explanation_text: The mission runs inside the National Health Mission across 17 high-burden States, mostly with large tribal populations, and widens outward from the school-age cohort to the full zero to 40 year band, not 45. The three activities it funds are awareness with pre-marital counselling, universal screening of that cohort, and continued care through a card-based follow-up record. The elimination goal is 2047.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Carries statement 2, whose age ceiling of 45 is wrong; the mission's band runs to 40 years.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Carries statement 2 and drops statement 1, the currently screened cohort.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Adds statement 2 to the two correct ones; the 45-year ceiling is what fails.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: This says the same as option D and therefore carries the same wrong age ceiling.

key_note: Statement 2 fails only on the number: the mission incrementally covers up to 40 years, not 45. Options D and E are also duplicates of each other, a drafting defect.

short_explanation: T holds 24% of 8,000, which is 1,920 people, and a quarter of them are female — 480, the largest female count of the five.
explanation_text: Build the table once and the whole set falls out of it. Populations: P is 18.5% of 8,000 = 1,480, Q 1,640, R 1,360, S 1,600 and T 1,920. Applying each male percentage leaves the female counts: P has 30% of 1,480 = 444, Q 15% of 1,640 = 246, R 35% of 1,360 = 476, S 12% of 1,600 = 192 and T 25% of 1,920 = 480. The male counts are 1,036, 1,394, 884, 1,408 and 1,440, which come to 6,162 in all.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: P has 444 females.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Q has only 246 females, because 85% of it is male.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: R has 476 females — the runner-up, just 4 short of T.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: S has 192 females, the fewest of the five, because 88% of it is male.

solution_steps: Females in P = 1,480 × 30% = 444.
Females in Q = 1,640 × 15% = 246.
Females in R = 1,360 × 35% = 476.
Females in S = 1,600 × 12% = 192.
Females in T = 1,920 × 25% = 480, the largest of the five.
formula_used: Count in a group = total population × group's population share × that group's percentage.
common_traps: R carries the largest female share at 35% but a small population; T wins on a quarter of a much bigger 1,920, and only by 4 people.
key_note: The pie-chart block is shared by six questions; the full population-male-female table is worked once here and used for the rest of the set.

short_explanation: R sits between N and M, and since N is the ivory person and ivory sits next to navy, navy is R's colour.
explanation_text: Reading round the table in the direction each seated person's left hand points, the order is M, P, O, Q, S, T, N, R and back to M. M likes lavender and sits immediately to R's left, which anchors the pair; Q is three seats further along from M in the same direction. S sits two seats to N's right and P sits immediately to O's right, and the only fit that also places an ivory-liking person directly opposite O is N — S is barred from ivory. Maroon must have two people between itself and T, which lands on O, and that is allowed because the clue only bars P, Q and R from maroon. The emerald person, one seat clear of Q, cannot be P, so emerald is T. Navy, the colour beside ivory, therefore falls to R. Cyan then sits immediately to ebony's left, giving S cyan and Q ebony, and amber is left for P.

option_rationales.label: B

option_rationales.rationale: Cyan belongs to S, who sits immediately to the left of the ebony person Q.

option_rationales.label: E

key_note: Solved once for this whole set of four questions from the shared direction block. Mirroring the table left for right gives another arrangement with all the same answers, since every clue is relational.

topic_name: Printers, printing metrics and display hardware
short_explanation: Laser printers are the office standard for bulk work — fast page rates, a low cost per page and large paper trays.
