short_explanation: Segment (b) reads 'a meeting by the leader of', but four countries are listed and four countries have four leaders, so it must be 'a meeting of the leaders of'.
explanation_text: A noun governed by a list of possessors takes the plural: the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the U.S.; the governors of the four States; the capitals of the member countries. The singular is right only when the office is genuinely shared by all of them, which is not the case here.

short_explanation: Certified seed carries a blue, or azure blue, tag issued by the State Seed Certification Agency.
explanation_text: The seed chain runs breeder to foundation to certified, each class raised from the one above under progressively wider but still controlled standards. Breeder seed carries a golden yellow tag issued by the producing institution, foundation seed a white tag, and certified seed a blue tag from the state certification agency. Truthfully labelled seed, which is not certified but is guaranteed by the producer, carries an opal green label. The tag colour is the quickest check of what class a bag actually holds.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Red is not a seed class tag colour in the Indian system.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Opal green marks truthfully labelled seed, which the producer guarantees without certification.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Golden yellow is the breeder seed tag; foundation seed is white.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Pink is not used in the Indian seed certification tag scheme.

common_traps: Golden yellow for breeder, white for foundation, blue for certified, opal green for truthfully labelled - the four are easy to shuffle.

short_explanation: Adolescent fertility rate and the share of own-account workers by sex are both sex-disaggregated measures and sit in the MoSPI list of gender-relevant indicators; the share of households using clean cooking fuel is measured at household level with no breakdown by sex.

topic_name: Pioneers and landmarks in computing history
short_explanation: John Atanasoff, working with Clifford Berry at Iowa State between 1937 and 1942, built the Atanasoff-Berry Computer, the first machine to compute electronically using vacuum tubes and binary arithmetic.
explanation_text: Credit here turns on a court case. For decades ENIAC, completed in 1945 by John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert, was called the first electronic computer. In 1973 the ruling in Honeywell v. Sperry Rand invalidated the ENIAC patent and held that its inventors had drawn on Atanasoff's earlier work, which placed the Atanasoff-Berry Computer first. The ABC was not programmable and solved only systems of linear equations, so ENIAC still holds the title of first general-purpose electronic computer.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Charles Xavier is not a figure in computing; the name echoes Charles Babbage, who designed mechanical calculating engines a century earlier.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: John Mauchly co-built ENIAC in 1945, which the 1973 ruling placed after Atanasoff's machine.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Alan Turing supplied the theory of computation and worked on wartime code-breaking machines, but is not credited with the first electronic computer.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976, long after electronic computing began.

common_traps: Mauchly and ENIAC are the older textbook answer; current keys follow the 1973 ruling in Atanasoff's favour.
key_note: The Mauchly reading is defensible on the older convention and is still keyed that way in some papers, so it is worth carrying both.

Here 'requested the Karnataka High Court on Monday' fixes the past, so the petitioning cannot sit in the present simple. Leaving it in the present turns the girls into habitual petitioners rather than the petitioners in this particular case.

short_explanation: Acacia catechu, the khair tree that yields katha and cutch, belongs to the family Fabaceae or Leguminosae; Mimosoideae is its subfamily within that family.

short_explanation: A saline soil has pH below 8.5 - in practice about 7 to 8.5 - with electrical conductivity above 4 dS/m, which is what the key's 4< stands for.
explanation_text: Salt-affected soils are separated by three measurements. A saline soil has EC above 4 dS/m, pH under 8.5 and exchangeable sodium percentage under 15; the salts are neutral chlorides and sulphates, the clay stays flocculated, and reclamation is by leaching with good water plus drainage. A sodic or alkali soil has EC under 4 dS/m, pH above 8.5 and ESP above 15; here sodium disperses the clay, so gypsum is applied to replace the sodium before leaching. A saline-sodic soil crosses both the EC and the ESP limit. Reading the wrong row gets both the diagnosis and the treatment wrong.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: pH 6 to 5 is acidic, and an EC below 4 dS/m is not saline at all.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: This reverses the inequality - with EC below 4 dS/m the soil is normal or sodic, not saline.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: pH 6 to 7 with low EC describes an ordinary soil that is not salt affected.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The paper writes the EC condition as 4< for above 4 and 4> for below 4; reading the sign the other way lands on option B.
key_note: The inequality notation in the options is sloppy. The key is read as EC greater than 4 dS/m with pH below 8.5, which is the standard definition of a saline soil.

short_explanation: CD-R is Compact Disc-Recordable: a blank disc that can be written once and afterwards only read.
explanation_text: The three related formats separate cleanly. CD-ROM is read-only memory, pressed at the factory and never written by the user. CD-R is recordable — a laser burns the dye layer once, after which the disc is permanent. CD-RW is rewritable, using a phase-change layer that can be erased and written again many times over.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Compact Disc-Read is not a format name; the read-only disc is CD-ROM.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: ReWritable is CD-RW, a different disc that can be erased and written again.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Random Access Memory is not what the letters hold; CD-ROM stands for Read Only Memory.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Write Once Read Many describes how a CD-R behaves, but WORM is a separate term and not the expansion of the R.

common_traps: Option E states a true property of the disc while giving the wrong expansion; the question asks what the letters stand for.

short_explanation: R is the navy one, and the seat straight across the eight-seat table from R belongs to Q.

explanation_text: When a noun such as warning, claim, assurance or ruling is followed by a that-clause giving its content, the party who made it is marked with the possessive: the government's warning, the court's ruling, the bank's assurance. Without the apostrophe, 'government' reads as a bare modifier and the phrase loses its owner.

option_rationales.label: B

topic_name: International economic forums and summit declarations
short_explanation: The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration groups its gender commitments under four heads: economic and social empowerment, bridging the gender digital divide, gender-inclusive climate action, and women's food security, nutrition and well-being. Raising women's political representation worldwide is not one of them.
explanation_text: The declaration's framing is 'women-led development' rather than women as beneficiaries, and the institutional follow-through was the creation of a Working Group on Empowerment of Women, carried forward under the Brazilian presidency. Political representation stayed out of the text, which is consistent with the G20's practice of avoiding commitments that touch member states' domestic electoral arrangements.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Carries item 3 on political leadership and drops item 1 on economic and social empowerment, the first of the four heads.

short_explanation: Cultivation in tracts receiving 750 to 1,150 mm of rainfall a year is called dryland agriculture; crop failure here is occasional rather than routine, and moisture conservation is the central practice.
explanation_text: The three terms are separated by annual rainfall and by how often the crop fails. Dry farming is practised below 750 mm, where the growing season is short and failure is frequent, so every operation is bent towards conserving moisture. Dryland farming covers 750 to 1,150 mm, where a full crop is usually possible and disposing of excess water in wet spells matters as much as conserving it. Rainfed farming applies above 1,150 mm, where rainfall exceeds crop need and drainage and erosion control become the problem. All three are unirrigated.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Rainfed agriculture is the term used above 1,150 mm, where excess water and drainage are the issue.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Dry agriculture, or dry farming, applies below 750 mm, where crop failure is frequent.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Dried agriculture is not a recognised category.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: 750 mm and 1,150 mm are the two cut-offs: dry farming below, dryland between, rainfed above.

short_explanation: Salinization is the accumulation of soluble salts, sodium among them, in the soil profile - typically where a high water table or poor quality irrigation water brings salts up and evaporation leaves them behind.
explanation_text: Three soil-forming processes are easy to confuse here. Salinization is the build-up of soluble salts in the profile, usual in arid and semi-arid tracts and under canal irrigation with inadequate drainage. Solonization, also called alkalization or sodication, is the specific accumulation of sodium on the exchange complex, which disperses clay and pushes pH above 8.5. Solodization is its reverse - sodium leaves the exchange complex and hydrogen replaces it, degrading the sodic horizon. Reclamation is not a natural process at all but the remedy: leaching for saline soils, gypsum followed by leaching for sodic ones.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Reclamation is the corrective operation - leaching, or gypsum application - and is the opposite of accumulation.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Solodization is the removal of sodium from the exchange complex, not its build-up.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Humification is the conversion of plant residues into humus, an organic matter process.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Decomposition is the breakdown of organic residues and has nothing to do with salt movement.

common_traps: Solodization sounds like solonization but means the opposite - sodium leaving rather than accumulating.
key_note: Strictly, sodium accumulating on the exchange complex is sodication or solonization, while salinization names the accumulation of soluble salts generally; among the options offered, salinization is the only accumulation process.

short_explanation: The four-tiered regulatory framework RBI put in place from 2022, following the Vijay Bhaskar expert committee, applies to urban cooperative banks: they are grouped by deposit size and capital and exposure norms scale with the tier.
explanation_text: The tiers run by deposits: Tier 1 covers unit UCBs and banks with deposits up to 100 crore rupees; Tier 2 from 100 crore to 1,000 crore; Tier 3 from 1,000 crore to 10,000 crore; Tier 4 above 10,000 crore. Minimum capital to risk-weighted assets is 9 per cent for Tier 1 and 12 per cent for Tiers 2 to 4. The point of the design is proportionality: a small single-branch society should not carry the same compliance load as a large multi-state UCB, while the large ones move closer to commercial bank norms.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Payment banks are licensed under a separate differentiated-bank framework with their own deposit cap, not a four-tier structure.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Private banks are regulated as scheduled commercial banks; no tiering of this kind applies to them.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Regional Rural Banks have their own sponsor-bank and capital framework, not this four-tier one.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Foreign banks in India are regulated through branch and wholly-owned-subsidiary modes, not by deposit tiers.

short_explanation: DAP, di-ammonium phosphate at 18-46-0, is a complex fertilizer - nitrogen and phosphorus are chemically combined in the same compound, not merely mixed together.
explanation_text: Fertilizers are grouped by how many nutrients they carry and how those nutrients got there. A straight fertilizer supplies one primary nutrient: urea with 46 per cent N, single super phosphate with 16 per cent P2O5 plus calcium and sulphur, muriate of potash with 60 per cent K2O. A complex fertilizer is manufactured so that two or more nutrients are chemically combined in every granule, so each granule carries the same analysis - DAP, and NPK grades such as 10-26-26 and 12-32-16. A mixed fertilizer is only a physical blend of straight fertilizers, so its granules can segregate in the bag. That is the practical difference: a complex cannot be separated by handling.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Single super phosphate supplies phosphorus, with calcium and sulphur, and is a straight phosphatic fertilizer.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Urea, spelt Uera in the paper, is a straight nitrogenous fertilizer carrying 46 per cent N.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Muriate of potash supplies potassium alone and is a straight potassic fertilizer.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The other three are straight fertilizers, so all of the above fails.

short_explanation: Bank loans to food and agro-processing units count as agriculture under priority sector lending, in the 'ancillary activities' leg, up to an aggregate limit of 100 crore rupees per borrower.
explanation_text: PSL agriculture has three legs. Farm credit is direct lending to farmers and to farmer groups. Agriculture infrastructure covers storage, cold chain and soil testing, capped at 100 crore rupees per borrower. Ancillary activities cover food and agro-processing up to 100 crore rupees per borrower, loans to cooperatives of farmers, and credit to input dealers. For domestic scheduled commercial banks the overall PSL target is 40 per cent of adjusted net bank credit, of which 18 per cent is for agriculture.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Export credit is its own PSL category with its own ceiling; it is not an agriculture ancillary activity.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Social infrastructure, such as schools and drinking water facilities, is a separate PSL category.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Renewable energy is a separate PSL category with a much smaller per-borrower limit.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: MSME is a separate PSL category; a food processing unit may also be an MSME, but the 100 crore ancillary limit is written under agriculture.

short_explanation: In relay intercropping the next crop is sown into the standing previous crop before it is harvested, so their life cycles overlap for part of the season and more crops fit into the year.
explanation_text: Intercropping types differ in how the component crops are laid out and timed. Mixed intercropping scatters two crops together with no row arrangement. Row intercropping grows them in a definite row pattern, as in a 2:1 pigeonpea and groundnut layout. Strip intercropping uses strips wide enough for separate machinery but narrow enough for the crops to interact. Multistorey cropping stacks crops of different heights, as with coconut, banana, pepper and pineapple on the same land. Relay intercropping is the only one defined by timing rather than space - the next crop is sown into the standing earlier one, as lathyrus is broadcast into standing paddy in the utera system.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Mixed intercropping grows the crops together with no row arrangement; they are sown at the same time, not in relay.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Row intercropping is defined by its row pattern, with the crops again sown together.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Strip intercropping uses strips wide enough for independent cultivation, sown in the same period.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Multistorey cropping stacks canopies of different heights; it is defined by space, not by overlap in time.

short_explanation: Pruning removes weak, crowded, dead or badly placed wood so that the plant puts its resources into a limited number of strong, healthy shoots.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Pruning does not simply encourage blooming; heavy pruning can delay flowering, which depends on the type of wood the species bears on.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Regulating flowering and fruiting is an outcome pruning is sometimes used for, and standard texts list it too - see the key note - but the key takes the direct objective.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Removing dead and diseased wood does limit disease spread, but recover potential mortality is not a standard statement of the objective.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Total growth is reduced rather than improved, since leaf area is cut; what improves is the vigour of the shoots left behind.

key_note: Regulation of flowering and fruiting, which option C names, is also listed as an objective of pruning in standard horticulture texts; the key treats the production of strong healthy shoots as the primary one.

short_explanation: Polyculture is raising more than one fish species together in the same pond, chosen so that they feed at different levels - surface, column and bottom - and use the whole water body.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Monoculture stocks a single species in the pond.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Mixed culture generally means stocking different sizes or age groups, rather than the planned combination of feeding habits that defines polyculture.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Monosex culture stocks one sex of a single species, common in tilapia to stop unwanted breeding.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Multisex culture is not a recognised aquaculture system.

short_explanation: Skills on Wheels, launched in September 2023 by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship with NSDC and IndusInd Bank, takes mobile training units into rural areas and aims to skill 60,000 young people over five years.

short_explanation: Krishi Vigyan Kendras came out of the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee of 1973, which ICAR set up to design a farm-level vocational training institution; the first KVK opened at Puducherry in 1974.
explanation_text: A KVK is a district-level farm science centre funded by ICAR and hosted by a state agricultural university, an NGO or a state department. Its mandate is not general extension but on-farm testing of technologies, frontline demonstrations and training of farmers and extension workers, with the district as the unit. The examinable part is keeping the three Mehta committees apart: Mohan Singh Mehta on farmers' education and the KVK, Balwant Rai Mehta on democratic decentralisation and the three-tier panchayati raj, and Ashok Mehta on the later review of panchayati raj.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee of 1957 recommended democratic decentralisation and the three-tier panchayati raj structure.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Ashok Mehta Committee of 1977 reviewed panchayati raj and proposed a two-tier structure.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Only one of the three committees dealt with the KVK, so all of the above fails.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: Three committees are named Mehta; only Mohan Singh Mehta relates to the KVK.

short_explanation: The Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure sub-scheme of ISAM, which gives back-ended subsidy for storage and market infrastructure, has been approved to continue up to 31 March 2026 for projects whose term loan is sanctioned on or after 1 April 2023.
explanation_text: AMI works through credit, not grant: the promoter takes a term loan from a bank, NABARD or NCDC, and the subsidy is released to the lender and adjusted against the loan once the project is built and inspected. The rate is 25 per cent of eligible project cost in general and 33.33 per cent for the North Eastern and hill States, and for SC and ST promoters, registered farmer producer organisations, women and cooperatives. Godowns, cold storage, grading and packing units and rural haats are the typical projects.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2024 falls inside the extended period, not at its end.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2025 falls inside the extended period.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 2027 runs past the approved continuation date.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2028 runs well past the approved continuation date.

short_explanation: The passage gives LIC a 66.2 per cent share in new business premiums, 74.6 per cent in individual policies issued and 81.1 per cent in group policies, so only statement I matches; II and III swap the two policy figures.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: III attaches 81.1 per cent to individual policies, but the passage gives that figure to group policies.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: I is right, but II gives 74.6 per cent for group policies when the passage assigns it to individual policies.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Both statements have the individual and group figures interchanged.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: I is right; III moves the 81.1 per cent from group policies to individual policies.

common_traps: Both wrong statements use figures that really appear in the passage — only the category attached to each has been switched.

short_explanation: Seed propagation is the commonest and easiest way to raise forest planting stock - seed is cheap to collect, store and transport, and large nursery numbers can be raised from it.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Seed propagation does produce variability, because seedlings arise from sexual reproduction and segregate.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: True-to-type plants come from vegetative propagation - cuttings, grafts and layers - not from seed.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Two of the three statements are wrong, so all of the above cannot hold.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The wood-based artisan and the traditional toy maker both work in trades on the scheme's list of 18. The tailor is out because her husband is a government servant, and PM Vishwakarma bars government employees and their family members.
explanation_text: Eligibility turns on four tests. The applicant must be 18 or older on the date of registration; must be self-employed in the unorganised sector working with hands and tools in one of the 18 listed family-based trades; only one member per family may register, and 'family' means husband, wife and unmarried children; and anyone who has taken a similar credit-linked government loan such as PMEGP, PM SVANidhi or Mudra in the last five years is excluded. Government servants and their family members are excluded outright.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Carries the tailor, who is disqualified by her husband's government job, and drops the toy maker, who is eligible.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Carries the tailor and drops the wood artisan.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Adds the tailor to the two eligible artisans.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The government-service bar reaches family members, not just the employee. That is what disqualifies the tailor, not her trade, which is on the list.

short_explanation: The technical group on population projections puts half of the 31.1 crore increase between 2011 and 2036 in five States: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh. Andhra Pradesh is not among them.
explanation_text: The split is a fertility story. The southern States, Andhra Pradesh included, reached replacement-level fertility well before the national average, so their populations grow now mainly from age structure rather than from births, and their share of the projected national increase is small. The northern and eastern States with later fertility decline account for most of it. This is the arithmetic behind the delimitation and tax-devolution debates: the States that slowed their growth fastest stand to lose relative weight.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Uttar Pradesh is the largest single contributor to the projected increase and is among the five.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Bihar has the highest total fertility rate among the large States and is among the five.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: West Bengal is among the five States named in the projection.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Maharashtra is among the five, driven as much by in-migration as by natural increase.

common_traps: The stem asks which State is NOT among the five. A hurried reader picks a State that is.

short_explanation: Under RBI's priority sector norms agriculture carries a target of 18 per cent of adjusted net bank credit, sitting inside the overall 40 per cent priority sector target for domestic scheduled commercial banks.
explanation_text: Priority sector targets are set as a share of adjusted net bank credit or of the credit equivalent of off-balance-sheet exposure, whichever is higher. For domestic scheduled commercial banks the overall target is 40 per cent, agriculture 18 per cent, micro enterprises 7.5 per cent and weaker sections 12 per cent. Inside the 18 per cent for agriculture sits a separate sub-target for small and marginal farmers, raised in stages to 10 per cent of ANBC by 2023-24. Shortfalls against these targets are deposited with NABARD, largely in the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund - which is how RIDF is funded in the first place.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 13 per cent is not a priority sector target figure.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 15 per cent is not one of the RBI targets; 12 per cent is the weaker sections figure.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 16 per cent does not correspond to any priority sector target.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 17 per cent is close to the agriculture target but is not the figure RBI has set.

common_traps: 18 per cent is the agriculture target; the small and marginal farmer sub-target is 10 per cent of ANBC, which is not offered here.
key_note: Read strictly, the sub-target for small and marginal farmers is 10 per cent of ANBC for 2023-24, a value absent from the options. The item is answerable only as the overall agriculture target of 18 per cent, which is how the key reads it.

short_explanation: The passage measures the ceding of space by growth rates: between 2015-16 and 2020-21 private life insurers' premiums grew at 18 per cent while LIC's grew at 9 per cent.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The passage credits no innovative technique to private players; it gives only the two growth numbers.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 'Failed to maintain' overstates it — LIC's premiums still grew, only more slowly than the private sector's.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Nothing inverse is described; both sets of premiums rose, one faster than the other.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: The National Overseas Scholarship for SCs funds study abroad at Master's and PhD level only, so the PhD aspirant and the master's in science aspirant both qualify; an undergraduate course is outside the scheme whatever the applicant's income.
explanation_text: The scheme, run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, awards a limited number of slots each year, with sub-quotas reserved for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic tribes, landless agricultural labourers and traditional artisans. Total family income must not exceed 8 lakh rupees a year, raised from 6 lakh in 2022. It covers tuition, maintenance and airfare. Since 2021-22 it sits inside the SHREYAS umbrella alongside Top Class Education, Free Coaching and the National Fellowship.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Carries the undergraduate applicant. The course level, not the income, is what rules that case out.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Carries the undergraduate applicant and drops the PhD aspirant, who is squarely eligible.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Adds the undergraduate applicant to the two eligible ones.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: The income in statement 2 is inside the 8 lakh ceiling, so the case reads as eligible. It fails on the level of study, not on money.

short_explanation: Jan Shikshan Sansthans run vocational training for non-literates, neo-literates and school dropouts in the 15 to 45 year age group, with the 70, 20 and 10 per cent split across those groups and graduates.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 16 to 42 narrows the band at both ends and matches no scheme guideline.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 17 to 48 is arbitrary.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 18 to 50 raises the entry age; the scheme deliberately starts at 15 to reach recent school dropouts.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 21 to 60 is far outside the band and would exclude the dropouts the scheme targets.

topic_name: Rural land records and property rights
short_explanation: SVAMITVA, Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas, drone-maps the inhabited abadi part of a village and issues property cards that give household owners a recorded legal title.
explanation_text: Rural India has long had land records for farmland but often none for the house sites inside the village. SVAMITVA, run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj with the Survey of India, closes that gap. A recorded title does two things: it settles boundary disputes that otherwise sit in court for years, and it turns the house into collateral a household can borrow against. It also gives the Gram Panchayat a property base it can levy on.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: SMILE is the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise scheme, for transgender persons and people engaged in begging.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: DAY-NRLM organises rural women into self-help groups for livelihoods; it does not deal with land titles.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: PMAY-Gramin builds new houses; it does not confer recorded title on existing ones.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: AMRUT 2.0 is an urban water supply and sewerage mission.

short_explanation: The passage says plainly that continued government interference in LIC's decision making will affect the corporation's prospects, and points to the steep discounts public sector companies trade at as evidence of the pattern.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The passage says the opposite about growth: India's low insurance density 'indicates scope for growth'.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Investment decisions are mentioned as something a listing would open to public scrutiny, not as the thing that will damage prospects.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: It pairs the correct statement with A, which the passage contradicts.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: Under PMFBY the threshold yield is the average yield of the past seven years, leaving out notified calamity years, multiplied by the indemnity level notified for that crop.
explanation_text: The indemnity level is the share of normal yield the scheme guarantees - 70, 80 or 90 per cent, notified crop by crop according to risk. Multiplying the seven-year moving average yield by that level gives the threshold yield, the benchmark against which the season's actual yield, measured by crop cutting experiments, is compared. If the actual yield falls short, the claim is the shortfall as a fraction of the threshold yield, applied to the sum insured. Dropping calamity years from the average keeps the benchmark from sinking after a run of bad seasons.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Production is total output from an area, not a factor that can be applied to an average yield.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Productivity is yield per unit area - the quantity being multiplied, not the multiplier.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Threshold level is not a defined PMFBY parameter; the product of average yield and indemnity level is the threshold yield.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Yield is again the quantity being adjusted rather than the factor applied to it.

common_traps: Threshold yield is the result; indemnity level is the multiplier that produces it.

short_explanation: In the passage 'garner' means to gather or collect — the government 'has only been able to garner Rs 12,030 crore'. Of the options only 'dissolve' moves the other way, breaking something up instead of gathering it in.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Congregate means to come together in a crowd, a synonym rather than an antonym.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Collect is the plain synonym of garner.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Gather is the closest synonym of all.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: An antonym is present among the options, so this cannot be chosen.

common_traps: The stem asks for the antonym. Three of the five options are synonyms, placed there for a reader who skims the question.
key_note: 'Disperse' or 'scatter' would be the cleaner antonym of garner; 'dissolve' earns the key by elimination, since congregate, collect and gather are all synonyms.

short_explanation: The Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme, announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 with an outlay of Rs 2,200 crore, sets up clean plant centres to supply virus-free, quality planting material for high value horticultural crops.
explanation_text: Indian horticulture loses heavily to viruses carried in the planting material itself, particularly in grape, citrus, apple and banana, where a farmer who replants infected stock carries the problem into the next cycle. The Clean Plant Programme, run under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, funds clean plant centres that index mother plants for viruses, hold disease-free foundation stock and certify the nurseries that multiply from it. The Rs 2,200 crore outlay and the 2023-24 Budget are the facts examiners ask for; the mechanism - certified virus-free mother stock - is what makes the scheme make sense.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The National Agricultural Development Scheme is the English name commonly used for Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana, a state-plan funding scheme, not this programme.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Green Revolution Horticulture Initiative is not the name of an Indian scheme.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Sustainable Horticulture Enhancement Project is not an announced programme.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Integrated Crop Management Program is not the Budget 2023-24 announcement referred to here.

short_explanation: e-NAM, launched in 2016, networks APMC mandis onto one online trading platform so a lot assayed in one yard can be bid for by traders elsewhere, widening price discovery beyond the local market.
explanation_text: e-NAM does not replace the physical mandi; it layers electronic trading on top of it. A State must first amend its APMC Act on three counts before its mandis can join: allow electronic trading, issue a single unified trading licence valid across the State, and levy market fee at a single point. Assaying facilities at the yard are what make remote bidding possible, since a buyer who cannot see the lot must be able to trust its grade. SFAC is the lead implementing agency.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: An APMC is the statutory market committee running a physical mandi, not a trading portal.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: GeM is the Government e-Marketplace for public procurement of goods and services.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: APEDA promotes exports of agricultural and processed food products.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: IARI is an agricultural research institute.

short_explanation: Hydration is the chemical weathering process in which whole water molecules are taken into a mineral's structure, as when anhydrite becomes gypsum or haematite becomes limonite; the mineral swells and the rock weakens.
explanation_text: The water-related weathering processes are easy to swap. In hydration the water molecule enters the mineral intact, the volume increases and the rock crumbles under the strain. In hydrolysis the water molecule splits and its hydrogen ion exchanges with a cation in the mineral - the reaction that turns feldspar into clay minerals and is the main route by which clay forms in soil. Oxidation adds oxygen, turning ferrous iron into ferric and giving well drained soils their red and yellow colours.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: In hydrolysis the water molecule dissociates and its hydrogen ion replaces a cation; the molecule is not added whole.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Decomposition is the umbrella term for chemical weathering as a whole, not this particular reaction.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Combination is not a standard named weathering process.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen, as when ferrous iron in a mineral is converted to ferric.

common_traps: Hydration takes the water molecule in whole; hydrolysis splits it. The two words differ by a syllable.

short_explanation: Grading is sorting produce into classes by size, colour, shape and quality against a defined standard, which is what lets a lot be priced and sold by description rather than by inspection.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Processing changes the form of the produce - milling, pulping, drying - rather than sorting it.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Packaging protects and presents the produce after it has been graded.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Threshing separates the grain from the ear or pod.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Transporting moves the produce and involves no sorting.

topic_name: Street vendor credit and livelihood schemes
short_explanation: PM SVANidhi, launched in June 2020, gives urban street vendors collateral-free working capital starting at 10,000 rupees, with a larger tranche unlocked on timely repayment.
explanation_text: The scheme is built as a ladder: 10,000 rupees first, then 20,000, then 50,000, each opening only on repayment of the last. A 7 per cent interest subsidy is credited to the account quarterly, and cashback rewards push vendors towards digital transactions, which in turn builds the credit history the scheme is really trying to create. It is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, with urban local bodies issuing the vending certificates that establish eligibility.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana subsidised employer and employee EPFO contributions for new formal-sector hires.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: There is no current scheme of this name; the old Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana for self-employment was subsumed into PMEGP years ago.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Stand-Up India finances greenfield enterprises by SC, ST and women borrowers, at a far larger loan size.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: There is no Sashakt Bharat Mission.

topic_name: DAY-NRLM, self-help groups and rural livelihoods
short_explanation: The list thrown up by Participatory Identification of the Poor is placed before the Gram Sabha, which verifies and approves it. That open-meeting check is what gives the list its standing under DAY-NRLM.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: The State Level Bankers' Committee coordinates bank credit planning; it has no role in identifying poor households.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: The lead bank handles district credit planning, not beneficiary identification.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The District Consultative Committee is a bank and administration coordination forum.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body and takes the approved list forward, but the verification itself is done by the Gram Sabha.

common_traps: Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat are not interchangeable. The Sabha is the whole adult electorate of the village meeting together, and it is the Sabha that verifies.

short_explanation: In 'the steep discounts that public sector companies trade at', steep means unusually large, so 'excessive' is the matching synonym.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Deprived means denied something needed; it says nothing about the size of a discount.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Moderate is the opposite — a steep discount is anything but moderate.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Void means empty or legally invalid, not large.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

common_traps: 'Steep' also means sharply sloping. The passage uses it of size, and the synonym must match that sense.

short_explanation: The overdraft under PMJDY goes up to 10,000 rupees, not 20,000, so that is the wrongly stated benefit; interest on deposits, the 2 lakh rupee accident cover on RuPay cards issued after 28 August 2018, the basic savings account and the zero minimum balance rule are all correctly stated.
explanation_text: Two ceilings in this scheme get confused. The accident cover attached to the RuPay card is 1 lakh rupees for cards issued up to 28 August 2018 and 2 lakh rupees after that date. The overdraft was raised from 5,000 to 10,000 rupees, with up to 2,000 available without conditions, and the eligible age band for it is 18 to 65 years. Nothing in the scheme reaches 20,000 rupees.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Correctly stated. A PMJDY account is a savings account and earns interest on the balance.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Correctly stated. The cover is 2 lakh rupees for RuPay cards issued after 28 August 2018.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Correctly stated. PMJDY opens one basic savings bank deposit account for an unbanked person.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Correctly stated. No minimum balance is required in a PMJDY account.

common_traps: The stem asks for the benefit stated incorrectly, so four of the five options here are true statements. Reading it as the usual 'which is correct' question inverts the whole item.

topic_name: Food security and the public distribution system
short_explanation: Free food grain is distributed under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, launched in April 2020 and since merged with the NFSA entitlement, so that NFSA beneficiaries receive their monthly grain at no cost.
explanation_text: The National Food Security Act, 2013 entitles priority households to 5 kg of grain per person per month and Antyodaya households to 35 kg per family, at subsidised issue prices through the public distribution system. PMGKAY began as an additional free allocation on top of that during the pandemic. From January 2023 the design changed: instead of an extra quantity, the NFSA entitlement itself was made free, with the centre bearing the subsidy, and the free scheme has since been extended for a further five years. The other options are different instruments altogether - income support, organic farming and credit.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Krishak Unnati Yojana is a state input assistance scheme for farmers, not a food grain distribution scheme.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana promotes organic farming through cluster-based support.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi transfers Rs 6,000 a year in cash to landholding farmer families.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: The Kisan Credit Card is a short-term crop credit instrument, not a food security scheme.

topic_name: Food security, PDS and free foodgrain schemes
short_explanation: From 1 January 2023 the government stopped charging the subsidised NFSA issue price and supplied the entire NFSA entitlement free for one year, folding the pandemic-era PMGKAY into the Act's own entitlement.
explanation_text: Under the NFSA the entitlement itself does not change: an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household gets 35 kg of foodgrain a month, and a priority household gets 5 kg per person per month, covering about 81 crore people. What changed on 1 January 2023 was only the price. Beneficiaries had been paying 3, 2 and 1 rupee a kilogram for rice, wheat and coarse grain; that charge was set to zero, with the Centre absorbing the cost as food subsidy. The free supply has since been extended beyond the first year.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Two years overstates the initial decision, which covered calendar 2023; later extensions were separate decisions.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Three years was not the period announced from 1 January 2023.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Four years is arbitrary.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Five years matches a later extension announced at the end of 2023, not the decision effective from 1 January 2023.

short_explanation: In drought-notified or calamity-affected rural areas the centre allows an additional 50 days of unskilled wage employment beyond the 100 days guaranteed to a household under MGNREGA.
explanation_text: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of unskilled manual work in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for it, with wages due within fifteen days and an unemployment allowance if work is not provided. Two extensions sit on top of that guarantee: an additional 100 days for scheduled tribe households in forest areas holding rights under the Forest Rights Act, and an additional 50 days where the state has notified drought or a natural calamity. The extra days are approved by the centre on the state's request, which is why the relief arrives as a specific notification rather than automatically.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 20 days is not the notified extension for calamity-affected areas.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 30 days does not correspond to any MGNREGA provision.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 40 days is not the figure allowed under the drought provision.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 60 days is not the approved extension; the additional entitlement is 50 days.

topic_name: Clean cooking fuel and energy access schemes
short_explanation: In September 2023 the Cabinet approved 75 lakh additional Ujjwala connections over three years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, taking the scheme's total towards about 10.35 crore connections.
explanation_text: PMUY gives a deposit-free LPG connection in the name of an adult woman of a poor household, with the connection cost met by the government and the first refill and stove supported. The scheme's live problem is not connections but refills: a household that cannot afford a cylinder at market price slides back to firewood, which is why the targeted subsidy per refill for Ujjwala beneficiaries matters more than the headline connection count.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 50 lakh over one year understates both the number approved and the period.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 60 lakh over two years understates both.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 1 crore over four years overstates the approval.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 1.5 crore over five years is far above what was approved in September 2023.

short_explanation: Under DAY-NRLM, women's self-help groups get interest subvention covering the gap between the bank's lending rate and 7 per cent on credit of up to Rs 3,00,000 per SHG.
explanation_text: DAY-NRLM works by organising rural poor women into self-help groups, building their savings and credit discipline, and then linking them to banks. To keep that bank credit affordable the mission meets the difference between the bank's lending rate and 7 per cent on loans up to Rs 3 lakh per group. In the identified districts, groups that repay promptly get a further subvention that brings the effective rate down to 4 per cent. The subvention is paid to the bank or routed through the state rural livelihoods mission; it is not handed to the group as cash.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 4,00,000 is not the subvention ceiling set under the mission.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 5,00,000 is not the limit for the 7 per cent subvention on SHG credit.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 6,00,000 is not a DAY-NRLM subvention ceiling.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Rs 7,00,000 is not the figure; the 7 in the stem is the interest rate, not the ceiling in lakhs.

topic_name: Credit schemes for SC, ST and women entrepreneurs
short_explanation: Stand-Up India requires every scheduled commercial bank branch to lend between 10 lakh rupees and 1 crore rupees to at least one SC or ST borrower and at least one woman borrower for a greenfield enterprise.
explanation_text: 'Greenfield' is the operative word: the loan must fund a first-time venture by that borrower, in manufacturing, services, trading or an agriculture-allied activity. The composite loan covers term loan and working capital together. Margin money may be up to 15 per cent, with the borrower contributing at least 10 per cent from own funds, and convergence with State schemes is allowed for the rest. SIDBI runs a refinance window and the loans can be backed by a credit guarantee.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 50 lakh rupees stops well short of the scheme's upper limit.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 70 lakh rupees is arbitrary; no guideline sets it.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 80 lakh rupees is arbitrary.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2 crore rupees is double the scheme's ceiling.

short_explanation: Jal Jeevan Mission (Rural), launched in 2019, set out to supply 55 litres per person per day of drinking water of prescribed quality to every rural household through a functional household tap connection.
explanation_text: The 55 litres per capita per day service level is the mission's yardstick, and the word functional is defined tightly: the connection must deliver the prescribed quantity, of water meeting the BIS 10500 standard, on a regular and long-term basis - a tap that runs dry does not count. States implement the mission with central cost sharing, and village water and sanitation committees, or paani samitis, are meant to plan, operate and maintain the in-village system so that the asset survives after construction.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 50 lpcd was the norm used under earlier rural water supply programmes, not the Jal Jeevan Mission service level.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 60 lpcd is above the mission's norm.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 65 lpcd is not the figure set for rural household supply.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 70 lpcd is not the mission norm; higher per capita figures belong to urban supply standards.

common_traps: Earlier rural water supply programmes used lower per capita norms; the Jal Jeevan Mission figure is 55 lpcd.

short_explanation: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II runs from 2020-21 to 2024-25, its aim being to sustain open defecation free status and add solid and liquid waste management so that villages become ODF Plus.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2023-24 is not the closing year of Phase II.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2022-23 falls inside the phase rather than at its end.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2020-21 is the starting year, which the question itself gives.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 2025-26 runs past the notified period of Phase II.

topic_name: Credit schemes for SC, ST and women entrepreneurs
short_explanation: The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation lends to applicants from Other Backward Classes whose annual family income is up to 3 lakh rupees, a single ceiling since the earlier rural and urban split was dropped.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 1.5 lakh rupees was closer to the older rural ceiling and is no longer the limit.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 2 lakh rupees is below the current unified ceiling.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 2.5 lakh rupees matches no NBCFDC guideline.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 3.5 lakh rupees is above the ceiling.

short_explanation: Carbon dioxide is the greenhouse gas common to all three sources named - volcanic eruptions, animal respiration and the burning of fossil fuels.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas; it does not absorb outgoing infrared radiation.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Methane is a greenhouse gas, but its main sources are flooded paddy, ruminant digestion, landfills and gas leakage rather than volcanoes and respiration.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Chlorofluorocarbons are entirely man-made refrigerants and propellants, released by neither volcanoes nor respiration.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Nitrogen makes up most of the atmosphere but is not a greenhouse gas.

topic_name: Pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers
short_explanation: The All Citizen Model is open to Indian citizens, resident or non-resident, and to Overseas Citizens of India. A Hindu Undivided Family is not a natural person and cannot hold an NPS account.
explanation_text: Entry age runs from 18 to 70 years. An NRI may open an account but it closes if Indian citizenship is given up. Statement 3 fails for a technical reason worth knowing: the Person of Indian Origin card scheme was merged into the OCI scheme in 2015, so PIO no longer exists as a separate category, and people who held PIO cards are covered as OCIs. An HUF is a tax entity, not an individual, so it is outside a personal pension account.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Carries Persons of Indian Origin, a category merged into OCI in 2015, and drops Indian citizens, the core eligible group.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Carries Persons of Indian Origin and drops Overseas Citizens of India.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Adds Persons of Indian Origin to the two correct categories.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

key_note: Statement 3 fails because the PIO category itself was merged into OCI in 2015, not because people of Indian origin are shut out of NPS.

short_explanation: eNAM, the electronic National Agriculture Market launched in 2016, is the pan-India portal that links existing APMC mandis into a single online trading platform for agricultural commodities.
explanation_text: eNAM does not replace the mandi; it puts the mandi's trade online. A farmer's lot arriving at an integrated APMC is assayed for quality, the assay report is displayed, and traders - including those licensed in other mandis and other states - bid against it online, with the sale confirmed and payment made against the electronic record. The Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium runs the platform for the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. The whole point of the design is to widen the pool of bidders beyond the traders physically standing in that yard on that day.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: eAgri Portal is not the national electronic trading platform.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: The Farmers' Portal is an information gateway for scheme, advisory and input details; no trading happens on it.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Only eNAM is a trading portal, so all of the above fails.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Filler option; a correct answer is present.

short_explanation: SHREYAS bundles four schemes for SC students from 2021-22: Top Class Education, Free Coaching for SCs and OBCs, the National Overseas Scholarship and the National Fellowship. The Post Matric Scholarship stays a separate and much larger scheme of its own.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Names only two of the four merged schemes.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Drops Free Coaching for SCs and OBCs, which is one of the four.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Pulls in the Post Matric Scholarship, which was not merged, and drops the overseas and fellowship schemes.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Pulls in the Post Matric Scholarship and drops the National Overseas Scholarship.

common_traps: Post Matric Scholarship for SCs is the best known of these names and is precisely the one left out of SHREYAS.

short_explanation: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covers up to 5 lakh rupees per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation, with no cap on family size or age and cover portable across empanelled hospitals anywhere in the country.
explanation_text: Beneficiary households are drawn from the deprivation and occupational criteria of SECC 2011, not from an income test, so there is no enrolment drive to qualify: the family is either on the list or not. The cover is cashless and paperless at empanelled public and private hospitals and includes three days of pre-hospitalisation and 15 days of post-hospitalisation expenses. PM-JAY is only the insurance arm of Ayushman Bharat; the other arm is the network of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, the renamed Health and Wellness Centres, which handle primary care.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 2 lakh rupees is below the cover; it is closer to the PMJDY accident cover figure and is often confused with it.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 3 lakh rupees is arbitrary.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: 4 lakh rupees is arbitrary.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 10 lakh rupees is double the cover; some State top-up schemes go higher, but PM-JAY itself does not.

topic_name: Kisan Credit Card and agricultural credit targets
short_explanation: The agriculture credit target was raised to Rs 20 lakh crore in the Union Budget 2023-24, with the announcement naming animal husbandry, dairy and fisheries as the focus areas.
explanation_text: The agriculture credit target is the volume of ground level credit banks are expected to disburse to agriculture and allied activities in a financial year. NABARD prepares the potential linked credit plans, district by district, on which that target rests, and the Kisan Credit Card is the main instrument through which short-term crop credit reaches the farmer. The KCC was extended to animal husbandry and fisheries in 2018-19, which is why the Budget's focus on those sub-sectors is tied to this figure. The target has risen in steps - Rs 16.5 lakh crore for 2021-22, Rs 18 lakh crore for 2022-23 and Rs 20 lakh crore for 2023-24.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: 10 lakh crore had been passed well before 2023-24.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: 15 lakh crore understates the announced target; 16.5 lakh crore was the 2021-22 figure.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: 25 lakh crore was not the figure announced for this year.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: 30 lakh crore is far above the Budget target.

common_traps: The stem says crore while the options are read as lakh crore; the target is Rs 20 lakh crore.

short_explanation: A tied ridge is a ridge-and-furrow layout in which small cross ties of earth are built across the furrow at intervals, breaking it into a row of small basins that hold runoff where it falls.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Compartmental bunding divides the whole field surface into small squares with low bunds, rather than tying ridges inside a furrow.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Contour bunding runs bunds along the contour across the slope to intercept runoff.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Strip cropping alternates strips of erosion-permitting and erosion-resisting crops across the slope.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Graded bunds are laid on a slight grade to carry excess water safely away, and are used in higher rainfall areas.

common_traps: Tied ridging works inside the ridge and furrow; compartmental bunding partitions the field surface itself.

topic_name: Pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers
short_explanation: Jeevan Pramaan is the Aadhaar-based digital life certificate: a pensioner authenticates by fingerprint or iris scan and the certificate reaches the disbursing agency electronically, removing the annual trip to the bank or treasury.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: An invented name.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: An invented name; 'Jeevan Sathi' belongs to insurance product branding, not to pension certification.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: An invented name.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: An invented name; 'sakshar' relates to literacy.

tag_note: The tagged topic is pension schemes for unorganised workers and farmers, but Jeevan Pramaan is a digital life certificate service for government and agency pensioners. It fits better under pension administration and digital governance, or e-governance service delivery.

short_explanation: Drip irrigation does demand technical skill - the system has to be designed for the field, emitters matched to soil and crop, and filters and laterals maintained against clogging.
explanation_text: Drip delivers water drop by drop through emitters straight into the root zone, so it uses less water than surface methods, cuts deep percolation and evaporation, and allows fertilizer to be injected with the water in fertigation. It suits wide-spaced crops, undulating land and poor quality or saline water, because the root zone stays continuously moist and salts are pushed out to the wetting front. What it asks in return is capital and skill - filtration, pressure regulation, a layout matched to the field, and regular flushing and acid treatment to keep emitters open.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: Drip uses less water than conventional surface irrigation, not more, because percolation and evaporation losses are cut.

option_rationales.label: B
option_rationales.rationale: Drip does the opposite - water, and fertilizer through fertigation, go directly to the root zone.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Drip is in fact suited to salt affected areas, since continuous moisture keeps salts pushed out to the edge of the wetted zone.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Drip reduces deep percolation, because water is applied near the roots and at a low rate.

common_traps: Four of the five statements are claims against drip; the true statement is what drip demands of the user, not a benefit it offers.

short_explanation: Earning more than 15,000 rupees a month is an automatic exclusion from PMAY-G, not an inclusion. The automatic inclusions are households without shelter, destitutes living on alms, manual scavengers, primitive tribal groups and legally released bonded labourers.
explanation_text: PMAY-G draws its beneficiary list from the housing deprivation parameters of SECC 2011, runs it through 13 exclusion filters such as a motorised vehicle, a Kisan Credit Card above a set limit, a government job in the household or that 15,000 rupee monthly earning, and then puts the remaining list to the Gram Sabha for verification. Unit assistance is 1.20 lakh rupees in the plains and 1.30 lakh in hill, difficult and left-wing-extremism affected areas, alongside 90 to 95 days of MGNREGA unskilled wage and a toilet funded under SBM-Gramin.

option_rationales.label: A
option_rationales.rationale: A household without shelter is one of the five automatic inclusions.

option_rationales.label: C
option_rationales.rationale: Manual scavengers are an automatic inclusion.

option_rationales.label: D
option_rationales.rationale: Primitive tribal groups are an automatic inclusion.

option_rationales.label: E
option_rationales.rationale: Destitutes living on alms are an automatic inclusion.

common_traps: The stem asks which is NOT an automatic inclusion. The 15,000 rupee figure is real, but it belongs to the exclusion list, which is what makes it the answer.
